lessons.title: Exercise 1 — Part 1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Expanded form writes a number as the sum of the place values of its digits.
  • Standard form is the ordinary number obtained by adding all the place value parts.
  • The place value of a digit is the digit multiplied by the value of its place.

Exercise 1 (Questions 1–23)

  • Q: a) Write the following number in expanded form: 675,432
    Ans: Rule: Expanded form writes a number as the sum of the place values of its digits.
    6 is in the hundred thousands place, so its value is 6 x 100,000 = 600,000.
    7 is in the ten thousands place, so its value is 7 x 10,000 = 70,000.
    5 is in the thousands place, so its value is 5 x 1,000 = 5,000.
    4 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 4 x 100 = 400.
    3 is in the tens place, so its value is 3 x 10 = 30.
    2 is in the ones place, so its value is 2 x 1 = 2.
    Answer: 675,432 = 600,000 + 70,000 + 5,000 + 400 + 30 + 2
  • Q: b) Write the following number in expanded form: 437,911
    Ans: Rule: Expanded form writes a number as the sum of the place values of its digits.
    4 is in the hundred thousands place, so its value is 4 x 100,000 = 400,000.
    3 is in the ten thousands place, so its value is 3 x 10,000 = 30,000.
    7 is in the thousands place, so its value is 7 x 1,000 = 7,000.
    9 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 9 x 100 = 900.
    1 is in the tens place, so its value is 1 x 10 = 10.
    1 is in the ones place, so its value is 1 x 1 = 1.
    Answer: 437,911 = 400,000 + 30,000 + 7,000 + 900 + 10 + 1
  • Q: c) Write the following number in expanded form: 210,956
    Ans: Rule: Expanded form writes a number as the sum of the place values of its digits.
    2 is in the hundred thousands place, so its value is 2 x 100,000 = 200,000.
    1 is in the ten thousands place, so its value is 1 x 10,000 = 10,000.
    0 is in the thousands place, so its value is 0 x 1,000 = 0.
    9 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 9 x 100 = 900.
    5 is in the tens place, so its value is 5 x 10 = 50.
    6 is in the ones place, so its value is 6 x 1 = 6.
    Answer: 210,956 = 200,000 + 10,000 + 0 + 900 + 50 + 6
  • Q: d) Write the following number in expanded form: 546,743
    Ans: Rule: Expanded form writes a number as the sum of the place values of its digits.
    5 is in the hundred thousands place, so its value is 5 x 100,000 = 500,000.
    4 is in the ten thousands place, so its value is 4 x 10,000 = 40,000.
    6 is in the thousands place, so its value is 6 x 1,000 = 6,000.
    7 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 7 x 100 = 700.
    4 is in the tens place, so its value is 4 x 10 = 40.
    3 is in the ones place, so its value is 3 x 1 = 3.
    Answer: 546,743 = 500,000 + 40,000 + 6,000 + 700 + 40 + 3
  • Q: e) Write the following number in expanded form: 786,594

  • Q: f) Write the following number in expanded form: 509,223
    Ans: Rule: Expanded form writes a number as the sum of the place values of its digits.
    5 is in the hundred thousands place, so its value is 5 x 100,000 = 500,000.

    9 is in the thousands place, so its value is 9 x 1,000 = 9,000.
    2 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 2 x 100 = 200.
    2 is in the tens place, so its value is 2 x 10 = 20.

    2 is in the thousands place, so its value is 2 x 1,000 = 2,000.
    1 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 1 x 100 = 100.
    6 is in the tens place, so its value is 6 x 10 = 60.

    Answer: 322,167 = 300,000 + 20,000 + 2,000 + 100 + 60 + 7
  • Q: h) Write the following number in expanded form: 657,890

  • Q: l) Write the following number in expanded form: 756,432
    Ans: Rule: Expanded form writes a number as the sum of the place values of its digits.

  • Q: a) Write the following number in standard form: 600,000+20,000+1,000+100+70+1 = _____
    Ans: Rule: Standard form is the ordinary number obtained by adding all the place value parts.
    Add the part 600,000: running total = 600,000.
    Add the part 20,000: running total = 620,000.
    Add the part 1,000: running total = 621,000.
    Add the part 100: running total = 621,100.
    Add the part 70: running total = 621,170.
    Add the part 1: running total = 621,171.
    Answer: 600,000+20,000+1,000+100+70+1 = 621,171
  • Q: b) Write the following number in standard form: 200,000+30,000+9,000+200+30+5 = _____
    Ans: Rule: Standard form is the ordinary number obtained by adding all the place value parts.
    Add the part 200,000: running total = 200,000.
    Add the part 30,000: running total = 230,000.
    Add the part 9,000: running total = 239,000.
    Add the part 200: running total = 239,200.
    Add the part 30: running total = 239,230.
    Add the part 5: running total = 239,235.
    Answer: 200,000+30,000+9,000+200+30+5 = 239,235
  • Q: c) Write the following number in standard form: 500,000+60,000+5,000+300+40+3 = _____
    Ans: Rule: Standard form is the ordinary number obtained by adding all the place value parts.
    Add the part 500,000: running total = 500,000.
    Add the part 60,000: running total = 560,000.
    Add the part 5,000: running total = 565,000.
    Add the part 300: running total = 565,300.
    Add the part 40: running total = 565,340.
    Add the part 3: running total = 565,343.
    Answer: 500,000+60,000+5,000+300+40+3 = 565,343
  • Q: d) Write the following number in standard form: 700,000+50,000+6,000+700+90+0 = _____
    Ans: Rule: Standard form is the ordinary number obtained by adding all the place value parts.
    Add the part 700,000: running total = 700,000.
    Add the part 50,000: running total = 750,000.
    Add the part 6,000: running total = 756,000.
    Add the part 700: running total = 756,700.
    Add the part 90: running total = 756,790.
    Add the part 0: running total = 756,790.
    Answer: 700,000+50,000+6,000+700+90+0 = 756,790
  • Q: a) Write the place and place value of the coloured digit 0 in 576,102.
    Ans: Rule: The place value of a digit is the digit multiplied by the value of its place.

lessons.title: Exercise 1 — Part 2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The place value of a digit is the digit multiplied by the value of its place.
  • Read the number in two parts: the thousands part first, then the remaining hundreds, tens and ones part.
  • Change the words into digits part by part: first the thousands part, then the hundreds, tens and ones part.

Exercise 1 (Questions 24–46)

  • Q: h) Write the place and place value of the coloured digit 0 in 200,042.
    Ans: Rule: The place value of a digit is the digit multiplied by the value of its place.
    Place value chart for 200,042: 2 in hundred thousands, 0 in ten thousands, 0 in thousands, 0 in hundreds, 4 in tens, 2 in ones.
    The coloured digit 0 is in the thousands place.
    Place value = 0 x 1,000 = 0.
    Answer: Place: thousands; Place value: 0
  • Q: i) Write the place and place value of the coloured digit 4 in 956,324.
    Ans: Rule: The place value of a digit is the digit multiplied by the value of its place.
    Place value chart for 956,324: 9 in hundred thousands, 5 in ten thousands, 6 in thousands, 3 in hundreds, 2 in tens, 4 in ones.
    The coloured digit 4 is in the ones place.
    Place value = 4 x 1 = 4.
    Answer: Place: ones; Place value: 4
  • Q: a) Write the following number in words: 674,325
    Ans: Rule: Read the number in two parts: the thousands part first, then the remaining hundreds, tens and ones part.
    Thousands part: 674 is written as 'six hundred and seventy-four', so we say 'six hundred and seventy-four thousand'.
    Remaining part: 325 is written as 'three hundred and twenty-five'.
    Answer: 674,325 in words is 'Six hundred and seventy-four thousand, three hundred and twenty-five'
  • Q: b) Write the following number in words: 943,711

    Remaining part: 711 is written as 'seven hundred and eleven'.
    Answer: 943,711 in words is 'Nine hundred and forty-three thousand, seven hundred and eleven'
  • Q: c) Write the following number in words: 219,560

lessons.title: Exercise 2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • To compare numbers, compare the digits from the left, starting from the greatest place, until you find two different digits. A number with more digits is the greater number.
  • For descending order, compare the digits from the left, starting from the greatest place. Write the greatest number first and the smallest last.
  • For ascending order, compare the digits from the left, starting from the greatest place. Write the smallest number first and the greatest last.

mcqs.q: Encircle the correct answer: The comparison of numbers always start from the __________.
mcqs.why: To compare numbers, compare the digits from the left, starting from the greatest place, and move right until two different digits are found. So the comparison of numbers always starts from the left.

lessons.title: Review Exercise — Part 3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The place value of a digit is the digit multiplied by the value of its place.
  • Standard form is the ordinary number obtained by adding all the place value parts.
  • To compare numbers, compare the digits from the left, starting from the greatest place, until you find two different digits. A number with more digits is the greater number.
  • For descending order, compare the digits from the left, starting from the greatest place. Write the greatest number first and the smallest last.
  • For ascending order, compare the digits from the left, starting from the greatest place. Write the smallest number first and the greatest last.

Review Exercise (Questions 45–65)

  • Q: a) Write the following in standard form: 300,000 + 40,000 + 4,000 + 600 + 80 + 3 = _____

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • One hundred thousand is 100,000. Count how many groups of 10,000 make 100,000.
  • Put a comma after every three digits from the right. The place value of a digit is the digit multiplied by the value of its place.
  • Read the thousands part first, then the remaining part. Expanded form writes a number as the sum of the place values of its digits.
  • The smallest 6-digit number begins with 1 followed by zeros. The greatest 6-digit number has 9 in every place.
  • For the greatest number, write the digits in descending order, greatest digit first. A 6-digit number uses six of the given digits, so use the six greatest digits: 9, 7, 6, 5, 3, 2.
  • For the smallest number, write the digits in ascending order, smallest digit first. A 6-digit number uses six of the given digits, so use the six smallest digits: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7.
  • The thousands place is the fourth digit from the right. Keep 3 fixed in the thousands place and arrange other digits around it. Many answers are possible; one set of answers is given.
  • Find two digits whose sum is 8 and whose difference is 2, then put them in the hundred thousands place and the tens place. Many answers are possible; one answer is given.

Try Yourself (book p. 2)

  • Q: How many ten thousands are there in one hundred thousand?
    Ans: Rule: One hundred thousand is 100,000. Count how many groups of 10,000 make 100,000.
    10,000 x 1 = 10,000
    10,000 x 2 = 20,000
    10,000 x 5 = 50,000
    10,000 x 10 = 100,000
    So 10 groups of ten thousand make one hundred thousand.
    Answer: 10 ten thousands

Try Yourself (book p. 3)

  • Q: Put commas in the correct place in 402918. Find the place value of each digit. Then write this number in words.
    Ans: Rule: Put a comma after every three digits from the right. The place value of a digit is the digit multiplied by the value of its place.
    Step 1: Put commas: 402918 becomes 402,918.
    Step 2: 4 is in the hundred thousands place, so its value is 4 x 100,000 = 400,000.
    Step 3: 0 is in the ten thousands place, so its value is 0 x 10,000 = 0.
    Step 4: 2 is in the thousands place, so its value is 2 x 1,000 = 2,000.
    Step 5: 9 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 9 x 100 = 900.
    Step 6: 1 is in the tens place, so its value is 1 x 10 = 10.
    Step 7: 8 is in the ones place, so its value is 8 x 1 = 8.
    Step 8: Thousands part 402 is 'four hundred and two', and the remaining part 918 is 'nine hundred and eighteen'.
    Answer: 402,918; place values: 4 = 400,000, 0 = 0, 2 = 2,000, 9 = 900, 1 = 10, 8 = 8; in words: Four hundred and two thousand, nine hundred and eighteen

Try Yourself (book p. 4)

  • Q: Murree is a tourist place. It is 7,500 feet or 228,600 cm approximately above sea level. Write 228,600 in words and then write in expanded form.
    Ans: Rule: Read the thousands part first, then the remaining part. Expanded form writes a number as the sum of the place values of its digits.
    Thousands part: 228 is 'two hundred and twenty-eight', so we say 'two hundred and twenty-eight thousand'.
    Remaining part: 600 is 'six hundred'.
    In words: Two hundred and twenty-eight thousand, six hundred.
    2 is in the hundred thousands place, so its value is 2 x 100,000 = 200,000.
    2 is in the ten thousands place, so its value is 2 x 10,000 = 20,000.
    8 is in the thousands place, so its value is 8 x 1,000 = 8,000.
    6 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 6 x 100 = 600.
    0 is in the tens place, so its value is 0 x 10 = 0.
    0 is in the ones place, so its value is 0 x 1 = 0.
    Answer: In words: Two hundred and twenty-eight thousand, six hundred; Expanded form: 228,600 = 200,000 + 20,000 + 8,000 + 600 + 0 + 0
  • Q: Can you tell what is the smallest and greatest 6-digit number?
    Ans: Rule: The smallest 6-digit number begins with 1 followed by zeros. The greatest 6-digit number has 9 in every place.
    The smallest 6-digit number is 100,000 (one hundred thousand).
    The greatest 6-digit number is 999,999 (nine hundred and ninety-nine thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine).
    Answer: Smallest 6-digit number: 100,000; Greatest 6-digit number: 999,999

Try It! (book p. 4)

  • Q: By using the given digits 7, 2, 9, 3, 1, 6, 5: make a greatest 6-digit number and write it in words.
    Ans: Rule: For the greatest number, write the digits in descending order, greatest digit first. A 6-digit number uses six of the given digits, so use the six greatest digits: 9, 7, 6, 5, 3, 2.
    Arrange in descending order: 9, 7, 6, 5, 3, 2.
    The number is 976,532.
    Thousands part: 976 is 'nine hundred and seventy-six'. Remaining part: 532 is 'five hundred and thirty-two'.
    Answer: 976,532; in words: Nine hundred and seventy-six thousand, five hundred and thirty-two
  • Q: By using the given digits 7, 2, 9, 3, 1, 6, 5: make the smallest 6-digit number and write the place value of each digit of it.
    Ans: Rule: For the smallest number, write the digits in ascending order, smallest digit first. A 6-digit number uses six of the given digits, so use the six smallest digits: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7.
    Arrange in ascending order: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7.
    The number is 123,567.
    1 is in the hundred thousands place, so its value is 1 x 100,000 = 100,000.
    2 is in the ten thousands place, so its value is 2 x 10,000 = 20,000.
    3 is in the thousands place, so its value is 3 x 1,000 = 3,000.
    5 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 5 x 100 = 500.
    6 is in the tens place, so its value is 6 x 10 = 60.
    7 is in the ones place, so its value is 7 x 1 = 7.
    Answer: 123,567; place values: 1 = 100,000, 2 = 20,000, 3 = 3,000, 5 = 500, 6 = 60, 7 = 7
  • Q: By using the given digits 7, 2, 9, 3, 1, 6, 5: write 3 different numbers whose thousand digit is 3.
    Ans: Rule: The thousands place is the fourth digit from the right. Keep 3 fixed in the thousands place and arrange other digits around it. Many answers are possible; one set of answers is given.
    Number 1: 123,456. Check: digits are 1 (hundred thousands), 2 (ten thousands), 3 (thousands), 4 (hundreds), 5 (tens), 6 (ones). The thousands digit is 3.
    Number 2: 453,210. Check: digits are 4, 5, 3, 2, 1, 0. The thousands digit is 3.
    Number 3: 783,915. Check: digits are 7, 8, 3, 9, 1, 5. The thousands digit is 3.
    Answer: 123,456; 453,210; 783,915 (any three 6-digit numbers with 3 in the thousands place are correct)
  • Q: By using the given digits 7, 2, 9, 3, 1, 6, 5: make a 6-digit whole number where sum of digits of hundred thousand place and tens place is 8 and difference is 2.
    Ans: Rule: Find two digits whose sum is 8 and whose difference is 2, then put them in the hundred thousands place and the tens place. Many answers are possible; one answer is given.
    The two digits are 5 and 3, because 5 + 3 = 8 and 5 - 3 = 2.
    Put 5 in the hundred thousands place and 3 in the tens place.
    Fill the remaining places with other digits, for example 1, 2, 4, 6: the number is 512,436.
    Check: hundred thousands digit is 5, tens digit is 3; 5 + 3 = 8 and 5 - 3 = 2.
    Answer: 512,436 (any 6-digit number with hundred thousands digit 5 and tens digit 3, or hundred thousands digit 3 and tens digit 5, is correct)
  • Q: By using the given digits 7, 2, 9, 3, 1, 6, 5: write a whole number in which no digit is repeated again.
    Ans: Rule: Use each digit only once. Many answers are possible; one answer is given.
    Arrange the digits in ascending order: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9.
    The number is 1,235,679.
    Check: the digits 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9 are all different; no digit is repeated.
    Answer: 1,235,679 (any number using each given digit at most once is correct)

Try Yourself (book p. 6)

  • Q: Compare 62,323 and 62,199. Which one is greatest?
    Ans: Rule: To compare numbers, compare the digits from the left, starting from the greatest place, until you find two different digits. A number with more digits is the greater number.
    Comparing from the left, the first different digits are at the hundreds place: 3 and 1.
    3 is greater than 1, so 62,323 is greater than 62,199.
    Answer: 62,323 > 62,199, so 62,323 is the greatest

Try Yourself (book p. 7)

  • Q: Compare the greatest and smallest 5-digit number.
    Ans: Rule: The greatest 5-digit number has 9 in every place. The smallest 5-digit number begins with 1 followed by zeros.
    The greatest 5-digit number is 99,999.
    The smallest 5-digit number is 10,000.
    Compare from the left: at the ten thousands place, 9 is greater than 1.
    Answer: 99,999 > 10,000, so the greatest 5-digit number is greater than the smallest 5-digit number
  • Q: Compare 8,799; 22,234 and 22,229. Which one is smallest?
    Ans: Rule: A number with fewer digits is smaller. For numbers with the same number of digits, compare the digits from the left.
    8,799 has 4 digits, while 22,234 and 22,229 have 5 digits each.
    A 4-digit number is always smaller than a 5-digit number.
    So 8,799 is smaller than both 22,234 and 22,229.
    Answer: 8,799 is the smallest

Try It! (book p. 8)

  • Q: Make two 4-digit and three 5-digit numbers. In every number the digit at the thousands place is 6 and digit at units place is 9. Then compare these numbers and write in descending order.
    Ans: Rule: Keep 6 fixed in the thousands place and 9 fixed in the units (ones) place, and choose the other digits freely. Many answers are possible; one set of answers is given.
    Two 4-digit numbers: 6,129 (thousands digit 6, units digit 9) and 6,859 (thousands digit 6, units digit 9).
    Three 5-digit numbers: 16,349 (thousands digit 6, units digit 9), 26,579 (thousands digit 6, units digit 9) and 36,289 (thousands digit 6, units digit 9).
    Compare: every 5-digit number is greater than every 4-digit number.
    Among the 5-digit numbers, at the ten thousands place 3 is greater than 2, and 2 is greater than 1, so 36,289 is greatest, then 26,579, then 16,349.
    Among the 4-digit numbers, at the hundreds place 8 is greater than 1, so 6,859 is greater than 6,129.
    Answer: Descending order: 36,289; 26,579; 16,349; 6,859; 6,129 (any five numbers meeting the conditions, written greatest to smallest, are correct)

lessons.title: Exercise 1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Add column by column, starting from the ones place and moving to the left. If a column total is 10 or more, write the ones digit of the total and carry 1 to the next column.
  • To compare numbers, compare the digits from the left, starting from the greatest place, until you find two different digits. A number with more digits is the greater number.

Exercise 1

  • Q: a) Solve the following (column addition): 13,927 + 2,415
    Ans: Rule: Add column by column, starting from the ones place and moving to the left. If a column total is 10 or more, write the ones digit of the total and carry 1 to the next column.
    Ones: 7 + 5 = 12; write 2, carry 1.
    Tens: 2 + 1 + carry 1 = 4; write 4.
    Hundreds: 9 + 4 = 13; write 3, carry 1.
    Thousands: 3 + 2 + carry 1 = 6; write 6.
    Ten thousands: 1 + 0 = 1; write 1.
    Answer: 13,927 + 2,415 = 16,342
  • Q: b) Solve the following (column addition): 35,321 + 4,649

    Tens: 2 + 4 + carry 1 = 7; write 7.
    Hundreds: 3 + 6 = 9; write 9.
    Thousands: 5 + 4 = 9; write 9.
    Ten thousands: 3 + 0 = 3; write 3.
    Answer: 35,321 + 4,649 = 39,970
  • Q: c) Solve the following (column addition): 75,679 + 16,828

    Hundreds: 6 + 8 + carry 1 = 15; write 5, carry 1.

  • Q: a) Solve the following: 58,134 + 45,367

  • Q: b) Solve the following: 78,954 + 12,236

Key Points

  • Subtract column by column, starting from the ones place and moving to the left. If the top digit is smaller than the bottom digit, borrow 1 from the next place on the left (that place gives 10 to this place and becomes 1 less).

lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Add column by column, starting from the ones place and moving to the left. If a column total is 10 or more, write the ones digit of the total and carry 1 to the next column.
  • The greatest 5-digit number has 9 in every place. The smallest 4-digit number begins with 1 followed by zeros. To find the sum, add the two numbers column by column.
  • Work column by column from the ones place, using the sum to find each missing digit and any carry.
  • The smallest 5-digit number begins with 1 followed by zeros. The greatest 4-digit number has 9 in every place. Subtract column by column from the ones place, borrowing from the next place whenever the top digit is smaller.
  • Try pairs from the given numbers and check both the sum and the difference.

Try Yourself (book p. 15)

  • Q: Find the sum of the greatest 5-digit and smallest 4-digit whole numbers.
    Ans: Rule: The greatest 5-digit number has 9 in every place. The smallest 4-digit number begins with 1 followed by zeros. To find the sum, add the two numbers column by column.
    The greatest 5-digit number is 99,999.
    The smallest 4-digit number is 1,000.
    Ones: 9 + 0 = 9; write 9.
    Tens: 9 + 0 = 9; write 9.
    Hundreds: 9 + 0 = 9; write 9.
    Thousands: 9 + 1 = 10; write 0, carry 1.
    Ten thousands: 9 + 0 + carry 1 = 10; write 0, carry 1.
    Answer: 99,999 + 1,000 = 100,999

Try It! (book p. 15)

  • Q: Copy and complete the following addition table: Ten Thousands, Thousands, Hundreds, Tens, Ones: first number 5, _, _, 3, _ ; second number +, _, 2, 9, _, 4 ; sum 7, 9, 4, 1, 8.
    Ans: Rule: Work column by column from the ones place, using the sum to find each missing digit and any carry.
    Ones: missing digit + 4 = 8, so the missing ones digit of the first number is 4. No carry.
    Tens: 3 + missing digit = 1 in the sum. This is only possible with a carry: 3 + 8 = 11, so the missing tens digit of the second number is 8; write 1, carry 1.
    Hundreds: missing digit + 9 + carry 1 = 4 in the sum, with a carry: missing digit + 10 = 14, so the missing hundreds digit of the first number is 4; carry 1.
    Thousands: missing digit + 2 + carry 1 = 9, so the missing thousands digit of the first number is 6. No carry.
    Ten Thousands: 5 + missing digit = 7, so the missing ten thousands digit of the second number is 2.
    Check: 56,434 + 22,984 = 79,418.
    Answer: First number: 56,434; Second number: 22,984; Sum: 79,418

Try Yourself (book p. 18)

  • Q: Subtract the greatest 4-digit number from the smallest 5-digit number.
    Ans: Rule: The smallest 5-digit number begins with 1 followed by zeros. The greatest 4-digit number has 9 in every place. Subtract column by column from the ones place, borrowing from the next place whenever the top digit is smaller.
    The smallest 5-digit number is 10,000.
    The greatest 4-digit number is 9,999.
    Ones: 0 is smaller than 9, so we must borrow. The tens, hundreds and thousands places are all 0, so the borrowing comes from the ten thousands place: 1 ten thousand becomes 10 thousands, then 1 thousand becomes 10 hundreds, then 1 hundred becomes 10 tens, then 1 ten becomes 10 ones. After this borrowing, 10,000 is regrouped as 0 ten thousands, 9 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones.
    Ones: 10 - 9 = 1; write 1.
    Tens: 9 - 9 = 0; write 0.
    Hundreds: 9 - 9 = 0; write 0.
    Thousands: 9 - 9 = 0; write 0.
    Ten thousands: 0 - 0 = 0; write 0.
    Answer: 10,000 - 9,999 = 1

Try It! (book p. 18)

  • Q: Find two numbers from the given numbers 46,924; 72,876; 31,524; 66,234; 89,076 whose sum is 78,448 and the difference is 15,400.
    Ans: Rule: Try pairs from the given numbers and check both the sum and the difference.
    Try 46,924 and 31,524.
    Add: 46,924 + 31,524 = 78,448. This matches the given sum.
    Subtract: 46,924 - 31,524 = 15,400. This matches the given difference.
    Both conditions are satisfied by the same pair.
    Answer: The two numbers are 46,924 and 31,524

lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • To multiply, multiply by the ones digit first, then by the tens digit, and add the partial products.
  • Find the red blocks by multiplying, then the green blocks by subtracting, then add all three colours.
  • A missing circle number is found by dividing the product in the box by the number in the known circle.
  • Each term is obtained by adding 5 to the previous term.
  • Look down a column, and look along a diagonal, and find how each next number is obtained.
  • Each term is obtained by adding 3 to the previous term.
  • Each term is obtained by subtracting 5 from the previous term.

Unit Opener (book p. 22)

  • Q: The earth completes its revolution around the sun in 365 days approximately. In how many days will it complete 3 revolutions?
    Ans: Rule: To multiply, multiply by the ones digit first, then by the tens digit, and add the partial products.
    Days for 3 revolutions = 365 x 3
    Multiply the ones: 3 x 5 = 15. Write 5, carry 1.
    Multiply the tens: 3 x 6 = 18, add the carried 1: 18 + 1 = 19. Write 9, carry 1.
    Multiply the hundreds: 3 x 3 = 9, add the carried 1: 9 + 1 = 10. Write 0, carry 1.
    Write the final carried digit 1 at the front.
    365 x 3 = 1,095
    Answer: 1,095 days

Try Yourself (book p. 24)

  • Q: Try Yourself: Multiply the greatest 4-digit number with the greatest 2-digit number.
    Ans: The greatest 4-digit number is 9,999.
    The greatest 2-digit number is 99.
    Rule: To multiply, multiply by the ones digit first, then by the tens digit, and add the partial products.
    Multiply by the ones digit: 9,999 x 9 = 89,991
    Multiply by the tens digit: 9,999 x 90 = 899,910
    Add the partial products: 89,991 + 899,910 = 989,901
    Answer: 989,901
  • Q: Try Yourself: Multiply the smallest 2-digit number with smallest 4-digit number.
    Ans: The smallest 2-digit number is 10.
    The smallest 4-digit number is 1,000.
    Rule: To multiply, multiply by the ones digit first, then by the tens digit, and add the partial products.
    Multiply by the ones digit: 1,000 x 0 = 0
    Multiply by the tens digit: 1,000 x 10 = 10,000
    Add the partial products: 0 + 10,000 = 10,000
    Answer: 10,000

Try Yourself (book p. 28)

  • Q: Try Yourself: A shopkeeper has three coloured blocks. The blocks in blue colour are 245. The red blocks are three times more the blue blocks. The green blocks are 415 less than the red blocks. Find the total number of blocks.
    Ans: Rule: Find the red blocks by multiplying, then the green blocks by subtracting, then add all three colours.
    Blue blocks = 245
    Red blocks = 245 x 3 = 735
    Green blocks = 735 - 415 = 320
    Total blocks = 245 + 735 + 320
    245 + 735 = 980
    980 + 320 = 1,300
    Answer: 1,300 blocks

Try It! (book p. 29)

  • Q: Try It! The numbers given in the boxes are the product of the numbers given in the two circles at both ends of squares. Find and write the correct numbers in the blank circles. (One circle has 12; the box on its side is 2,808 and the box on the other side is 2,340.)
    Ans: Rule: A missing circle number is found by dividing the product in the box by the number in the known circle.
    Top circle: 2,808 / 12 = 234
    Check: 234 x 12 = 2,808
    Bottom right circle: 2,340 / 234 = 10
    Check: 234 x 10 = 2,340
    Answer: The top circle is 234 and the bottom right circle is 10

Try Yourself (book p. 30)

  • Q: Try Yourself: Find the next two terms of this sequence. 5, 10, 15, 20, _____, _____
    Ans: Rule: Each term is obtained by adding 5 to the previous term.
    10 - 5 = 5, 15 - 10 = 5, 20 - 15 = 5, so the rule is adding 5.
    Next term: 20 + 5 = 25
    Next term: 25 + 5 = 30
    Answer: 25, 30

Try Yourself (book p. 31)

  • Q: Try Yourself: Observe the hundred's chart and find at least 2 patterns of different mathematical operations. Also find the rules of these patterns.
    Ans: Rule: Look down a column, and look along a diagonal, and find how each next number is obtained.
    Pattern 1: 7, 17, 27, 37, 47, 57, 67, 77, 87, 97 (down the column of numbers ending in 7)
    17 - 7 = 10, 27 - 17 = 10, so the rule is adding 10.
    Pattern 2: 95, 84, 73, 62, 51 (diagonally down to the left from 95)
    95 - 84 = 11, 84 - 73 = 11, so the rule is subtracting 11.
    Answer: Pattern 1 rule is adding 10; Pattern 2 rule is subtracting 11 (other correct patterns are also possible)

Try It! (book p. 32)

  • Q: Try It! Complete the patterns. a) 2, 5, 8, 11, _____, _____
    Ans: Rule: Each term is obtained by adding 3 to the previous term.
    5 - 2 = 3, 8 - 5 = 3, 11 - 8 = 3
    Next term: 11 + 3 = 14
    Next term: 14 + 3 = 17
    Answer: 14, 17
  • Q: Try It! Complete the patterns. b) 40, 35, 30, 25, _____, _____
    Ans: Rule: Each term is obtained by subtracting 5 from the previous term.
    40 - 35 = 5, 35 - 30 = 5, 30 - 25 = 5
    Next term: 25 - 5 = 20
    Next term: 20 - 5 = 15
    Answer: 20, 15

lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A composite number has more than two factors. Check every number between 30 and 50 and keep the numbers that have a factor other than 1 and the number itself.
  • A prime number has only two factors, 1 and the number itself. A number with more than two factors is composite.
  • A composite number has more than two factors. 1 is neither prime nor composite. Every number from 1 to 100 that is not prime and is not 1 is composite.

lessons.title: Review Exercise — Part 1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A composite number has more than two factors. 1 is not composite, and 2 and 3 are prime, so start counting from 4.
  • A prime number has only two factors, 1 and the number itself. Check every number between 21 and 60.

Review Exercise (Questions 1–26)

  • Q: 1a) Encircle the correct answer: 13 is a __________ number.
    Options: (a) composite   (b) common   (c) multiple   (d) prime
    Ans: prime
  • Q: 1b) Encircle the correct answer: If __________ of the all digits of a number is divisible by 3 then that number is divisible by 3.
    Options: (a) sum   (b) difference   (c) product   (d) quotient
    Ans: sum
  • Q: 1c) Encircle the correct answer: The Prime factorization of 24 is:
    Options: (a) 8 x 3   (b) 1 x 24   (c) 2 x 2 x 2 x 3   (d) 2 x 6 x 2
    Ans: 2 x 2 x 2 x 3
  • Q: 1d) Encircle the correct answer: The common factors of 2 and 4 is __________. Note: The printed answer key gives iii (4, 8), which is incorrect.
    Options: (a) 1, 2   (b) 2, 4   (c) 4, 8   (d) 8, 12
    Ans: 1, 2
  • Q: 1e) Encircle the correct answer: The first common multiple of 5 and 10 is __________.
    Options: (a) 5   (b) 10   (c) 20   (d) 50
    Ans: 10
  • Q: 2a) Use the divisibility rule to complete the table: For 112, write Yes or No for divisible by 2, divisible by 3, divisible by 5 and divisible by 10.
    Ans: Rules: A number is divisible by 2 if its ones digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8; by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3; by 5 if its ones digit is 0 or 5; by 10 if its ones digit is 0.
    The number is 112. Its ones digit is 2.

mcqs.q: If __________ of the all digits of a number is divisible by 3 then that number is divisible by 3.
mcqs.why:
Rule: A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 3.
So the missing word in the sentence is the sum of the digits.
Answer: sum

Answer: 2 x 2 x 2 x 3

Method: First write the factors of each number. The factors that are the same in all the numbers are the common factors.
Factors of 28 = 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28
Factors of 56 = 1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 14, 28, 56
Factors of 14 = 1, 2, 7, 14
The factors common to all the numbers are: 1, 2, 7, 14
Answer: The common factors of 28, 56, 14 are 1, 2, 7, 14.

mcqs.q: What is the first common multiple of 2 and 7?
mcqs.why:
Method: Write the multiples of each number. The smallest multiple that is the same in all the lists is the first common multiple.
Multiples of 2 = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14
Multiples of 7 = 7, 14
The smallest multiple common to all the numbers is 14.
Answer: The first common multiple of 2 and 7 is 14.

mcqs.q: What is the first common multiple of 6 and 10?
mcqs.why:
Method: Write the multiples of each number. The smallest multiple that is the same in all the lists is the first common multiple.
Multiples of 6 = 6, 12, 18, 24, 30
Multiples of 10 = 10, 20, 30
The smallest multiple common to all the numbers is 30.
Answer: The first common multiple of 6 and 10 is 30.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 3.
  • A number is divisible by 5 if the digit at the ones place is 0 or 5.
  • A number divisible by 2, 3, 5 and 10 must end with 0 (for 2, 5 and 10) and the sum of its digits must be divisible by 3.
  • A prime number is a number greater than 1 having only two factors, 1 and the number itself.
  • A composite number has more than two factors.

Try Yourself (book p. 37)

  • Q: Amar has Rs. 5,040. Is this amount divisible by 3?
    Ans: Rule: A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 3.
    The number is 5,040.
    Sum of digits = 5 + 0 + 4 + 0 = 9
    9 is divisible by 3, because 9 / 3 = 3.
    So, 5,040 is divisible by 3.
    Answer: Yes, Rs. 5,040 is divisible by 3.

Try Yourself (book p. 38)

  • Q: The total number of pages in a book are 230. Can we divide these pages into groups of 5?
    Ans: Rule: A number is divisible by 5 if the digit at the ones place is 0 or 5.
    The number is 230.
    The digit at the ones place of 230 is 0.
    So, 230 is divisible by 5.
    230 / 5 = 46, so the pages make 46 groups of 5.
    Answer: Yes, the 230 pages can be divided into groups of 5 (46 groups).
  • Q: Try It! Write 5 numbers that are divisible by 2, 3, 5 and 10.
    Ans: Rule: A number divisible by 2, 3, 5 and 10 must end with 0 (for 2, 5 and 10) and the sum of its digits must be divisible by 3.
    30: ends with 0, and 3 + 0 = 3, which is divisible by 3.
    60: ends with 0, and 6 + 0 = 6, which is divisible by 3.
    90: ends with 0, and 9 + 0 = 9, which is divisible by 3.
    120: ends with 0, and 1 + 2 + 0 = 3, which is divisible by 3.
    150: ends with 0, and 1 + 5 + 0 = 6, which is divisible by 3.
    Answer: 30, 60, 90, 120, 150 are divisible by 2, 3, 5 and 10.

Try Yourself (book p. 41)

  • Q: 10 is the multiple of which numbers/factors?
    Ans: Method: 10 is a multiple of every number that divides 10 completely. These numbers are the factors of 10.
    10 = 1 x 10
    10 = 2 x 5
    10 = 5 x 2
    10 = 10 x 1
    1, 2, 5 and 10 divide 10 completely.
    Answer: 10 is a multiple of 1, 2, 5 and 10.

Try Yourself (book p. 42)

  • Q: i) Write 5 prime numbers.
    Ans: Rule: A prime number is a number greater than 1 having only two factors, 1 and the number itself.
    2 has factors 1 and 2 only, so 2 is prime.
    3 has factors 1 and 3 only, so 3 is prime.
    5 has factors 1 and 5 only, so 5 is prime.
    7 has factors 1 and 7 only, so 7 is prime.
    11 has factors 1 and 11 only, so 11 is prime.
    Answer: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 are 5 prime numbers.
  • Q: ii) What is the greatest and smallest composite number between 1 and 100?
    Ans: Rule: A composite number has more than two factors.
    The smallest number with more than two factors is 4, because 4 = 1 x 4 and 4 = 2 x 2, so its factors are 1, 2 and 4.
    Counting down from 100, 99 = 9 x 11, so 99 has factors 1, 9, 11 and 99 and is composite. It is the greatest composite number between 1 and 100.
    Answer: The smallest composite number between 1 and 100 is 4 and the greatest composite number between 1 and 100 is 99.

Try Yourself (book p. 45)

  • Q: Find the common factors of 30 and 45.
    Ans: Method: First write the factors of each number. The factors that are the same in all the numbers are the common factors.
    Factors of 30 = 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30
    Factors of 45 = 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45
    The factors common to all the numbers are: 1, 3, 5, 15
    Answer: The common factors of 30 and 45 are 1, 3, 5, 15.

Try Yourself (book p. 46)

  • Q: 1. Find first two common multiples of 9 and 15.
    Ans: Method: Write the multiples of each number. The multiples that are the same in both lists are the common multiples.
    Multiples of 9 = 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72, 81, 90
    Multiples of 15 = 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90
    The first two multiples common to both numbers are 45 and 90.
    Answer: The first two common multiples of 9 and 15 are 45 and 90.
  • Q: 2. Find the first common multiple of 8 and 24.
    Ans: Method: Write the multiples of each number. The smallest multiple that is the same in all the lists is the first common multiple.
    Multiples of 8 = 8, 16, 24
    Multiples of 24 = 24
    The smallest multiple common to all the numbers is 24.
    Answer: The first common multiple of 8 and 24 is 24.

lessons.title: Exercise 1 — Part 1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Fractions with different denominators are unlike fractions.
  • Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions.
  • To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
  • To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
  • A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator. A mixed number has a whole number part and a proper fraction part.

Exercise 1 (Questions 1–25)

  • Q: 1a) Encircle the unlike fractions: 3/5, 1/2. Are they like or unlike fractions?
    Ans: Rule: Fractions with different denominators are unlike fractions.
    Denominator of 3/5 = 5
    Denominator of 1/2 = 2
    5 and 2 are different.
    Answer: Unlike fractions - encircle 3/5 and 1/2.
  • Q: 1b) Encircle the unlike fractions: 7/9, 4/9. Are they like or unlike fractions?
    Ans: Rule: Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions.
    Denominator of 7/9 = 9
    Denominator of 4/9 = 9
    Both denominators are the same (9).
    Answer: Like fractions - do not encircle.
  • Q: 1c) Encircle the unlike fractions: 6/11, 1/11. Are they like or unlike fractions?
    Ans: Rule: Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions.
    Denominator of 6/11 = 11
    Denominator of 1/11 = 11
    Both denominators are the same (11).
    Answer: Like fractions - do not encircle.
  • Q: 1d) Encircle the unlike fractions: 2/8, 3/8. Are they like or unlike fractions?
    Ans: Rule: Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions.
    Denominator of 2/8 = 8
    Denominator of 3/8 = 8
    Both denominators are the same (8).
    Answer: Like fractions - do not encircle.
  • Q: 1e) Encircle the unlike fractions: 6/10, 1/5. Are they like or unlike fractions?
    Ans: Rule: Fractions with different denominators are unlike fractions.
    Denominator of 6/10 = 10
    Denominator of 1/5 = 5
    10 and 5 are different.
    Answer: Unlike fractions - encircle 6/10 and 1/5.
  • Q: 1f) Encircle the unlike fractions: 5/9, 2/7. Are they like or unlike fractions?
    Ans: Rule: Fractions with different denominators are unlike fractions.
    Denominator of 5/9 = 9
    Denominator of 2/7 = 7
    9 and 7 are different.
    Answer: Unlike fractions - encircle 5/9 and 2/7.
  • Q: 2a) Compare the given fractions and write the symbol of <, > or =: 1/2 ___ 3/6
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 2 and 6 = 6
    1/2 = (1 x 3)/(2 x 3) = 3/6
    3/6 stays 3/6
    3 = 3, so the fractions are equal.
    Answer: 1/2 = 3/6
  • Q: 2b) Compare the given fractions and write the symbol of <, > or =: 4/5 ___ 9/10
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 5 and 10 = 10
    4/5 = (4 x 2)/(5 x 2) = 8/10
    9/10 stays 9/10
    8 is smaller than 9, so 8/10 < 9/10.
    Answer: 4/5 < 9/10
  • Q: 2c) Compare the given fractions and write the symbol of <, > or =: 6/12 ___ 3/4
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 12 and 4 = 12
    6/12 stays 6/12
    3/4 = (3 x 3)/(4 x 3) = 9/12
    6 is smaller than 9, so 6/12 < 9/12.
    Answer: 6/12 < 3/4
  • Q: 2d) Compare the given fractions and write the symbol of <, > or =: 1/7 ___ 5/8
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 7 and 8 = 56
    1/7 = (1 x 8)/(7 x 8) = 8/56
    5/8 = (5 x 7)/(8 x 7) = 35/56
    8 is smaller than 35, so 8/56 < 35/56.
    Answer: 1/7 < 5/8
  • Q: 2e) Compare the given fractions and write the symbol of <, > or =: 2/9 ___ 5/6
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 9 and 6 = 18
    2/9 = (2 x 2)/(9 x 2) = 4/18
    5/6 = (5 x 3)/(6 x 3) = 15/18
    4 is smaller than 15, so 4/18 < 15/18.
    Answer: 2/9 < 5/6
  • Q: 2f) Compare the given fractions and write the symbol of <, > or =: 8/12 ___ 5/7
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 12 and 7 = 84
    8/12 = (8 x 7)/(12 x 7) = 56/84
    5/7 = (5 x 12)/(7 x 12) = 60/84
    56 is smaller than 60, so 56/84 < 60/84.
    Answer: 8/12 < 5/7
  • Q: 2g) Compare the given fractions and write the symbol of <, > or =: 1/3 ___ 1/4
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 3 and 4 = 12
    1/3 = (1 x 4)/(3 x 4) = 4/12
    1/4 = (1 x 3)/(4 x 3) = 3/12
    4 is greater than 3, so 4/12 > 3/12.
    Answer: 1/3 > 1/4
  • Q: 2h) Compare the given fractions and write the symbol of <, > or =: 4/11 ___ 7/10
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 11 and 10 = 110
    4/11 = (4 x 10)/(11 x 10) = 40/110
    7/10 = (7 x 11)/(10 x 11) = 77/110
    40 is smaller than 77, so 40/110 < 77/110.
    Answer: 4/11 < 7/10
  • Q: 3a) Write the fraction into simplest form: 4/20
    Ans: Rule: To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
    Common factor of 4 and 20 = 4
    4/20 = (4 / 4)/(20 / 4)
    = 1/5
    Answer: 1/5
  • Q: 3b) Write the fraction into simplest form: 2/12
    Ans: Rule: To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
    Common factor of 2 and 12 = 2
    2/12 = (2 / 2)/(12 / 2)
    = 1/6
    Answer: 1/6
  • Q: 3c) Write the fraction into simplest form: 30/45
    Ans: Rule: To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
    Common factor of 30 and 45 = 15
    30/45 = (30 / 15)/(45 / 15)
    = 2/3
    Answer: 2/3
  • Q: 3d) Write the fraction into simplest form: 9/27
    Ans: Rule: To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
    Common factor of 9 and 27 = 9
    9/27 = (9 / 9)/(27 / 9)
    = 1/3
    Answer: 1/3
  • Q: 3e) Write the fraction into simplest form: 12/16
    Ans: Rule: To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
    Common factor of 12 and 16 = 4
    12/16 = (12 / 4)/(16 / 4)
    = 3/4
    Answer: 3/4
  • Q: 3f) Write the fraction into simplest form: 15/25
    Ans: Rule: To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
    Common factor of 15 and 25 = 5
    15/25 = (15 / 5)/(25 / 5)
    = 3/5
    Answer: 3/5
  • Q: 3g) Write the fraction into simplest form: 16/24
    Ans: Rule: To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
    Common factor of 16 and 24 = 8
    16/24 = (16 / 8)/(24 / 8)
    = 2/3
    Answer: 2/3
  • Q: 3h) Write the fraction into simplest form: 4/18
    Ans: Rule: To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
    Common factor of 4 and 18 = 2
    4/18 = (4 / 2)/(18 / 2)
    = 2/9
    Answer: 2/9
  • Q: 3i) Write the fraction into simplest form: 14/20
    Ans: Rule: To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
    Common factor of 14 and 20 = 2
    14/20 = (14 / 2)/(20 / 2)
    = 7/10
    Answer: 7/10
  • Q: 3j) Write the fraction into simplest form: 17/34
    Ans: Rule: To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
    Common factor of 17 and 34 = 17
    17/34 = (17 / 17)/(34 / 17)
    = 1/2
    Answer: 1/2
  • Q: 4a) Encircle the proper fractions and tick the mixed numbers: Is 2/5 a proper fraction or a mixed number?
    Ans: Rule: A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator. A mixed number has a whole number part and a proper fraction part.
    Numerator 2 is smaller than denominator 5.

lessons.title: Exercise 1 — Part 2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator. A mixed number has a whole number part and a proper fraction part.
  • Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
  • Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
  • When the numerators are the same, the fraction with the bigger denominator is smaller. To check fully, convert to a common denominator.
  • To order unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
  • A mixed number is a whole number plus a proper fraction.
  • To convert a mixed number into an improper fraction, multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.

Exercise 1 (Questions 26–50)

  • Q: 4b) Encircle the proper fractions and tick the mixed numbers: Is 7/8 a proper fraction or a mixed number?
    Ans: Rule: A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator. A mixed number has a whole number part and a proper fraction part.
    Numerator 7 is smaller than denominator 8.
    Answer: 7/8 is a proper fraction.
  • Q: 4c) Encircle the proper fractions and tick the mixed numbers: Is 3/4 a proper fraction or a mixed number?
    Ans: Rule: A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator. A mixed number has a whole number part and a proper fraction part.
    Numerator 3 is smaller than denominator 4.
    Answer: 3/4 is a proper fraction.
  • Q: 4d) Encircle the proper fractions and tick the mixed numbers: Is 3 4/7 a proper fraction or a mixed number?
    Ans: Rule: A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator. A mixed number has a whole number part and a proper fraction part.
    It has whole number 3 and fraction part 4/7.
    Answer: 3 4/7 is a mixed number (tick it).
  • Q: 4e) Encircle the proper fractions and tick the mixed numbers: Is 1 1/2 a proper fraction or a mixed number?
    Ans: Rule: A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator. A mixed number has a whole number part and a proper fraction part.
    It has whole number 1 and fraction part 1/2.
    Answer: 1 1/2 is a mixed number (tick it).
  • Q: 4f) Encircle the proper fractions and tick the mixed numbers: Is 3/8 a proper fraction or a mixed number?
    Ans: Rule: A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator. A mixed number has a whole number part and a proper fraction part.
    Numerator 3 is smaller than denominator 8.
    Answer: 3/8 is a proper fraction.
  • Q: 4g) Encircle the proper fractions and tick the mixed numbers: Is 9/11 a proper fraction or a mixed number?
    Ans: Rule: A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator. A mixed number has a whole number part and a proper fraction part.
    Numerator 9 is smaller than denominator 11.
    Answer: 9/11 is a proper fraction.
  • Q: 4h) Encircle the proper fractions and tick the mixed numbers: Is 3 7/11 a proper fraction or a mixed number?
    Ans: Rule: A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator. A mixed number has a whole number part and a proper fraction part.
    It has whole number 3 and fraction part 7/11.
    Answer: 3 7/11 is a mixed number (tick it).
  • Q: 4i) Encircle the proper fractions and tick the mixed numbers: Is 6/7 a proper fraction or a mixed number?
    Ans: Rule: A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator. A mixed number has a whole number part and a proper fraction part.
    Numerator 6 is smaller than denominator 7.
    Answer: 6/7 is a proper fraction.
  • Q: 4j) Encircle the proper fractions and tick the mixed numbers: Is 11 1/2 a proper fraction or a mixed number?
    Ans: Rule: A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator. A mixed number has a whole number part and a proper fraction part.
    It has whole number 11 and fraction part 1/2.
    Answer: 11 1/2 is a mixed number (tick it).
  • Q: 5a) Convert the improper fraction to a mixed number: 8/5
    Ans: Rule: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
    8 / 5 = 1, remainder 3
    8/5 = 1 + 3/5
    = 1 3/5
    Answer: 1 3/5
  • Q: 5b) Convert the improper fraction to a mixed number: 11/5
    Ans: Rule: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
    11 / 5 = 2, remainder 1
    11/5 = 2 + 1/5
    = 2 1/5
    Answer: 2 1/5
  • Q: 5c) Convert the improper fraction to a mixed number: 13/10
    Ans: Rule: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
    13 / 10 = 1, remainder 3
    13/10 = 1 + 3/10
    = 1 3/10
    Answer: 1 3/10
  • Q: 5d) Convert the improper fraction to a mixed number: 20/9
    Ans: Rule: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
    20 / 9 = 2, remainder 2
    20/9 = 2 + 2/9
    = 2 2/9
    Answer: 2 2/9
  • Q: 5e) Convert the improper fraction to a mixed number: 15/2
    Ans: Rule: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
    15 / 2 = 7, remainder 1
    15/2 = 7 + 1/2
    = 7 1/2
    Answer: 7 1/2
  • Q: 6a) Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: 2 3/5
    Ans: Rule: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
    2 3/5 = ((2 x 5) + 3)/5
    = (10 + 3)/5
    = 13/5
    Answer: 13/5
  • Q: 6b) Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: 7 5/6
    Ans: Rule: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
    7 5/6 = ((7 x 6) + 5)/6
    = (42 + 5)/6
    = 47/6
    Answer: 47/6
  • Q: 6c) Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: 4 1/7
    Ans: Rule: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
    4 1/7 = ((4 x 7) + 1)/7
    = (28 + 1)/7
    = 29/7
    Answer: 29/7
  • Q: 6d) Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: 5 3/11
    Ans: Rule: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
    5 3/11 = ((5 x 11) + 3)/11
    = (55 + 3)/11
    = 58/11
    Answer: 58/11
  • Q: 6e) Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: 6 1/3
    Ans: Rule: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
    6 1/3 = ((6 x 3) + 1)/3
    = (18 + 1)/3
    = 19/3
    Answer: 19/3
  • Q: 6f) Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: 2 4/13
    Ans: Rule: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
    2 4/13 = ((2 x 13) + 4)/13
    = (26 + 4)/13
    = 30/13
    Answer: 30/13
  • Q: 7a) Write the given fractions in ascending and descending order: 3/5, 3/9, 3/7
    Ans: Rule: When the numerators are the same, the fraction with the bigger denominator is smaller. To check fully, convert to a common denominator.
    Common denominator of 5, 9 and 7 = 315
    3/5 = (3 x 63)/(5 x 63) = 189/315
    3/9 = (3 x 35)/(9 x 35) = 105/315
    3/7 = (3 x 45)/(7 x 45) = 135/315
    105 < 135 < 189, so 3/9 < 3/7 < 3/5.
    Answer: Ascending order: 3/9, 3/7, 3/5. Descending order: 3/5, 3/7, 3/9
  • Q: 7b) Write the given fractions in ascending and descending order: 3/4, 1/3, 6/7
    Ans: Rule: To order unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 4, 3 and 7 = 84
    3/4 = (3 x 21)/(4 x 21) = 63/84
    1/3 = (1 x 28)/(3 x 28) = 28/84
    6/7 = (6 x 12)/(7 x 12) = 72/84
    28 < 63 < 72, so 1/3 < 3/4 < 6/7.
    Answer: Ascending order: 1/3, 3/4, 6/7. Descending order: 6/7, 3/4, 1/3
  • Q: 7c) Write the given fractions in ascending and descending order: 3/5, 2/10, 4/15
    Ans: Rule: To order unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 5, 10 and 15 = 30
    3/5 = (3 x 6)/(5 x 6) = 18/30
    2/10 = (2 x 3)/(10 x 3) = 6/30
    4/15 = (4 x 2)/(15 x 2) = 8/30
    6 < 8 < 18, so 2/10 < 4/15 < 3/5.
    Answer: Ascending order: 2/10, 4/15, 3/5. Descending order: 3/5, 4/15, 2/10
  • Q: 8) Ali has three full and one half pizza. How can we write this in mixed number form?

    = 3/2
    Answer: 3/2 kilogram

lessons.title: Exercise 2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • To add like fractions, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
  • First find the greater fraction, then subtract the smaller numerator from the greater numerator and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
  • To find the total part painted, add the like fractions: add the numerators and keep the denominator the same.
  • To find how much more, subtract the like fractions: subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same.
  • To find the total quantity, add the like fractions: add the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
  • To find the total time, add the like fractions: add the numerators and keep the denominator the same.
  • For like fractions, the fraction with the greater numerator is greater. To find how much more, subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same.

Exercise 2

  • Q: 3a) A painter paints 7/13 parts of the wall in one day and 3/13 part on the second day. How much wall does he paint in two days?

  • Q: 3b) A painter paints 7/13 parts of the wall in one day and 3/13 part on the second day. How much more does he paint on the first day?

  • Q: 6) Shiraz and Omar invest money in a business. Shiraz gets 7/11 share and Omar gets 10/11 share of the profit. Whose share is more? How much?

lessons.title: Exercise 3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • To multiply a fraction or mixed number by a whole number, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
  • To multiply fractions, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Then simplify if possible.
  • To divide a fraction by a whole number, change the division sign to multiplication and write the whole number as its reciprocal (1 over the number), then multiply.
  • To find the weight of 1 packet, divide the total weight by the number of packets. Change the mixed number into an improper fraction and change division by a whole number into multiplication by its reciprocal.
  • 'Of' means multiply. Multiply the fraction by the sister's age.
  • To share equally, divide the total packets by the number of children. Change the mixed number into an improper fraction and change division by a whole number into multiplication by its reciprocal.
  • He makes the trip 5 times, so multiply the one-trip distance by 5. First change the mixed number into an improper fraction.

Exercise 3

  • Q: 1a) Multiply the following: 6/7, 4
    Ans: Rule: To multiply a fraction or mixed number by a whole number, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    6/7 x 4 = (6 x 4)/7
    = 24/7
    Answer: 24/7
  • Q: 1b) Multiply the following: 9, 5/6

    = 45/6
    Answer: 45/6
  • Q: 1c) Multiply the following: 13/11, 11
    Ans: Rule: To multiply a fraction or mixed number by a whole number, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.

    = 143/11
    = 13
    Answer: 13
  • Q: 1d) Multiply the following: 8/9, 6
    Ans: Rule: To multiply a fraction or mixed number by a whole number, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    8/9 x 6 = (8 x 6)/9
    = 48/9
    Divide numerator and denominator by 3: 48/9 = 16/3
    Answer: 16/3
  • Q: 1e) Multiply the following: 1/10, 2
    Ans: Rule: To multiply a fraction or mixed number by a whole number, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    1/10 x 2 = (1 x 2)/10
    = 2/10
    Divide numerator and denominator by 2: 2/10 = 1/5
    Answer: 1/5
  • Q: 1f) Multiply the following: 6/13, 1
    Ans: Rule: To multiply a fraction or mixed number by a whole number, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    6/13 x 1 = (6 x 1)/13
    = 6/13
    Answer: 6/13
  • Q: 1g) Multiply the following: 7/11, 2
    Ans: Rule: To multiply a fraction or mixed number by a whole number, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    7/11 x 2 = (7 x 2)/11
    = 14/11
    Answer: 14/11
  • Q: 1h) Multiply the following: 3 2/3, 1
    Ans: Rule: To multiply a fraction or mixed number by a whole number, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    3 2/3 = ((3 x 3) + 2)/3 = 11/3
    11/3 x 1 = (11 x 1)/3
    = 11/3
    Answer: 11/3
  • Q: 2a) Solve the given fractions: 6/2 x 3/6
    Ans: Rule: To multiply fractions, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Then simplify if possible.
    6/2 x 3/6 = (6 x 3)/(2 x 6)
    = 18/12
    Divide numerator and denominator by 6: 18/12 = 3/2
    Answer: 3/2
  • Q: 2b) Solve the given fractions: 9/11 x 5/10
    Ans: Rule: To multiply fractions, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Then simplify if possible.

    Divide numerator and denominator by 5: 45/110 = 9/22
    Answer: 9/22
  • Q: 2c) Solve the given fractions: 3/17 x 3 3/4
    Ans: Rule: To multiply fractions, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Then simplify if possible.

  • Q: 2d) Solve the given fractions: 7 1/7 x 1 5/8

    7 1/7 = ((7 x 7) + 1)/7 = 50/7

    Answer: 77/30
  • Q: 3a) Solve the following: 7/20 / 2

  • Q: 3c) Solve the following: 20/35 / 9

  • Q: 3d) Solve the following: 21/27 / 3

    14/16 / 7 = 14/16 x 1/7

    Divide numerator and denominator by 14: 14/112 = 1/8
    Answer: 1/8
  • Q: 3f) Solve the following: 15/20 / 21

    15/20 / 21 = 15/20 x 1/21

    = 15/420

  • Q: 3g) Solve the following: 18/24 / 3

  • Q: 3h) Solve the following: 14/18 / 18

    = (14 x 1)/(18 x 18)
    = 14/324
    Divide numerator and denominator by 2: 14/324 = 7/162
    Answer: 7/162
  • Q: 4) If the weight of 5 packets of sugar is 4 7/8 kilogram. What will be the weight of 1 packet of sugar?
    Ans: Rule: To find the weight of 1 packet, divide the total weight by the number of packets. Change the mixed number into an improper fraction and change division by a whole number into multiplication by its reciprocal.
    4 7/8 = ((4 x 8) + 7)/8 = 39/8
    Weight of 1 packet = 39/8 / 5
    = 39/8 x 1/5
    = (39 x 1)/(8 x 5)
    = 39/40
    Answer: 39/40 kilogram
  • Q: 5a) Ayesha's age is 1/2 of her sister's age. If her sister is 20 years old, how old is Ayesha?
    Ans: Rule: 'Of' means multiply. Multiply the fraction by the sister's age.
    Ayesha's age = 1/2 of 20

    Answer: 15 years old
  • Q: 6a) Kamal will distribute 4 1/2 packets of candies among 6 children. How many packets of candies will each child get?
    Ans: Rule: To share equally, divide the total packets by the number of children. Change the mixed number into an improper fraction and change division by a whole number into multiplication by its reciprocal.
    4 1/2 = ((4 x 2) + 1)/2 = 9/2
    Each child gets = 9/2 / 6
    = 9/2 x 1/6
    = (9 x 1)/(2 x 6)
    = 9/12
    Divide numerator and denominator by 3: 9/12 = 3/4
    Answer: 3/4 packets
  • Q: 6b) Kamal will distribute 4 1/2 packets of candies among 9 children. How many packets of candies will each child get?
    Ans: Rule: To share equally, divide the total packets by the number of children. Change the mixed number into an improper fraction and change division by a whole number into multiplication by its reciprocal.
    4 1/2 = ((4 x 2) + 1)/2 = 9/2
    Each child gets = 9/2 / 9
    = 9/2 x 1/9
    = (9 x 1)/(2 x 9)
    = 9/18
    Divide numerator and denominator by 9: 9/18 = 1/2
    Answer: 1/2 packets
  • Q: 7) The distance between Hamid's house and Masjid is 2 3/4 kilometres. If Hamid goes to Masjid for the five prayers then how much distance does he cover daily?
    Ans: Rule: He makes the trip 5 times, so multiply the one-trip distance by 5. First change the mixed number into an improper fraction.
    2 3/4 = ((2 x 4) + 3)/4 = 11/4
    Daily distance = 11/4 x 5
    = (11 x 5)/4
    = 55/4
    55/4 = 13 3/4
    Answer: 55/4 kilometres = 13 3/4 kilometres

mcqs.q: Multiply the following: 6/7, 4
mcqs.why:
Rule: To multiply a fraction or mixed number by a whole number, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
6/7 x 4 = (6 x 4)/7
= 24/7
Answer: 24/7

mcqs.q: Multiply the following: 13/11, 11
mcqs.why:
Rule: To multiply a fraction or mixed number by a whole number, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
13/11 x 11 = (13 x 11)/11

= 13
Answer: 13

mcqs.q: Multiply the following: 8/9, 6
mcqs.why:
Rule: To multiply a fraction or mixed number by a whole number, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
8/9 x 6 = (8 x 6)/9

Divide numerator and denominator by 3: 48/9 = 16/3

mcqs.q: Multiply the following: 1/10, 2
mcqs.why:
Rule: To multiply a fraction or mixed number by a whole number, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
1/10 x 2 = (1 x 2)/10
= 2/10
Divide numerator and denominator by 2: 2/10 = 1/5

mcqs.q: Solve the given fractions: 6/2 x 3/6
mcqs.why:
Rule: To multiply fractions, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Then simplify if possible.
6/2 x 3/6 = (6 x 3)/(2 x 6)
= 18/12
Divide numerator and denominator by 6: 18/12 = 3/2
Answer: 3/2

mcqs.q: Solve the given fractions: 9/11 x 5/10
mcqs.why:

9/11 x 5/10 = (9 x 5)/(11 x 10)
= 45/110
Divide numerator and denominator by 5: 45/110 = 9/22
Answer: 9/22

mcqs.q: Solve the following: 7/20 / 2
mcqs.why:
Rule: To divide a fraction by a whole number, change the division sign to multiplication and write the whole number as its reciprocal (1 over the number), then multiply.
7/20 / 2 = 7/20 x 1/2
= (7 x 1)/(20 x 2)
= 7/40
Answer: 7/40

mcqs.q: Solve the following: 14/16 / 7
mcqs.why:
Rule: To divide a fraction by a whole number, change the division sign to multiplication and write the whole number as its reciprocal (1 over the number), then multiply.
14/16 / 7 = 14/16 x 1/7
= (14 x 1)/(16 x 7)
= 14/112
Divide numerator and denominator by 14: 14/112 = 1/8
Answer: 1/8

mcqs.q: If the weight of 5 packets of sugar is 4 7/8 kilogram. What will be the weight of 1 packet of sugar?
mcqs.why:

4 7/8 = ((4 x 8) + 7)/8 = 39/8
Weight of 1 packet = 39/8 / 5
= 39/8 x 1/5
= (39 x 1)/(8 x 5)
= 39/40
Answer: 39/40 kilogram

mcqs.q: Ayesha's age is 1/2 of her sister's age. If her sister is 20 years old, how old is Ayesha?
mcqs.why:

= 1/2 x 20
= 20/2
= 10
Answer: 10 years old

lessons.title: Review Exercise — Part 1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions.
  • To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
  • To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
  • A unit fraction has numerator 1. An improper fraction has numerator greater than or equal to the denominator.
  • Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.

Review Exercise (Questions 1–27)

  • Q: 1a) _____ is a proper fraction. i) 5/4 ii) 9/7 iii) 1/2 iv) 4/2
    Options: (a) 5/4   (b) 9/7   (c) 1/2   (d) 4/2
    Ans: 1/2
  • Q: 1b) _____ is an improper fraction. i) 5/4 ii) 1/2 iii) 3 5/9 iv) 4/7
    Options: (a) 5/4   (b) 1/2   (c) 3 5/9   (d) 4/7
    Ans: 5/4
  • Q: 1c) 1/4 + 3/4 is equal to. i) 1/4 ii) 3/4 iii) 1 iv) 2/4
    Options: (a) 1/4   (b) 3/4   (c) 1   (d) 2/4
    Ans: 1
  • Q: 1d) 7/6 - 2/6 is equal to. i) 9/6 ii) 2/6 iii) 1/6 iv) 5/6
    Options: (a) 9/6   (b) 2/6   (c) 1/6   (d) 5/6
    Ans: 5/6
  • Q: 1e) The product of 7/6 and 5 is _____. i) 34/6 ii) 34/7 iii) 35/7 iv) 35/6
    Options: (a) 34/6   (b) 34/7   (c) 35/7   (d) 35/6
    Ans: 35/6
  • Q: 2a) Tick the like fractions: 4/9, 1/9, 2/9
    Ans: Rule: Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions.
    All denominators are 9.
    Answer: Like fractions - tick them.
  • Q: 2b) Tick the like fractions: 5/7, 6/11, 2/13

    Denominators are 7, 11 and 13, all different.
    Answer: Not like fractions - do not tick.
  • Q: 2c) Tick the like fractions: 2/17, 9/23, 11/12
    Ans: Rule: Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions.

  • Q: 2d) Tick the like fractions: 6/14, 1/14, 2/14

  • Q: 2e) Tick the like fractions: 4/13, 1/5, 6/7
    Ans: Rule: Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions.

  • Q: 2f) Tick the like fractions: 3/10, 9/10, 1/10
    Ans: Rule: Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions.
    All denominators are 10.
    Answer: Like fractions - tick them.
  • Q: 3a) Compare the given fractions and write the symbol of <, > or =: 9/10 ___ 5/7
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 10 and 7 = 70
    9/10 = (9 x 7)/(10 x 7) = 63/70
    5/7 = (5 x 10)/(7 x 10) = 50/70
    63 is greater than 50, so 63/70 > 50/70.
    Answer: 9/10 > 5/7
  • Q: 3b) Compare the given fractions and write the symbol of <, > or =: 6/13 ___ 1/12
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 13 and 12 = 156
    6/13 = (6 x 12)/(13 x 12) = 72/156
    1/12 = (1 x 13)/(12 x 13) = 13/156
    72 is greater than 13, so 72/156 > 13/156.
    Answer: 6/13 > 1/12
  • Q: 3c) Compare the given fractions and write the symbol of <, > or =: 3/5 ___ 6/11
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 5 and 11 = 55
    3/5 = (3 x 11)/(5 x 11) = 33/55
    6/11 = (6 x 5)/(11 x 5) = 30/55
    33 is greater than 30, so 33/55 > 30/55.
    Answer: 3/5 > 6/11
  • Q: 3d) Compare the given fractions and write the symbol of <, > or =: 8/9 ___ 1/2
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 9 and 2 = 18
    8/9 = (8 x 2)/(9 x 2) = 16/18
    1/2 = (1 x 9)/(2 x 9) = 9/18
    16 is greater than 9, so 16/18 > 9/18.
    Answer: 8/9 > 1/2
  • Q: 4a) Write the given fraction into simplest form: 52/18
    Ans: Rule: To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
    Common factor of 52 and 18 = 2
    52/18 = (52 / 2)/(18 / 2)
    = 26/9
    Answer: 26/9
  • Q: 4b) Write the given fraction into simplest form: 17/51
    Ans: Rule: To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
    Common factor of 17 and 51 = 17
    17/51 = (17 / 17)/(51 / 17)

  • Q: 4c) Write the given fraction into simplest form: 9/19

  • Q: 4d) Write the given fraction into simplest form: 22/33

    22/33 = (22 / 11)/(33 / 11)

    Answer: 2/3
  • Q: 5a) Encircle the unit fraction and tick the improper fraction: Is 9/9 a unit fraction or an improper fraction?
    Ans: Rule: A unit fraction has numerator 1. An improper fraction has numerator greater than or equal to the denominator.
    Numerator 9 is equal to denominator 9.
    Answer: 9/9 is an improper fraction (tick it).
  • Q: 5b) Encircle the unit fraction and tick the improper fraction: Is 1/6 a unit fraction or an improper fraction?

    Ans: Rule: A unit fraction has numerator 1. An improper fraction has numerator greater than or equal to the denominator.
    Numerator is 1.
    Answer: 1/9 is a unit fraction (encircle it).
  • Q: 6a) Convert the improper fraction to a mixed number: 7/5
    Ans: Rule: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
    7 / 5 = 1, remainder 2
    7/5 = 1 + 2/5
    = 1 2/5
    Answer: 1 2/5
  • Q: 6b) Convert the improper fraction to a mixed number: 11/8
    Ans: Rule: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
    11 / 8 = 1, remainder 3
    11/8 = 1 + 3/8
    = 1 3/8
    Answer: 1 3/8
  • Q: 6c) Convert the improper fraction to a mixed number: 17/4
    Ans: Rule: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
    17 / 4 = 4, remainder 1
    17/4 = 4 + 1/4
    = 4 1/4
    Answer: 4 1/4

mcqs.q: _____ is a proper fraction. i) 5/4  ii) 9/7  iii) 1/2  iv) 4/2
mcqs.why: A proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator. In 1/2 the numerator 1 is smaller than the denominator 2. In 5/4, 9/7 and 4/2 the numerator is not smaller than the denominator, so only 1/2 is a proper fraction.

mcqs.q: _____ is an improper fraction. i) 5/4  ii) 1/2  iii) 3 5/9  iv) 4/7
mcqs.why: An improper fraction has numerator greater than or equal to the denominator. In 5/4 the numerator 5 is greater than the denominator 4. 1/2 and 4/7 are proper fractions and 3 5/9 is a mixed number, so 5/4 is the improper fraction.

mcqs.q: 1/4 + 3/4 is equal to. i) 1/4  ii) 3/4  iii) 1  iv) 2/4

1/4 + 3/4 = (1 + 3)/4

= 1
Answer: 1

7/6 - 2/6 = (7 - 2)/6
= 5/6
Answer: 5/6

mcqs.q: The product of 7/6 and 5 is _____. i) 34/6  ii) 34/7  iii) 35/7  iv) 35/6

7/6 x 5 = (7 x 5)/6
= 35/6
Answer: 35/6

mcqs.q: Compare the given fractions and write the symbol of <, > or =: 9/10 ___ 5/7

9/10 = (9 x 7)/(10 x 7) = 63/70
5/7 = (5 x 10)/(7 x 10) = 50/70
63 is greater than 50, so 63/70 > 50/70.

mcqs.q: Compare the given fractions and write the symbol of <, > or =: 8/9 ___ 1/2
