lessons.title: Review Exercise — Part 2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
  • Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
  • To order unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
  • To add like fractions, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
  • To subtract like fractions, subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
  • To multiply fractions, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Then simplify if possible.
  • To divide a fraction by a whole number, change the division sign to multiplication and write the whole number as its reciprocal (1 over the number), then multiply.
  • To divide by 1, the number stays the same. First change the mixed number into an improper fraction.

Review Exercise (Questions 28–53)

  • Q: 6d) Convert the improper fraction to a mixed number: 5/4
    Ans: Rule: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
    5 / 4 = 1, remainder 1
    5/4 = 1 + 1/4
    = 1 1/4
    Answer: 1 1/4
  • Q: 7a) Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: 1 3/5
    Ans: Rule: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
    1 3/5 = ((1 x 5) + 3)/5
    = (5 + 3)/5
    = 8/5
    Answer: 8/5
  • Q: 7b) Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: 3 5/10
    Ans: Rule: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
    3 5/10 = ((3 x 10) + 5)/10
    = (30 + 5)/10
    = 35/10 = 7/2
    Answer: 35/10 = 7/2
  • Q: 7c) Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: 6 4/7
    Ans: Rule: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
    6 4/7 = ((6 x 7) + 4)/7
    = (42 + 4)/7
    = 46/7
    Answer: 46/7
  • Q: 7d) Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: 2 1/9
    Ans: Rule: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
    2 1/9 = ((2 x 9) + 1)/9
    = (18 + 1)/9
    = 19/9
    Answer: 19/9
  • Q: 8a) Write the given fractions in ascending and descending order: 4/8, 5/2, 6/7, 1/6
    Ans: Rule: To order unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 8, 2, 7 and 6 = 168
    4/8 = (4 x 21)/(8 x 21) = 84/168
    5/2 = (5 x 84)/(2 x 84) = 420/168
    6/7 = (6 x 24)/(7 x 24) = 144/168
    1/6 = (1 x 28)/(6 x 28) = 28/168
    28 < 84 < 144 < 420, so 1/6 < 4/8 < 6/7 < 5/2.
    Answer: Ascending order: 1/6, 4/8, 6/7, 5/2. Descending order: 5/2, 6/7, 4/8, 1/6
  • Q: 8b) Write the given fractions in ascending and descending order: 2/9, 8/9, 5/6, 1/3
    Ans: Rule: To order unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 9, 9, 6 and 3 = 18
    2/9 = (2 x 2)/(9 x 2) = 4/18
    8/9 = (8 x 2)/(9 x 2) = 16/18
    5/6 = (5 x 3)/(6 x 3) = 15/18
    1/3 = (1 x 6)/(3 x 6) = 6/18
    4 < 6 < 15 < 16, so 2/9 < 1/3 < 5/6 < 8/9.
    Answer: Ascending order: 2/9, 1/3, 5/6, 8/9. Descending order: 8/9, 5/6, 1/3, 2/9
  • Q: 8c) Write the given fractions in ascending and descending order: 4/12, 7/18, 3/10, 5/6
    Ans: Rule: To order unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 12, 18, 10 and 6 = 180
    4/12 = (4 x 15)/(12 x 15) = 60/180
    7/18 = (7 x 10)/(18 x 10) = 70/180
    3/10 = (3 x 18)/(10 x 18) = 54/180
    5/6 = (5 x 30)/(6 x 30) = 150/180
    54 < 60 < 70 < 150, so 3/10 < 4/12 < 7/18 < 5/6.
    Answer: Ascending order: 3/10, 4/12, 7/18, 5/6. Descending order: 5/6, 7/18, 4/12, 3/10
  • Q: 9a) Add the given fractions: 1/3, 2/3
    Ans: Rule: To add like fractions, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    1/3 + 2/3 = (1 + 2)/3
    = 3/3
    = 1
    Answer: 1
  • Q: 9b) Add the given fractions: 11/12, 7/12
    Ans: Rule: To add like fractions, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    11/12 + 7/12 = (11 + 7)/12
    = 18/12
    Divide numerator and denominator by 6: 18/12 = 3/2
    Answer: 3/2
  • Q: 9c) Add the given fractions: 9/5, 4/5
    Ans: Rule: To add like fractions, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    9/5 + 4/5 = (9 + 4)/5
    = 13/5
    Answer: 13/5
  • Q: 9d) Add the given fractions: 3/9, 7/9
    Ans: Rule: To add like fractions, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    3/9 + 7/9 = (3 + 7)/9
    = 10/9
    Answer: 10/9
  • Q: 10a) Subtract the given fractions: 9/10 - 3/10
    Ans: Rule: To subtract like fractions, subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    9/10 - 3/10 = (9 - 3)/10
    = 6/10
    Divide numerator and denominator by 2: 6/10 = 3/5
    Answer: 3/5
  • Q: 10b) Subtract the given fractions: 8/13 - 2/13
    Ans: Rule: To subtract like fractions, subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    8/13 - 2/13 = (8 - 2)/13
    = 6/13
    Answer: 6/13
  • Q: 10c) Subtract the given fractions: 6/17 - 1/17
    Ans: Rule: To subtract like fractions, subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    6/17 - 1/17 = (6 - 1)/17
    = 5/17
    Answer: 5/17
  • Q: 10d) Subtract the given fractions: 4/7 - 3/7
    Ans: Rule: To subtract like fractions, subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    4/7 - 3/7 = (4 - 3)/7
    = 1/7
    Answer: 1/7
  • Q: 11a) Multiply the given fractions: 9/5 x 7
    Ans: Rule: To multiply fractions, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Then simplify if possible.
    9/5 x 7 = (9 x 7)/5
    = 63/5
    Answer: 63/5
  • Q: 11b) Multiply the given fractions: 4 2/11 x 9/10
    Ans: Rule: To multiply fractions, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Then simplify if possible.
    4 2/11 = ((4 x 11) + 2)/11 = 46/11
    46/11 x 9/10 = (46 x 9)/(11 x 10)
    = 414/110
    Divide numerator and denominator by 2: 414/110 = 207/55
    Answer: 207/55
  • Q: 11c) Multiply the given fractions: 1/2 x 7 8/9
    Ans: Rule: To multiply fractions, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Then simplify if possible.
    7 8/9 = ((7 x 9) + 8)/9 = 71/9
    1/2 x 71/9 = (1 x 71)/(2 x 9)
    = 71/18
    Answer: 71/18
  • Q: 11d) Multiply the given fractions: 3 2/11 x 1 5/14
    Ans: Rule: To multiply fractions, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Then simplify if possible.
    3 2/11 = ((3 x 11) + 2)/11 = 35/11
    1 5/14 = ((1 x 14) + 5)/14 = 19/14
    35/11 x 19/14 = (35 x 19)/(11 x 14)
    = 665/154
    Divide numerator and denominator by 7: 665/154 = 95/22
    Answer: 95/22
  • Q: 11e) Multiply the given fractions: 1 1/4 x 7 3/9
    Ans: Rule: To multiply fractions, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Then simplify if possible.
    1 1/4 = ((1 x 4) + 1)/4 = 5/4
    7 3/9 = ((7 x 9) + 3)/9 = 66/9
    5/4 x 66/9 = (5 x 66)/(4 x 9)
    = 330/36
    Divide numerator and denominator by 6: 330/36 = 55/6
    Answer: 55/6
  • Q: 11f) Multiply the given fractions: 1/6 / 9 (printed with a division sign in the book)
    Ans: Rule: To divide a fraction by a whole number, change the division sign to multiplication and write the whole number as its reciprocal (1 over the number), then multiply.
    1/6 / 9 = 1/6 x 1/9
    = (1 x 1)/(6 x 9)
    = 1/54
    Answer: 1/54
  • Q: 11g) Multiply the given fractions: 4 7/12 / 1 (printed with a division sign in the book)
    Ans: Rule: To divide by 1, the number stays the same. First change the mixed number into an improper fraction.
    4 7/12 = ((4 x 12) + 7)/12 = 55/12
    55/12 / 1 = 55/12
    Answer: 55/12
  • Q: 12) In a garden 7/12 of the trees are mango trees. In another garden 9/12 of the trees are mango trees. How many mango trees are there altogether?
    Ans: Rule: To find the total, add the like fractions: add the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    Total = 7/12 + 9/12
    = (7 + 9)/12
    = 16/12
    Divide numerator and denominator by 4: 16/12 = 4/3
    Answer: 4/3
  • Q: 13) Hania has 12 8/14 meters of ribbon. She wants to cut it into 8 equal pieces. What will be the length of each piece?
    Ans: Rule: To find the length of each piece, divide the total length by the number of pieces. Change the mixed number into an improper fraction and change division by a whole number into multiplication by its reciprocal.
    12 8/14 = ((12 x 14) + 8)/14 = 176/14
    Length of each piece = 176/14 / 8
    = 176/14 x 1/8
    = (176 x 1)/(14 x 8)
    = 176/112
    Divide numerator and denominator by 16: 176/112 = 11/7
    Answer: 11/7 meters
  • Q: 14) Jamal reads 2/7 of 140 pages of a book and Farhan reads 2 times more pages than Jamal. How many pages does Farhan read?
    Ans: Rule: 'Of' means multiply. First find how many pages Jamal reads, then multiply by 2 for Farhan.
    Pages read by Jamal = 2/7 of 140
    = 2/7 x 140
    = (2 x 140)/7
    = 280/7
    = 40 pages
    Pages read by Farhan = 2 x 40
    = 80
    Answer: 80 pages

mcqs.q: Convert the improper fraction to a mixed number: 5/4
mcqs.why:
Rule: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
5 / 4 = 1, remainder 1
5/4 = 1 + 1/4
= 1 1/4
Answer: 1 1/4

mcqs.q: Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: 1 3/5
mcqs.why:
Rule: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
1 3/5 = ((1 x 5) + 3)/5
= (5 + 3)/5
= 8/5
Answer: 8/5

mcqs.q: Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: 3 5/10
mcqs.why:
Rule: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
3 5/10 = ((3 x 10) + 5)/10
= (30 + 5)/10
= 35/10 = 7/2
Answer: 35/10 = 7/2

mcqs.q: Convert the mixed number to an improper fraction: 6 4/7
mcqs.why:
Rule: Multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
6 4/7 = ((6 x 7) + 4)/7
= (42 + 4)/7
= 46/7
Answer: 46/7

mcqs.q: Add the given fractions: 1/3, 2/3
mcqs.why:
Rule: To add like fractions, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
1/3 + 2/3 = (1 + 2)/3
= 3/3
= 1
Answer: 1

mcqs.q: Add the given fractions: 11/12, 7/12
mcqs.why:
Rule: To add like fractions, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
11/12 + 7/12 = (11 + 7)/12
= 18/12
Divide numerator and denominator by 6: 18/12 = 3/2
Answer: 3/2

mcqs.q: Subtract the given fractions: 9/10 - 3/10
mcqs.why:
Rule: To subtract like fractions, subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
9/10 - 3/10 = (9 - 3)/10
= 6/10
Divide numerator and denominator by 2: 6/10 = 3/5
Answer: 3/5

mcqs.q: Subtract the given fractions: 4/7 - 3/7
mcqs.why:
Rule: To subtract like fractions, subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
4/7 - 3/7 = (4 - 3)/7
= 1/7
Answer: 1/7

mcqs.q: Multiply the given fractions: 9/5 x 7
mcqs.why:
Rule: To multiply fractions, first change any mixed number into an improper fraction, then multiply the numerators together and the denominators together. Then simplify if possible.
9/5 x 7 = (9 x 7)/5
= 63/5
Answer: 63/5

mcqs.q: Hania has 12 8/14 meters of ribbon. She wants to cut it into 8 equal pieces. What will be the length of each piece?
mcqs.why:
Rule: To find the length of each piece, divide the total length by the number of pieces. Change the mixed number into an improper fraction and change division by a whole number into multiplication by its reciprocal.
12 8/14 = ((12 x 14) + 8)/14 = 176/14
Length of each piece = 176/14 / 8
= 176/14 x 1/8
= (176 x 1)/(14 x 8)
= 176/112
Divide numerator and denominator by 16: 176/112 = 11/7
Answer: 11/7 meters

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The whole garden is 1, that is, 10/10. Subtract the part with roses from the whole.
  • Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions. Fractions with different denominators are unlike fractions.
  • To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
  • To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
  • To convert an improper fraction into a mixed number, divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
  • To convert a mixed number into an improper fraction, multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
  • A mixed number is a whole number plus a proper fraction. Read each clue one by one.
  • To add like fractions, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same.

Unit Opener (book p. 50)

  • Q: Danyal designed a garden in his home. On one tenth of the garden he grew roses. On the remaining part he grew other plants. On what part of the garden did he grow the other plants?
    Ans: Rule: The whole garden is 1, that is, 10/10. Subtract the part with roses from the whole.
    Part with roses = 1/10
    Remaining part = 1 - 1/10
    = 10/10 - 1/10
    = (10 - 1)/10
    = 9/10
    Answer: He grew the other plants on 9/10 of the garden.

Try Yourself (book p. 52)

  • Q: Separate the like and unlike fractions: a) 1/8, 3/8
    Ans: Rule: Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions. Fractions with different denominators are unlike fractions.
    Denominator of 1/8 = 8
    Denominator of 3/8 = 8
    Both denominators are the same (8).
    Answer: 1/8 and 3/8 are like fractions.
  • Q: Separate the like and unlike fractions: b) 4/5, 7/11, 1/9
    Ans: Rule: Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions. Fractions with different denominators are unlike fractions.
    Denominators are 5, 11 and 9.
    All three denominators are different.
    Answer: 4/5, 7/11 and 1/9 are unlike fractions.
  • Q: Separate the like and unlike fractions: c) 3/7, 4/5
    Ans: Rule: Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions. Fractions with different denominators are unlike fractions.
    Denominator of 3/7 = 7
    Denominator of 4/5 = 5
    The denominators are different.
    Answer: 3/7 and 4/5 are unlike fractions.
  • Q: Separate the like and unlike fractions: d) 4/6, 5/6, 1/6
    Ans: Rule: Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions. Fractions with different denominators are unlike fractions.
    Denominator of each fraction = 6
    All denominators are the same (6).
    Answer: 4/6, 5/6 and 1/6 are like fractions.

Try Yourself (book p. 53)

  • Q: Compare the following: a) 1/4, 3/5
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 4 and 5 = 20
    1/4 = (1 x 5)/(4 x 5) = 5/20
    3/5 = (3 x 4)/(5 x 4) = 12/20
    5 is smaller than 12, so 5/20 < 12/20.
    Answer: 1/4 < 3/5
  • Q: Compare the following: b) 6/7, 2/9
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 7 and 9 = 63
    6/7 = (6 x 9)/(7 x 9) = 54/63
    2/9 = (2 x 7)/(9 x 7) = 14/63
    54 is greater than 14, so 54/63 > 14/63.
    Answer: 6/7 > 2/9
  • Q: Compare the following: c) 9/10, 2/5
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 10 and 5 = 10
    9/10 stays 9/10
    2/5 = (2 x 2)/(5 x 2) = 4/10
    9 is greater than 4, so 9/10 > 4/10.
    Answer: 9/10 > 2/5
  • Q: Compare the following: d) 7/8, 2/4
    Ans: Rule: To compare unlike fractions, convert them into equivalent fractions with the same denominator, then compare the numerators.
    Common denominator of 8 and 4 = 8
    7/8 stays 7/8
    2/4 = (2 x 2)/(4 x 2) = 4/8
    7 is greater than 4, so 7/8 > 4/8.
    Answer: 7/8 > 2/4

Try Yourself (book p. 54)

  • Q: Asad has 18 candies. He eats 6 candies i.e. 6/18 candies. Write this fraction in simplest form.
    Ans: Rule: To write a fraction in simplest form, divide the numerator and the denominator by their common factor.
    Common factor of 6 and 18 = 6
    6/18 = (6 / 6)/(18 / 6)
    = 1/3
    1 and 3 have no common factor except 1.
    Answer: 1/3

Try Yourself (book p. 57)

  • Q: Convert 9/4 into a mixed number.
    Ans: Rule: To convert an improper fraction into a mixed number, divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
    9 / 4 = 2, remainder 1
    9/4 = 2 + 1/4
    = 2 1/4
    Answer: 2 1/4
  • Q: Convert 11/6 into a mixed number.
    Ans: Rule: To convert an improper fraction into a mixed number, divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole number, the remainder is the new numerator and the denominator stays the same.
    11 / 6 = 1, remainder 5
    11/6 = 1 + 5/6
    = 1 5/6
    Answer: 1 5/6

Try Yourself (book p. 58)

  • Q: Convert 4 1/4 into an improper fraction.
    Ans: Rule: To convert a mixed number into an improper fraction, multiply the whole number by the denominator, add the numerator, and write the result over the same denominator.
    4 1/4 = ((4 x 4) + 1)/4
    = (16 + 1)/4
    = 17/4
    Answer: 17/4

Try It! (book p. 59)

  • Q: I am a mixed number between 2 and 10. I am nearer to 8 than 4. If you separate my fractional part then I am an odd number. Who am I?
    Ans: Rule: A mixed number is a whole number plus a proper fraction. Read each clue one by one.
    The number is between 2 and 10.
    Nearer to 8 than to 4 means the number is greater than 6.
    When the fractional part is separated, the remaining whole number is odd, so the whole part is 7 or 9.
    A number with whole part 9 is 9 or more, which is farther from 8 than a number with whole part 7.
    So the whole part is 7, with any proper fraction part, for example 1/2.
    Answer: 7 1/2 (any mixed number with whole part 7, such as 7 1/2, fits the clues)

Try Yourself (book p. 61)

  • Q: Add the following fractions: a) 3/4 + 1/4
    Ans: Rule: To add like fractions, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same.
    3/4 + 1/4 = (3 + 1)/4
    = 4/4
    = 1
    Answer: 1
  • Q: Add the following fractions: b) 9/10 + 7/10
    Ans: Rule: To add like fractions, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    9/10 + 7/10 = (9 + 7)/10
    = 16/10
    Divide numerator and denominator by 2: 16/10 = 8/5
    8/5 = 1 3/5
    Answer: 8/5 = 1 3/5
  • Q: Add the following fractions: c) 3/9 + 7/9
    Ans: Rule: To add like fractions, add the numerators and keep the denominator the same.
    3/9 + 7/9 = (3 + 7)/9
    = 10/9
    10/9 = 1 1/9
    Answer: 10/9 = 1 1/9

Try Yourself (book p. 62)

  • Q: Solve the following fractions: a) 5/8 - 3/8
    Ans: Rule: To subtract like fractions, subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    5/8 - 3/8 = (5 - 3)/8
    = 2/8
    Divide numerator and denominator by 2: 2/8 = 1/4
    Answer: 1/4
  • Q: Solve the following fractions: b) 10/11 - 5/11
    Ans: Rule: To subtract like fractions, subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same.
    10/11 - 5/11 = (10 - 5)/11
    = 5/11
    Answer: 5/11
  • Q: Solve the following fractions: c) 7/12 - 5/12
    Ans: Rule: To subtract like fractions, subtract the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    7/12 - 5/12 = (7 - 5)/12
    = 2/12
    Divide numerator and denominator by 2: 2/12 = 1/6
    Answer: 1/6

Try It! (book p. 62)

  • Q: Maryam wants to make three kinds of biscuits. She needs 2/7 cups of flour for the first kind, 5/7 cups of flour for the second kind, and 3/7 cups of flour for the third kind. How many cups of flour will she need to make the three kinds of biscuits?
    Ans: Rule: To find the total, add the like fractions: add the numerators and keep the denominator the same.
    Total flour = 2/7 + 5/7 + 3/7
    = (2 + 5 + 3)/7
    = 10/7
    10/7 = 1 3/7
    Answer: 1 3/7 cups of flour

Try Yourself (book p. 64)

  • Q: Multiply the following fractions and whole numbers: a) 5/8 x 12
    Ans: Rule: To multiply a fraction by a whole number, multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    5/8 x 12 = (5 x 12)/8
    = 60/8
    Divide numerator and denominator by 4: 60/8 = 15/2
    15/2 = 7 1/2
    Answer: 15/2 = 7 1/2
  • Q: Multiply the following fractions and whole numbers: b) 5/11 x 22
    Ans: Rule: To multiply a fraction by a whole number, multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    5/11 x 22 = (5 x 22)/11
    = 110/11
    = 10
    Answer: 10
  • Q: Multiply the following fractions and whole numbers: c) 6/8 x 4
    Ans: Rule: To multiply a fraction by a whole number, multiply the numerator by the whole number and keep the denominator the same. Then simplify if possible.
    6/8 x 4 = (6 x 4)/8
    = 24/8
    = 3
    Answer: 3

Try It! (book p. 66)

  • Q: 4/8 of 480 animals in the Zoo are rabbits and half of the rabbits are white. How many white rabbits are there?
    Ans: Rule: 'Of' means multiply. First find the number of rabbits, then find half of the rabbits.
    Number of rabbits = 4/8 of 480
    = 4/8 x 480
    = (4 x 480)/8
    = 1920/8
    = 240 rabbits
    White rabbits = 1/2 of 240
    = 1/2 x 240
    = 240/2
    = 120
    Answer: 120 white rabbits

lessons.title: Exercise 1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • count the zeros in the denominator and put the decimal point that many digits from the right in the numerator.
  • the place value of a digit = digit x value of its place.
  • 0.2 means 2 parts out of 10 equal parts.
  • 0.7 means 7 parts out of 10 equal parts.
  • 0.9 means 9 parts out of 10 equal parts.
  • ones place has value 1, so multiply the digit by 1.
  • tenths place has value 0.1, so multiply the digit by 0.1.
  • hundredths place has value 0.01, so multiply the digit by 0.01.

Exercise 1

  • Q: 1(a) Write the fraction 16/100 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: count the zeros in the denominator and put the decimal point that many digits from the right in the numerator.
    Denominator 100 has 2 zeros, so count 2 digits in 16 from right to left.
    16/100 = 0.16
    Answer: 0.16
  • Q: 1(b) Write the fraction 1/10 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: count the zeros in the denominator and put the decimal point that many digits from the right in the numerator.
    Denominator 10 has 1 zero, so count 1 digit in 1 from right to left.
    1/10 = 0.1
    Answer: 0.1
  • Q: 1(c) Write the fraction 324/1000 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: count the zeros in the denominator and put the decimal point that many digits from the right in the numerator.
    Denominator 1,000 has 3 zeros, so count 3 digits in 324 from right to left.
    324/1000 = 0.324
    Answer: 0.324
  • Q: 1(d) Write the fraction 2/100 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: count the zeros in the denominator and put the decimal point that many digits from the right in the numerator.
    Denominator 100 has 2 zeros, so count 2 digits from right to left; write 0 to fill the extra place.
    2/100 = 0.02
    Answer: 0.02
  • Q: 1(e) Write the fraction 70/1000 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: count the zeros in the denominator and put the decimal point that many digits from the right in the numerator.
    Denominator 1,000 has 3 zeros, so count 3 digits in 70 from right to left; write 0 to fill the extra place.
    70/1000 = 0.070 = 0.07
    Answer: 0.07
  • Q: 2(a) Write the place value of the coloured digit in 1.56. (The coloured digit is 5.)
    Ans: Rule: the place value of a digit = digit x value of its place.
    5 is at tenths place.
    5 x 0.1 = 0.5
    Answer: 0.5
  • Q: 2(b) Write the place value of the coloured digit in 45.987. (The coloured digit is 8.)
    Ans: Rule: the place value of a digit = digit x value of its place.
    8 is at hundredths place.
    8 x 0.01 = 0.08
    Answer: 0.08
  • Q: 2(c) Write the place value of the coloured digit in 321.17. (The coloured digit is 3.)
    Ans: Rule: the place value of a digit = digit x value of its place.
    3 is at hundreds place.
    3 x 100 = 300
    Answer: 300
  • Q: 2(d) Write the place value of the coloured digit in 6.897. (The coloured digit is 9.)
    Ans: Rule: the place value of a digit = digit x value of its place.
    9 is at hundredths place.
    9 x 0.01 = 0.09
    Answer: 0.09
  • Q: 2(e) Write the place value of the coloured digit in 6.340. (The coloured digit is 0, the last digit.)
    Ans: Rule: the place value of a digit = digit x value of its place.
    0 is at thousandths place.
    0 x 0.001 = 0.000
    Answer: 0.000
  • Q: 2(f) Write the place value of the coloured digit in 12.123. (The coloured digit is 2, in 12.)
    Ans: Rule: the place value of a digit = digit x value of its place.
    2 is at ones place.
    2 x 1 = 2
    Answer: 2
  • Q: 2(g) Write the place value of the coloured digit in 78.808. (The coloured digit is 8, the last digit.)
    Ans: Rule: the place value of a digit = digit x value of its place.
    8 is at thousandths place.
    8 x 0.001 = 0.008
    Answer: 0.008
  • Q: 2(h) Write the place value of the coloured digit in 4.009. (The coloured digit is 0, the first digit after the decimal point.)
    Ans: Rule: the place value of a digit = digit x value of its place.
    0 is at tenths place.
    0 x 0.1 = 0.0
    Answer: 0.0
  • Q: 3(a) Colour the given shape (a circle divided into 10 equal parts) with the help of the decimal 0.2.
    Ans: Rule: 0.2 means 2 parts out of 10 equal parts.
    0.2 = 2/10
    The circle has 10 equal parts.
    Colour any 2 of the 10 parts.
    Answer: colour 2 out of 10 parts
  • Q: 3(b) Colour the given shape (a rectangle divided into 10 equal strips) with the help of the decimal 0.7.
    Ans: Rule: 0.7 means 7 parts out of 10 equal parts.
    0.7 = 7/10
    The rectangle has 10 equal strips.
    Colour any 7 of the 10 strips.
    Answer: colour 7 out of 10 strips
  • Q: 3(c) Colour the given shape (a rectangle divided into 10 equal parts) with the help of the decimal 0.9.
    Ans: Rule: 0.9 means 9 parts out of 10 equal parts.
    0.9 = 9/10
    The shape has 10 equal parts.
    Colour any 9 of the 10 parts.
    Answer: colour 9 out of 10 parts
  • Q: 4(a)(i) Fill in the blanks: In 7.45, 7 is at ones place, the place value of 7 is: 7 x _____ = _____
    Ans: Rule: ones place has value 1, so multiply the digit by 1.
    7 x 1 = 7
    Answer: 7 x 1 = 7
  • Q: 4(a)(ii) Fill in the blanks: In 7.45, 4 is at tenths place, the place value of 4 is: 4 x _____ = _____

  • Q: 4(b)(iv) Fill in the blanks: In 87.391, 9 is at hundredths place, the place value of 9 is: 9 x _____ = _____
    Ans: Rule: hundredths place has value 0.01, so multiply the digit by 0.01.

  • Q: 4(b)(v) Fill in the blanks: In 87.391, 1 is at thousandths place, the place value of 1 is: 1 x _____ = _____
    Ans: Rule: thousandths place has value 0.001, so multiply the digit by 0.001.

  • Q: 4(c)(i) Fill in the blanks: In 99.999, 9 is at tens place, the place value of 9 is: 9 x _____ = _____

lessons.title: Exercise 2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • denominator 100 has 2 zeros, so put the decimal point 2 digits from the right.
  • denominator 1,000 has 3 zeros, so put the decimal point 3 digits from the right and fill empty places with 0.
  • denominator 10 has 1 zero, so put the decimal point 1 digit from the right.
  • if the denominator is not 10, 100 or 1,000, first make an equivalent fraction with denominator 1,000.
  • 1 decimal place means tenths; write the number over 10.
  • 2 decimal places mean hundredths; write the number over 100 and simplify.
  • 1 decimal place means tenths; write the number over 10 and simplify.
  • keep the whole part and write the decimal part over 100, then simplify.

Exercise 2

  • Q: 1(a) Represent 24/100 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: denominator 100 has 2 zeros, so put the decimal point 2 digits from the right.
    24/100 = 0.24
    Answer: 0.24
  • Q: 1(b) Represent 5/1000 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: denominator 1,000 has 3 zeros, so put the decimal point 3 digits from the right and fill empty places with 0.
    5/1000 = 0.005
    Answer: 0.005
  • Q: 1(c) Represent 6/10 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: denominator 10 has 1 zero, so put the decimal point 1 digit from the right.
    6/10 = 0.6
    Answer: 0.6
  • Q: 1(d) Represent 12/500 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: if the denominator is not 10, 100 or 1,000, first make an equivalent fraction with denominator 1,000.
    12/500 = (12 x 2)/(500 x 2) = 24/1000
    24/1000 = 0.024
    Answer: 0.024
  • Q: 1(e) Represent 3/250 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: if the denominator is not 10, 100 or 1,000, first make an equivalent fraction with denominator 1,000.
    3/250 = (3 x 4)/(250 x 4) = 12/1000
    12/1000 = 0.012
    Answer: 0.012
  • Q: 1(f) Represent 47/25 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: if the denominator is not 10, 100 or 1,000, first make an equivalent fraction with denominator 100.
    47/25 = (47 x 4)/(25 x 4) = 188/100
    188/100 = 1.88
    Answer: 1.88
  • Q: 1(g) Represent 60/200 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: if the denominator is not 10, 100 or 1,000, first make an equivalent fraction with denominator 100.
    60/200 = (60 / 2)/(200 / 2) = 30/100
    30/100 = 0.30 = 0.3
    Answer: 0.3
  • Q: 1(h) Represent 606/1000 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: denominator 1,000 has 3 zeros, so put the decimal point 3 digits from the right.
    606/1000 = 0.606
    Answer: 0.606
  • Q: 1(i) Represent 80/1000 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: denominator 1,000 has 3 zeros, so put the decimal point 3 digits from the right.
    80/1000 = 0.080 = 0.08
    Answer: 0.08
  • Q: 1(j) Represent 1/50 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: if the denominator is not 10, 100 or 1,000, first make an equivalent fraction with denominator 100.
    1/50 = (1 x 2)/(50 x 2) = 2/100
    2/100 = 0.02
    Answer: 0.02
  • Q: 2(a) Convert the decimal 1.3 to a fraction.
    Ans: Rule: 1 decimal place means tenths; write the number over 10.
    1.3 = 1 + 3/10
    1.3 = 13/10
    Answer: 13/10 (1 3/10)
  • Q: 2(b) Convert the decimal 2.04 to a fraction.
    Ans: Rule: 2 decimal places mean hundredths; write the number over 100 and simplify.
    2.04 = 204/100
    Divide numerator and denominator by 4: 204/100 = 51/25
    Answer: 51/25 (2 1/25)
  • Q: 2(c) Convert the decimal 6.98 to a fraction.
    Ans: Rule: 2 decimal places mean hundredths; write the number over 100 and simplify.
    6.98 = 698/100
    Divide numerator and denominator by 2: 698/100 = 349/50
    Answer: 349/50 (6 49/50)
  • Q: 2(d) Convert the decimal 5.5 to a fraction.
    Ans: Rule: 1 decimal place means tenths; write the number over 10 and simplify.
    5.5 = 55/10
    Divide numerator and denominator by 5: 55/10 = 11/2
    Answer: 11/2 (5 1/2)
  • Q: 2(e) Convert the decimal 0.68 to a fraction.
    Ans: Rule: 2 decimal places mean hundredths; write the number over 100 and simplify.
    0.68 = 68/100
    Divide numerator and denominator by 4: 68/100 = 17/25
    Answer: 17/25
  • Q: 2(f) Convert the decimal 21.72 to a fraction.
    Ans: Rule: keep the whole part and write the decimal part over 100, then simplify.
    21.72 = 21 + 72/100
    Divide 72/100 by 4: 72/100 = 18/25
    21.72 = 21 18/25
    Answer: 21 18/25
  • Q: 2(g) Convert the decimal 7.87 to a fraction.
    Ans: Rule: keep the whole part and write the decimal part over 100.
    7.87 = 7 + 87/100
    87/100 cannot be simplified.
    Answer: 7 87/100
  • Q: 2(h) Convert the decimal 0.98 to a fraction.
    Ans: Rule: 2 decimal places mean hundredths; write the number over 100 and simplify.
    0.98 = 98/100
    Divide numerator and denominator by 2: 98/100 = 49/50
    Answer: 49/50
  • Q: 2(i) Convert the decimal 11.1 to a fraction.
    Ans: Rule: 1 decimal place means tenths; keep the whole part and write the decimal part over 10.
    11.1 = 11 + 1/10
    11.1 = 111/10 = 11 1/10
    Answer: 11 1/10
    Note: The printed answer key gives 11 11/100, which is incorrect.
  • Q: 2(j) Convert the decimal 6.10 to a fraction.
    Ans: Rule: keep the whole part and write the decimal part over 100, then simplify.
    6.10 = 6 + 10/100
    Divide 10/100 by 10: 10/100 = 1/10
    6.10 = 6 1/10
    Answer: 6 1/10

lessons.title: Exercise 3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • write the same place values in one column and add place by place.
  • write the same place values in one column and subtract place by place, borrowing when needed.
  • first write 78.9 as 78.90 so both numbers have 2 decimal places, then subtract place by place.
  • altogether means add; add place by place with decimal points in one column.
  • difference means subtract the smaller mass from the greater mass, place by place.
  • total means add; add place by place with decimal points in one column.

Exercise 3

  • Q: 1(a) Add the following: 9.11, 8.03
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and add place by place.
    Hundredths place: 1 + 3 = 4
    Tenths place: 1 + 0 = 1
    Ones place: 9 + 8 = 17, write 7 and carry 1 to the tens place.
    Tens place: 0 + 0 + 1 carried = 1
    Answer: 17.14
  • Q: 1(b) Add the following: 43.1, 12.7
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and add place by place.
    Tenths place: 1 + 7 = 8
    Ones place: 3 + 2 = 5
    Tens place: 4 + 1 = 5
    Answer: 55.8
  • Q: 1(c) Add the following: 52.9, 2.2
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and add place by place.
    Tenths place: 9 + 2 = 11, write 1 and carry 1 to the ones place.
    Ones place: 2 + 2 + 1 carried = 5
    Tens place: 5 + 0 = 5
    Answer: 55.1
  • Q: 1(d) Add the following: 5.69, 2.98
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and add place by place.
    Hundredths place: 9 + 8 = 17, write 7 and carry 1 to the tenths place.
    Tenths place: 6 + 9 + 1 carried = 16, write 6 and carry 1 to the ones place.
    Ones place: 5 + 2 + 1 carried = 8
    Answer: 8.67
  • Q: 1(e) Add the following: 6.02, 1.89
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and add place by place.
    Hundredths place: 2 + 9 = 11, write 1 and carry 1 to the tenths place.
    Tenths place: 0 + 8 + 1 carried = 9
    Ones place: 6 + 1 = 7
    Answer: 7.91
  • Q: 1(f) Add the following: 49.3, 21.6
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and add place by place.
    Tenths place: 3 + 6 = 9
    Ones place: 9 + 1 = 10, write 0 and carry 1 to the tens place.
    Tens place: 4 + 2 + 1 carried = 7
    Answer: 70.9
  • Q: 2(a) Solve the following: 4.91 - 3.92
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and subtract place by place, borrowing when needed.
    Hundredths place: 1 < 2, borrow 1 tenth: 11 - 2 = 9, tenths left 8.
    Tenths place: 8 < 9, borrow 1 one: 18 - 9 = 9, ones left 3.
    Ones place: 3 - 3 = 0
    Answer: 0.99
  • Q: 2(b) Solve the following: 7.34 - 2.86
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and subtract place by place, borrowing when needed.
    Hundredths place: 4 < 6, borrow 1 tenth: 14 - 6 = 8, tenths left 2.
    Tenths place: 2 < 8, borrow 1 one: 12 - 8 = 4, ones left 6.
    Ones place: 6 - 2 = 4
    Answer: 4.48
  • Q: 2(c) Solve the following: 5.06 - 2.76
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and subtract place by place, borrowing when needed.
    Hundredths place: 6 - 6 = 0
    Tenths place: 0 < 7, borrow 1 one: 10 - 7 = 3, ones left 4.
    Ones place: 4 - 2 = 2
    Answer: 2.30
  • Q: 2(d) Solve the following: 7.88 - 6.19
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and subtract place by place, borrowing when needed.
    Hundredths place: 8 < 9, borrow 1 tenth: 18 - 9 = 9, tenths left 7.
    Tenths place: 7 - 1 = 6
    Ones place: 7 - 6 = 1
    Answer: 1.69
  • Q: 2(e) Solve the following: 9.80 - 1.09
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and subtract place by place, borrowing when needed.
    Hundredths place: 0 < 9, borrow 1 tenth: 10 - 9 = 1, tenths left 7.
    Tenths place: 7 - 0 = 7
    Ones place: 9 - 1 = 8
    Answer: 8.71
  • Q: 2(f) Solve the following: 78.9 - 7.84
    Ans: Rule: first write 78.9 as 78.90 so both numbers have 2 decimal places, then subtract place by place.
    Hundredths place: 0 < 4, borrow 1 tenth: 10 - 4 = 6, tenths left 8.
    Tenths place: 8 - 8 = 0
    Ones place: 8 - 7 = 1
    Tens place: 7 - 0 = 7
    Answer: 71.06
  • Q: 3. Zubair bought chocolates for Rs. 45.7 and candies for Rs. 10.2. How much did he spend altogether?
    Ans: Rule: altogether means add; add place by place with decimal points in one column.
    Total spent = 45.7 + 10.2
    Tenths place: 7 + 2 = 9
    Ones place: 5 + 0 = 5
    Tens place: 4 + 1 = 5
    Answer: Rs. 55.9
  • Q: 4(a) The mass of apples is 38.9 kilograms and the mass of guavas is 42.6 kilograms. Find the difference between the mass of apples and guavas.
    Ans: Rule: difference means subtract the smaller mass from the greater mass, place by place.
    Difference = 42.6 - 38.9
    Tenths place: 6 < 9, borrow 1 one: 16 - 9 = 7, ones left 1.
    Ones place: 1 < 8, borrow 1 ten: 11 - 8 = 3, tens left 3.
    Tens place: 3 - 3 = 0
    Answer: 3.7 kilograms
  • Q: 4(b) The mass of apples is 38.9 kilograms and the mass of guavas is 42.6 kilograms. Find the total mass of fruit.
    Ans: Rule: total means add; add place by place with decimal points in one column.
    Total mass = 38.9 + 42.6
    Tenths place: 9 + 6 = 15, write 5 and carry 1 to the ones place.
    Ones place: 8 + 2 + 1 carried = 11, write 1 and carry 1 to the tens place.
    Tens place: 3 + 4 + 1 carried = 8
    Answer: 81.5 kilograms

lessons.title: Exercise 4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier.
  • multiply as whole numbers first, then put 1 decimal place in the product because the decimal number has 1 decimal place.
  • divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
  • total oil = oil for 1 cake x 10; multiplying by 10 moves the decimal point 1 place to the right.
  • total cloth = cloth for 1 shirt x 8; multiply as whole numbers, then put 1 decimal place in the product.
  • length of each piece = total length / number of pieces.
  • time for 1 question = total time / number of questions.

Exercise 4

  • Q: 1(a) Solve the following: 5.9 x 10
    Ans: Rule: to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier.
    10 has 1 zero, so move the point 1 place to the right.
    5.9 x 10 = 59
    Answer: 59
  • Q: 1(b) Solve the following: 4.8 x 100
    Ans: Rule: to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier.
    100 has 2 zeros, so move the point 2 places to the right and fill with 0.
    4.8 x 100 = 480
    Answer: 480
  • Q: 1(c) Solve the following: 0.3 x 1000
    Ans: Rule: to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier.
    1,000 has 3 zeros, so move the point 3 places to the right and fill with 0s.
    0.3 x 1000 = 300
    Answer: 300
  • Q: 1(d) Solve the following: 8.2 x 10
    Ans: Rule: to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier.
    10 has 1 zero, so move the point 1 place to the right.
    8.2 x 10 = 82
    Answer: 82
  • Q: 1(e) Solve the following: 4.3 x 1000
    Ans: Rule: to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier.
    1,000 has 3 zeros, so move the point 3 places to the right and fill with 0s.
    4.3 x 1000 = 4,300
    Answer: 4,300
  • Q: 1(f) Solve the following: 9.1 x 100
    Ans: Rule: to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier.
    100 has 2 zeros, so move the point 2 places to the right and fill with 0.
    9.1 x 100 = 910
    Answer: 910
  • Q: 2(a) Solve the following: 5.6 x 8
    Ans: Rule: multiply as whole numbers first, then put 1 decimal place in the product because the decimal number has 1 decimal place.
    5.6 = 56 tenths
    56 x 8 = 448
    448 tenths = 44.8
    Answer: 44.8
  • Q: 2(b) Solve the following: 7.1 x 2
    Ans: Rule: multiply as whole numbers first, then put 1 decimal place in the product because the decimal number has 1 decimal place.
    7.1 = 71 tenths
    71 x 2 = 142
    142 tenths = 14.2
    Answer: 14.2
  • Q: 2(c) Solve the following: 4.9 x 4
    Ans: Rule: multiply as whole numbers first, then put 1 decimal place in the product because the decimal number has 1 decimal place.
    4.9 = 49 tenths
    49 x 4 = 196
    196 tenths = 19.6
    Answer: 19.6
  • Q: 2(d) Solve the following: 3.4 x 3
    Ans: Rule: multiply as whole numbers first, then put 1 decimal place in the product because the decimal number has 1 decimal place.
    3.4 = 34 tenths
    34 x 3 = 102
    102 tenths = 10.2
    Answer: 10.2
  • Q: 2(e) Solve the following: 1.3 x 7
    Ans: Rule: multiply as whole numbers first, then put 1 decimal place in the product because the decimal number has 1 decimal place.
    1.3 = 13 tenths
    13 x 7 = 91
    91 tenths = 9.1
    Answer: 9.1
  • Q: 2(f) Solve the following: 9.8 x 9
    Ans: Rule: multiply as whole numbers first, then put 1 decimal place in the product because the decimal number has 1 decimal place.
    9.8 = 98 tenths
    98 x 9 = 882
    882 tenths = 88.2
    Answer: 88.2
  • Q: 3(a) Solve the following: 1.4 / 2 (divide 1.4 by 2)
    Ans: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
    1.4 = 14 tenths
    14 tenths / 2 = 7 tenths
    7 tenths = 0.7
    Answer: 0.7
  • Q: 3(b) Solve the following: 1.8 / 9 (divide 1.8 by 9)
    Ans: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
    1.8 = 18 tenths
    18 tenths / 9 = 2 tenths
    2 tenths = 0.2
    Answer: 0.2
  • Q: 3(c) Solve the following: 6.4 / 4 (divide 6.4 by 4)
    Ans: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
    6.4 = 64 tenths
    64 tenths / 4 = 16 tenths
    16 tenths = 1.6
    Answer: 1.6
  • Q: 3(d) Solve the following: 8.4 / 6 (divide 8.4 by 6)
    Ans: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
    8.4 = 84 tenths
    84 tenths / 6 = 14 tenths
    14 tenths = 1.4
    Answer: 1.4
  • Q: 3(e) Solve the following: 2.7 / 3 (divide 2.7 by 3)
    Ans: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
    2.7 = 27 tenths
    27 tenths / 3 = 9 tenths
    9 tenths = 0.9
    Answer: 0.9
  • Q: 3(f) Solve the following: 2.6 / 2 (divide 2.6 by 2)
    Ans: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
    2.6 = 26 tenths
    26 tenths / 2 = 13 tenths
    13 tenths = 1.3
    Answer: 1.3
  • Q: 4. Saba uses 9.8 ml of oil to bake a cake. How much oil will she use to bake 10 such cakes?
    Ans: Rule: total oil = oil for 1 cake x 10; multiplying by 10 moves the decimal point 1 place to the right.
    Oil for 10 cakes = 9.8 x 10
    9.8 x 10 = 98
    Answer: 98 ml
  • Q: 5. A tailor uses 2.5 m of cloth to make a shirt. How much cloth will he use to make 8 such shirts?
    Ans: Rule: total cloth = cloth for 1 shirt x 8; multiply as whole numbers, then put 1 decimal place in the product.
    Cloth = 2.5 x 8
    2.5 = 25 tenths
    25 x 8 = 200 tenths
    200 tenths = 20.0 m
    Answer: 20 m
  • Q: 6(a) The length of one piece of rope is 7.2 m. Iram cuts this rope into 4 equal pieces. What will be the length of each piece?
    Ans: Rule: length of each piece = total length / number of pieces.
    Length of each piece = 7.2 / 4
    7.2 = 72 tenths
    72 tenths / 4 = 18 tenths
    18 tenths = 1.8 m
    Answer: 1.8 m
  • Q: 6(b) The length of one piece of rope is 7.2 m. If Iram cuts the rope in 2 equal pieces, what will be the length of each piece?
    Ans: Rule: length of each piece = total length / number of pieces.
    Length of each piece = 7.2 / 2
    7.2 = 72 tenths
    72 tenths / 2 = 36 tenths
    36 tenths = 3.6 m
    Answer: 3.6 m
  • Q: 7. Ahmad solves 5 questions of math in 8.5 minutes. How long does he take to solve 1 question?
    Ans: Rule: time for 1 question = total time / number of questions.
    Time for 1 question = 8.5 / 5
    8.5 = 85 tenths
    85 tenths / 5 = 17 tenths
    17 tenths = 1.7 minutes
    Answer: 1.7 minutes

mcqs.q: Solve the following: 4.8 x 100
mcqs.why: Rule: to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier. 100 has 2 zeros, so move the point 2 places to the right and fill with 0. 4.8 x 100 = 480. Answer: 480

mcqs.q: Solve the following: 0.3 x 1000
mcqs.why: Rule: to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier. 1,000 has 3 zeros, so move the point 3 places to the right and fill with 0s. 0.3 x 1000 = 300. Answer: 300

mcqs.q: Solve the following: 4.3 x 1000
mcqs.why: Rule: to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier. 1,000 has 3 zeros, so move the point 3 places to the right and fill with 0s. 4.3 x 1000 = 4,300. Answer: 4,300

mcqs.q: Solve the following: 5.6 x 8
mcqs.why: Rule: multiply as whole numbers first, then put 1 decimal place in the product because the decimal number has 1 decimal place. 5.6 = 56 tenths. 56 x 8 = 448. 448 tenths = 44.8. Answer: 44.8

mcqs.q: Solve the following: 9.8 x 9
mcqs.why: Rule: multiply as whole numbers first, then put 1 decimal place in the product because the decimal number has 1 decimal place. 9.8 = 98 tenths. 98 x 9 = 882. 882 tenths = 88.2. Answer: 88.2

mcqs.q: Solve the following: 6.4 / 4 (divide 6.4 by 4)
mcqs.why: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals. 6.4 = 64 tenths. 64 tenths / 4 = 16 tenths. 16 tenths = 1.6. Answer: 1.6

mcqs.q: Solve the following: 2.7 / 3 (divide 2.7 by 3)
mcqs.why: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals. 2.7 = 27 tenths. 27 tenths / 3 = 9 tenths. 9 tenths = 0.9. Answer: 0.9

mcqs.q: Saba uses 9.8 ml of oil to bake a cake. How much oil will she use to bake 10 such cakes?
mcqs.why: Rule: total oil = oil for 1 cake x 10; multiplying by 10 moves the decimal point 1 place to the right. Oil for 10 cakes = 9.8 x 10. 9.8 x 10 = 98. Answer: 98 ml

mcqs.q: A tailor uses 2.5 m of cloth to make a shirt. How much cloth will he use to make 8 such shirts?
mcqs.why: Rule: total cloth = cloth for 1 shirt x 8; multiply as whole numbers, then put 1 decimal place in the product. Cloth = 2.5 x 8. 2.5 = 25 tenths. 25 x 8 = 200 tenths. 200 tenths = 20.0 m. Answer: 20 m

lessons.title: Exercise 5
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • look at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down, and write zeros in the places to the right.
  • look at the tenths digit; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down.

  • Q: 1(a) Round off the whole number 9,871 to the nearest 10, 100 and 1,000.
    Ans: Rule: look at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down, and write zeros in the places to the right.
    Nearest 10: ones digit is 1, less than 5, round down: 9,871 = 9,870
    Nearest 100: tens digit is 7, 5 or more, round up: 9,871 = 9,900
    Nearest 1,000: hundreds digit is 8, 5 or more, round up: 9,871 = 10,000
    Answer: nearest 10 = 9,870; nearest 100 = 9,900; nearest 1,000 = 10,000
  • Q: 1(b) Round off the whole number 5,467 to the nearest 10, 100 and 1,000.

    Nearest 100: tens digit is 6, 5 or more, round up: 5,467 = 5,500
    Nearest 1,000: hundreds digit is 4, less than 5, round down: 5,467 = 5,000
    Answer: nearest 10 = 5,470; nearest 100 = 5,500; nearest 1,000 = 5,000
  • Q: 1(c) Round off the whole number 1,212 to the nearest 10, 100 and 1,000.

lessons.title: Review Exercise — Part 1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • denominator 100 has 2 zeros, so put the decimal point 2 digits from the right.
  • if the denominator is not 10, 100 or 1,000, first make an equivalent fraction with denominator 1,000.
  • keep the whole part and write the decimal part over 10 for 1 decimal place.
  • keep the whole part and write the decimal part over 100 for 2 decimal places, then simplify.
  • write the same place values in one column and add place by place.
  • first write 12.8 as 12.80 so both numbers have 2 decimal places, then add place by place.
  • write the same place values in one column and subtract place by place.
  • to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier.

Review Exercise (Questions 1–25)

  • Q: 1(a) Encircle the correct answer: The decimal is a fraction with the denominator as _____, 100 or 1,000.
    Options: (a) 0   (b) 2   (c) 10   (d) 15
    Ans: 10
  • Q: 1(b) Encircle the correct answer: When we divide a shape into 10 equal parts, each part is called _____.
    Options: (a) hundredths   (b) tenths   (c) one   (d) half
    Ans: tenths
  • Q: 1(c) Encircle the correct answer: To add the decimals always _____ ones in ones, tenths in tenths and hundredths in hundredths.
    Options: (a) add   (b) subtract   (c) multiply   (d) divide
    Ans: add
  • Q: 1(d) Encircle the correct answer: When we multiply any decimal by 100, we move the decimal _____ place to the right.
    Options: (a) 1   (b) 2   (c) 3   (d) 0
    Ans: 2
  • Q: 1(e) Encircle the correct answer: _____ means to find such a number that is nearest to that number, but not exactly.
    Options: (a) Decimal   (b) Fraction   (c) Round off   (d) Estimation
    Ans: Estimation
  • Q: 2(a) Represent 17/100 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: denominator 100 has 2 zeros, so put the decimal point 2 digits from the right.
    17/100 = 0.17
    Answer: 0.17
  • Q: 2(b) Represent 15/200 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: if the denominator is not 10, 100 or 1,000, first make an equivalent fraction with denominator 1,000.
    15/200 = (15 x 5)/(200 x 5) = 75/1000
    75/1000 = 0.075
    Answer: 0.075
  • Q: 2(c) Represent 4/20 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: if the denominator is not 10, 100 or 1,000, first make an equivalent fraction with denominator 100.
    4/20 = (4 x 5)/(20 x 5) = 20/100
    20/100 = 0.2
    Answer: 0.2
  • Q: 2(d) Represent 19/100 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: denominator 100 has 2 zeros, so put the decimal point 2 digits from the right.
    19/100 = 0.19
    Answer: 0.19
  • Q: 2(e) Represent 200/250 in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: if the denominator is not 10, 100 or 1,000, first make an equivalent fraction with denominator 1,000.
    200/250 = (200 x 4)/(250 x 4) = 800/1000
    800/1000 = 0.800 = 0.8
    Answer: 0.8
  • Q: 3(a) Convert the decimal 6.7 to a common fraction.
    Ans: Rule: keep the whole part and write the decimal part over 10 for 1 decimal place.
    6.7 = 6 + 7/10
    Answer: 6 7/10
  • Q: 3(b) Convert the decimal 45.56 to a common fraction.
    Ans: Rule: keep the whole part and write the decimal part over 100 for 2 decimal places, then simplify.
    45.56 = 45 + 56/100
    Divide 56/100 by 4: 56/100 = 14/25
    Answer: 45 14/25
  • Q: 3(c) Convert the decimal 1.02 to a common fraction.
    Ans: Rule: keep the whole part and write the decimal part over 100 for 2 decimal places, then simplify.
    1.02 = 1 + 2/100
    Divide 2/100 by 2: 2/100 = 1/50
    Answer: 1 1/50
  • Q: 3(d) Convert the decimal 7.87 to a common fraction.
    Ans: Rule: keep the whole part and write the decimal part over 100 for 2 decimal places.
    7.87 = 7 + 87/100
    87/100 cannot be simplified.
    Answer: 7 87/100
  • Q: 3(e) Convert the decimal 15.8 to a common fraction.
    Ans: Rule: keep the whole part and write the decimal part over 10 for 1 decimal place, then simplify.
    15.8 = 15 + 8/10
    Divide 8/10 by 2: 8/10 = 4/5
    Answer: 15 4/5
  • Q: 4(a) Add the following: 6.03, 5.56
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and add place by place.
    Hundredths place: 3 + 6 = 9
    Tenths place: 0 + 5 = 5
    Ones place: 6 + 5 = 11, write 1 and carry 1 to the tens place.
    Tens place: 0 + 0 + 1 carried = 1
    Answer: 11.59
  • Q: 4(b) Add the following: 8.28, 1.24
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and add place by place.
    Hundredths place: 8 + 4 = 12, write 2 and carry 1 to the tenths place.
    Tenths place: 2 + 2 + 1 carried = 5
    Ones place: 8 + 1 = 9
    Answer: 9.52
  • Q: 4(c) Add the following: 12.8, 3.14
    Ans: Rule: first write 12.8 as 12.80 so both numbers have 2 decimal places, then add place by place.
    Hundredths place: 0 + 4 = 4
    Tenths place: 8 + 1 = 9
    Ones place: 2 + 3 = 5
    Tens place: 1 + 0 = 1
    Answer: 15.94
  • Q: 5(a) Solve the following: 7.59 - 2.48
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and subtract place by place.
    Hundredths place: 9 - 8 = 1
    Tenths place: 5 - 4 = 1
    Ones place: 7 - 2 = 5
    Answer: 5.11
  • Q: 5(b) Solve the following: 6.19 - 4.21
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and subtract place by place, borrowing when needed.
    Hundredths place: 9 - 1 = 8
    Tenths place: 1 < 2, borrow 1 one: 11 - 2 = 9, ones left 5.
    Ones place: 5 - 4 = 1
    Answer: 1.98
  • Q: 5(c) Solve the following: 5.06 - 1.09
    Ans: Rule: write the same place values in one column and subtract place by place, borrowing when needed.
    Hundredths place: 6 < 9; tenths has 0, so borrow 1 one into tenths (10 tenths), then borrow 1 tenth: 16 - 9 = 7, tenths left 9, ones left 4.
    Tenths place: 9 - 0 = 9
    Ones place: 4 - 1 = 3
    Answer: 3.97
  • Q: 6(a) Solve the following: 1.3 x 10
    Ans: Rule: to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier.
    10 has 1 zero, so move the point 1 place to the right.
    1.3 x 10 = 13
    Answer: 13
  • Q: 6(b) Solve the following: 8.9 x 100
    Ans: Rule: to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier.
    100 has 2 zeros, so move the point 2 places to the right and fill with 0.
    8.9 x 100 = 890
    Answer: 890
  • Q: 6(c) Solve the following: 4.5 x 1,000
    Ans: Rule: to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier.
    1,000 has 3 zeros, so move the point 3 places to the right and fill with 0s.
    4.5 x 1,000 = 4,500
    Answer: 4,500
  • Q: 6(d) Solve the following: 8.2 x 7
    Ans: Rule: multiply as whole numbers first, then put 1 decimal place in the product.
    8.2 = 82 tenths. 82 x 7 = 574 tenths = 57.4.
    Answer: 57.4

mcqs.q: Encircle the correct answer: The decimal is a fraction with the denominator as _____, 100 or 1,000.
mcqs.why: A decimal is a fraction whose denominator is 10, 100 or 1,000. This is the rule used in this lesson, for example 17/100 = 0.17 because denominator 100 has 2 zeros, so the decimal point is put 2 digits from the right.

mcqs.q: Encircle the correct answer: When we divide a shape into 10 equal parts, each part is called _____.
mcqs.why: When a shape is divided into 10 equal parts, each part is one part out of 10, written 1/10 = 0.1, and parts out of 10 are called tenths. Hundredths are parts when a shape is divided into 100 equal parts.

mcqs.q: Encircle the correct answer: To add the decimals always _____ ones in ones, tenths in tenths and hundredths in hundredths.
mcqs.why: To add decimals, the rule in this lesson is: write the same place values in one column and add place by place — ones in ones, tenths in tenths and hundredths in hundredths, for example 6.03 + 5.56 is added hundredths, then tenths, then ones.

mcqs.q: Encircle the correct answer: When we multiply any decimal by 100, we move the decimal _____ place to the right.
mcqs.why: Rule: to multiply a decimal by 10, 100 or 1,000, move the decimal point to the right by the number of zeros in the multiplier. 100 has 2 zeros, so the point moves 2 places to the right, for example 8.9 x 100 = 890.

mcqs.q: Encircle the correct answer: _____ means to find such a number that is nearest to that number, but not exactly.
mcqs.why: Estimation means to find a number that is nearest to the given number but not exactly equal to it — an approximate value. It is different from a decimal or a fraction, which name exact kinds of numbers.

mcqs.why: Rule: write the same place values in one column and add place by place. Hundredths place: 3 + 6 = 9. Tenths place: 0 + 5 = 5. Ones place: 6 + 5 = 11, write 1 and carry 1 to the tens place. Tens place: 0 + 0 + 1 carried = 1. Answer: 11.59

lessons.title: Review Exercise — Part 2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • multiply as whole numbers first, then put 1 decimal place in the product.
  • divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
  • look at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down, and write zeros in the places to the right.
  • look at the tenths digit; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down.
  • total length means add; add place by place with decimal points in one column.
  • difference means subtract the smaller length from the greater length, place by place.
  • total capacity = capacity of 1 pack x number of packs; multiply as whole numbers, then put 1 decimal place in the product.
  • mass of 1 box = total mass / number of boxes.

    Ans: Rule: multiply as whole numbers first, then put 1 decimal place in the product.

  • Q: 6(f) Solve the following: 7.1 x 6
    Ans: Rule: multiply as whole numbers first, then put 1 decimal place in the product.
    7.1 = 71 tenths. 71 x 6 = 426 tenths = 42.6.
    Answer: 42.6
  • Q: 7(a) Solve the following: 6.8 / 4 (divide 6.8 by 4)
    Ans: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
    6.8 = 68 tenths
    68 tenths / 4 = 17 tenths
    17 tenths = 1.7
    Answer: 1.7
  • Q: 7(b) Solve the following: 8.8 / 2 (divide 8.8 by 2)
    Ans: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
    8.8 = 88 tenths
    88 tenths / 2 = 44 tenths
    44 tenths = 4.4
    Answer: 4.4
  • Q: 7(c) Solve the following: 8.1 / 9 (divide 8.1 by 9)
    Ans: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
    8.1 = 81 tenths
    81 tenths / 9 = 9 tenths
    9 tenths = 0.9
    Answer: 0.9
  • Q: 7(d) Solve the following: 3.5 / 7 (divide 3.5 by 7)
    Ans: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
    3.5 = 35 tenths
    35 tenths / 7 = 5 tenths
    5 tenths = 0.5
    Answer: 0.5
  • Q: 7(e) Solve the following: 4.8 / 6 (divide 4.8 by 6)
    Ans: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
    4.8 = 48 tenths
    48 tenths / 6 = 8 tenths
    8 tenths = 0.8
    Answer: 0.8
  • Q: 7(f) Solve the following: 5.1 / 3 (divide 5.1 by 3)
    Ans: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
    5.1 = 51 tenths
    51 tenths / 3 = 17 tenths
    17 tenths = 1.7
    Answer: 1.7
  • Q: 8(a) Round off the whole number 3,429 to the nearest 10, 100 and 1,000.
    Ans: Rule: look at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down, and write zeros in the places to the right.
    Nearest 10: ones digit is 9, 5 or more, round up: 3,429 = 3,430
    Nearest 100: tens digit is 2, less than 5, round down: 3,429 = 3,400
    Nearest 1,000: hundreds digit is 4, less than 5, round down: 3,429 = 3,000
    Answer: nearest 10 = 3,430; nearest 100 = 3,400; nearest 1,000 = 3,000
  • Q: 8(b) Round off the whole number 1,009 to the nearest 10, 100 and 1,000.
    Ans: Rule: look at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down, and write zeros in the places to the right.
    Nearest 10: ones digit is 9, 5 or more, round up: 1,009 = 1,010
    Nearest 100: tens digit is 0, less than 5, round down: 1,009 = 1,000
    Nearest 1,000: hundreds digit is 0, less than 5, round down: 1,009 = 1,000
    Answer: nearest 10 = 1,010; nearest 100 = 1,000; nearest 1,000 = 1,000
  • Q: 8(c) Round off the whole number 7,824 to the nearest 10, 100 and 1,000.
    Ans: Rule: look at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down, and write zeros in the places to the right.
    Nearest 10: ones digit is 4, less than 5, round down: 7,824 = 7,820
    Nearest 100: tens digit is 2, less than 5, round down: 7,824 = 7,800
    Nearest 1,000: hundreds digit is 8, 5 or more, round up: 7,824 = 8,000
    Answer: nearest 10 = 7,820; nearest 100 = 7,800; nearest 1,000 = 8,000
  • Q: 8(d) Round off the whole number 8,417 to the nearest 10, 100 and 1,000.

    Nearest 10: ones digit is 7, 5 or more, round up: 8,417 = 8,420
    Nearest 100: tens digit is 1, less than 5, round down: 8,417 = 8,400
    Nearest 1,000: hundreds digit is 4, less than 5, round down: 8,417 = 8,000
    Answer: nearest 10 = 8,420; nearest 100 = 8,400; nearest 1,000 = 8,000
  • Q: 8(e) Round off the whole number 4,090 to the nearest 10, 100 and 1,000.
    Ans: Rule: look at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down, and write zeros in the places to the right.
    Nearest 10: ones digit is 0, less than 5, round down: 4,090 = 4,090
    Nearest 100: tens digit is 9, 5 or more, round up: 4,090 = 4,100
    Nearest 1,000: hundreds digit is 0, less than 5, round down: 4,090 = 4,000
    Answer: nearest 10 = 4,090; nearest 100 = 4,100; nearest 1,000 = 4,000
  • Q: 8(f) Round off the whole number 1,717 to the nearest 10, 100 and 1,000.
    Ans: Rule: look at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down, and write zeros in the places to the right.
    Nearest 10: ones digit is 7, 5 or more, round up: 1,717 = 1,720
    Nearest 100: tens digit is 1, less than 5, round down: 1,717 = 1,700
    Nearest 1,000: hundreds digit is 7, 5 or more, round up: 1,717 = 2,000
    Answer: nearest 10 = 1,720; nearest 100 = 1,700; nearest 1,000 = 2,000
  • Q: 9(a) Round off the decimal 4.17 to the nearest whole number.
    Ans: Rule: look at the tenths digit; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down.
    In 4.17, the tenths digit is 1, which is less than 5, so the whole part stays the same.
    4.17 = 4
    Answer: 4
  • Q: 9(b) Round off the decimal 78.3 to the nearest whole number.
    Ans: Rule: look at the tenths digit; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down.
    In 78.3, the tenths digit is 3, which is less than 5, so the whole part stays the same.
    78.3 = 78
    Answer: 78
  • Q: 9(c) Round off the decimal 13.45 to the nearest whole number.
    Ans: Rule: look at the tenths digit; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down.
    In 13.45, the tenths digit is 4, which is less than 5, so the whole part stays the same.
    13.45 = 13
    Answer: 13
  • Q: 9(d) Round off the decimal 0.98 to the nearest whole number.
    Ans: Rule: look at the tenths digit; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down.
    In 0.98, the tenths digit is 9, which is 5 or more, so add 1 to the ones digit: 0 + 1 = 1.
    0.98 = 1
    Answer: 1
  • Q: 9(e) Round off the decimal 41.41 to the nearest whole number.
    Ans: Rule: look at the tenths digit; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down.
    In 41.41, the tenths digit is 4, which is less than 5, so the whole part stays the same.
    41.41 = 41
    Answer: 41
  • Q: 9(f) Round off the decimal 9.82 to the nearest whole number.
    Ans: Rule: look at the tenths digit; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down.
    In 9.82, the tenths digit is 8, which is 5 or more, so add 1 to the ones digit: 9 + 1 = 10.
    9.82 = 10
    Answer: 10
  • Q: 10(a) The length of a wire is 3.41 metres and the length of another wire is 7.56 metres. What will be the total length of the wire?
    Ans: Rule: total length means add; add place by place with decimal points in one column.
    Total length = 3.41 + 7.56
    Hundredths place: 1 + 6 = 7
    Tenths place: 4 + 5 = 9
    Ones place: 3 + 7 = 10, write 0 and carry 1 to the tens place.
    Tens place: 0 + 0 + 1 carried = 1
    Answer: 10.97 metres
  • Q: 10(b) The length of a wire is 3.41 metres and the length of another wire is 7.56 metres. What is the difference between the lengths?
    Ans: Rule: difference means subtract the smaller length from the greater length, place by place.
    Difference = 7.56 - 3.41
    Hundredths place: 6 - 1 = 5
    Tenths place: 5 - 4 = 1
    Ones place: 7 - 3 = 4
    Answer: 4.15 metres
  • Q: 11(a) The capacity of a pack of juice is 3.4 litres. What is the capacity of such 7 packs?
    Ans: Rule: total capacity = capacity of 1 pack x number of packs; multiply as whole numbers, then put 1 decimal place in the product.
    Capacity of 7 packs = 3.4 x 7
    3.4 = 34 tenths
    34 x 7 = 238 tenths
    238 tenths = 23.8 litres
    Answer: 23.8 litres
  • Q: 11(b) If the capacity of a pack of juice is 2.8 litres, what will be the capacity of 5 packs?
    Ans: Rule: total capacity = capacity of 1 pack x number of packs; multiply as whole numbers, then put 1 decimal place in the product.
    Capacity of 5 packs = 2.8 x 5
    2.8 = 28 tenths
    28 x 5 = 140 tenths
    140 tenths = 14.0 litres
    Answer: 14 litres
  • Q: 12. The mass of 4 boxes of pencils is 1.8 kilogram. What will be the mass of 1 box?
    Ans: Rule: mass of 1 box = total mass / number of boxes.
    Mass of 1 box = 1.8 / 4
    1.8 = 18 tenths
    18 tenths / 4 = 4.5 tenths
    4.5 tenths = 0.45 kilogram
    Answer: 0.45 kilogram

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • a fraction with denominator 100 is written with 2 decimal places.
  • the hundredth part of a number is found by dividing the number by 100.
  • 1 kg = 1,000 g, so grams are written as thousandths of a kilogram.
  • the place value of a digit = digit x value of its place.
  • to convert a decimal to a fraction, keep the whole part and write the decimal part over 10, 100 or 1,000 according to its places.
  • read the places after the decimal point as tenths, then hundredths, and write the decimal over 100.
  • to add decimals, write the same place values in one column and add place by place.
  • to find a missing part, subtract the known part from the sum; subtract place by place, borrowing when needed.

Try Yourself (book p. 74)

  • Q: Ahmer solves 89 MCQs out of 100, in a test. Write it in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: a fraction with denominator 100 is written with 2 decimal places.
    89 out of 100 = 89/100
    Count 2 digits in the numerator from right to left and put the decimal point before them.
    89/100 = 0.89
    Answer: 0.89
  • Q: Write the hundredth part of one thousand in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: the hundredth part of a number is found by dividing the number by 100.
    Hundredth part of 1,000 = 1,000 / 100
    1,000 / 100 = 10
    In decimals, 10 is written as 10.0
    Answer: 10

Try Yourself (book p. 75)

  • Q: Write 4 kg 987 g in decimals and represent it in the place value chart.
    Ans: Rule: 1 kg = 1,000 g, so grams are written as thousandths of a kilogram.
    987 g = 987/1000 kg = 0.987 kg
    4 kg 987 g = 4 + 0.987 = 4.987 kg
    Place value chart: Ones = 4, Decimal Point = ., tenths = 9, hundredths = 8, thousandths = 7
    Answer: 4.987 kg

Try It! (book p. 76)

  • Q: Write the place value of each digit in 200.149 and express it in expanded form.
    Ans: Rule: the place value of a digit = digit x value of its place.
    2 is at hundreds place: 2 x 100 = 200
    0 is at tens place: 0 x 10 = 0
    0 is at ones place: 0 x 1 = 0
    1 is at tenths place: 1 x 0.1 = 0.1
    4 is at hundredths place: 4 x 0.01 = 0.04
    9 is at thousandths place: 9 x 0.001 = 0.009
    Expanded form: 200.149 = 200 + 0 + 0 + 1/10 + 4/100 + 9/1000
    200.149 = 200 + 0.1 + 0.04 + 0.009
    Answer: place values are 200, 0, 0, 0.1, 0.04 and 0.009; expanded form is 200 + 0.1 + 0.04 + 0.009

Try Yourself (book p. 78)

  • Q: About 95 out of 100 patients were recovering from the corona virus in Pakistan. Write it in decimals.
    Ans: Rule: a fraction with denominator 100 is written with 2 decimal places.
    95 out of 100 = 95/100
    Count 2 digits in the numerator from right to left and put the decimal point before them.
    95/100 = 0.95
    Answer: 0.95

Try Yourself (book p. 80)

  • Q: The highest temperature of Multan is 44.1 C. What will be this temperature in fraction form?
    Ans: Rule: to convert a decimal to a fraction, keep the whole part and write the decimal part over 10, 100 or 1,000 according to its places.
    44.1 = 44 ones + 1 tenth
    44.1 = 44 + 1/10
    44.1 = 441/10 = 44 1/10
    Answer: 44 1/10 C

Try It! (book p. 80)

  • Q: Show 7.74 in the place value chart and convert 7.74 into a fraction.
    Ans: Rule: read the places after the decimal point as tenths, then hundredths, and write the decimal over 100.
    Place value chart: Ones = 7, Decimal Point = ., tenths = 7, hundredths = 4
    7.74 = 7 + 7/10 + 4/100
    7.74 = 774/100
    Divide numerator and denominator by 2: 774/100 = 387/50
    387/50 = 7 37/50
    Answer: chart: 7 ones, 7 tenths, 4 hundredths; fraction = 7 37/50

Try Yourself (book p. 82)

  • Q: Ali has 2.98 kilograms of sugar and 1.09 kilograms of rice. What is the total amount of sugar and rice that he has?
    Ans: Rule: to add decimals, write the same place values in one column and add place by place.
    Hundredths place: 8 + 9 = 17, write 7 and carry 1 to the tenths place.
    Tenths place: 9 + 0 + 1 carried = 10, write 0 and carry 1 to the ones place.
    Ones place: 2 + 1 + 1 carried = 4
    2.98 + 1.09 = 4.07
    Answer: 4.07 kilograms

Try It! (book p. 83)

  • Q: If the sum of two decimals is 12.8 then find the first decimal fraction if the second decimal fraction is 7.9. What will we add in 12.8, so that we get 25.8?
    Ans: Rule: to find a missing part, subtract the known part from the sum; subtract place by place, borrowing when needed.
    First decimal = 12.8 - 7.9
    Tenths place: 8 < 9, borrow 1 one: 18 - 9 = 9, ones left 1.
    Ones place: 1 < 7, borrow 1 ten: 11 - 7 = 4, tens left 0.
    So the first decimal fraction is 4.9.
    Number to add = 25.8 - 12.8
    Tenths place: 8 - 8 = 0
    Ones place: 5 - 2 = 3
    Tens place: 2 - 1 = 1
    So we add 13.0.
    Answer: the first decimal fraction is 4.9, and 13.0 is added to 12.8 to get 25.8

Try Yourself (book p. 83)

  • Q: Sara has two ribbons. The length of a ribbon is 42.9 centimetres and the length of the other is 56.8 centimetres. What is the difference between their length?
    Ans: Rule: to find the difference, subtract the smaller decimal from the greater decimal, place by place.
    Difference = 56.8 - 42.9
    Tenths place: 8 < 9, borrow 1 one: 18 - 9 = 9, ones left 5.
    Ones place: 5 - 2 = 3
    Tens place: 5 - 4 = 1
    56.8 - 42.9 = 13.9
    Answer: 13.9 centimetres

Try Yourself (book p. 85)

  • Q: A bus covers 8.5 km when it travels between two towns. It takes five rounds in a day. How many kilometers does it travel?
    Ans: Rule: total distance = distance of one round x number of rounds; multiply as whole numbers, then give the product the same number of decimal places.
    Distance = 8.5 x 5
    8.5 = 85 tenths
    85 x 5 = 425 tenths
    425 tenths = 42.5
    Answer: 42.5 kilometers

Try Yourself (book p. 86)

  • Q: Divide 2.8 by 4.
    Ans: Rule: divide the tenths by the whole number, then write the result in decimals.
    2.8 = 28 tenths
    28 tenths / 4 = 7 tenths
    7 tenths = 0.7
    Answer: 0.7

Try It! (book p. 87)

  • Q: Write decimals with one decimal place which, when divided by 4, will give 1.2, 0.2 and 0.4.
    Ans: Rule: to find the starting decimal, multiply each answer by 4 (the opposite of dividing by 4).
    1.2 x 4: 12 tenths x 4 = 48 tenths = 4.8. Check: 4.8 / 4 = 1.2
    0.2 x 4: 2 tenths x 4 = 8 tenths = 0.8. Check: 0.8 / 4 = 0.2
    0.4 x 4: 4 tenths x 4 = 16 tenths = 1.6. Check: 1.6 / 4 = 0.4
    Answer: 4.8, 0.8 and 1.6

Try Yourself (book p. 88)

  • Q: Write 6,789 by rounding off to the nearest 10, 100 and 1,000.
    Ans: Rule: look at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to; if it is 5 or more, round up, and if it is less than 5, round down.
    Nearest 10: the ones digit is 9, which is more than 5, so round the tens digit 8 up to 9: 6,789 = 6,790
    Nearest 100: the tens digit is 8, which is more than 5, so round the hundreds digit 7 up to 8: 6,789 = 6,800
    Nearest 1,000: the hundreds digit is 7, which is more than 5, so round the thousands digit 6 up to 7: 6,789 = 7,000
    Answer: nearest 10 = 6,790; nearest 100 = 6,800; nearest 1,000 = 7,000

Try It! (book p. 90)

  • Q: Write 3 decimals that can be rounded off to 68.
    Ans: Rule: a decimal rounds to 68 if its tenths digit makes the ones stay 68 or make 67 round up: tenths digit less than 5 keeps the whole part, and 67 with tenths digit 5 or more rounds up to 68. (Many answers are possible.)
    67.7: tenths digit 7 is 5 or more, so 67 rounds up to 68.
    68.2: tenths digit 2 is less than 5, so it stays 68.
    68.4: tenths digit 4 is less than 5, so it stays 68.
    Answer: 67.7, 68.2 and 68.4 (many answers are possible)

Try It! (book p. 90)

  • Q: Write pairs of 3-digit decimals up to 2-decimal places whose product is 1, 2 and 3 respectively. Verify your answer.
    Ans: Rule: multiply as whole numbers, then put in the product as many decimal places as both numbers have together (2 + 2 = 4 decimal places). (Many answers are possible.)
    Product 1: 1.25 x 0.80. 125 x 80 = 10,000, so 1.25 x 0.80 = 1.0000 = 1. Verified.
    Product 2: 2.50 x 0.80. 250 x 80 = 20,000, so 2.50 x 0.80 = 2.0000 = 2. Verified.
    Product 3: 3.75 x 0.80. 375 x 80 = 30,000, so 3.75 x 0.80 = 3.0000 = 3. Verified.
    Answer: 1.25 x 0.80 = 1; 2.50 x 0.80 = 2; 3.75 x 0.80 = 3 (many answers are possible)

lessons.title: Exercise 1
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 1

  • Q: 1a) Circle the correct unit of length for a pencil: m / cm
    Ans: A pencil is a short object.
    Short objects are measured in centimetres.
    Answer: cm
  • Q: 1b) Circle the correct unit of length for an ant: mm / cm
    Ans: The length of an ant is measured in centimetres.
    Answer: cm
  • Q: 1c) Circle the correct unit of length for a school building: m / cm
    Ans: A school building is a long object.
    Long objects are measured in metres.
    Answer: m
  • Q: 1d) Circle the correct unit of length for a road: m / km
    Ans: A road covers a long distance between places.
    Distances between places are measured in kilometres.
    Answer: km
  • Q: 2a) Convert 12 km into m.
    Ans: 1 km = 1000 m
    12 km = 12 x 1000 m
    12 x 1000 = 12000
    Answer: 12000 m
    Note: The printed answer key gives 1200 m, which is incorrect.
  • Q: 2b) Convert 56 km 930 m into m.
    Ans: 1 km = 1000 m
    56 km 930 m = 56 km + 930 m
    = 56 x 1000 m + 930 m
    = 56000 m + 930 m
    = 56930 m
    Answer: 56930 m
  • Q: 2c) Convert 88 m into cm.
    Ans: 1 m = 100 cm
    88 m = 88 x 100 cm
    88 x 100 = 8800
    Answer: 8800 cm
  • Q: 2d) Convert 60 m 78 cm into cm.
    Ans: 1 m = 100 cm
    60 m 78 cm = 60 m + 78 cm
    = 60 x 100 cm + 78 cm
    = 6000 cm + 78 cm
    = 6078 cm
    Answer: 6078 cm
  • Q: 2e) Convert 3.2 cm into mm.
    Ans: 1 cm = 10 mm
    3.2 cm = 3.2 x 10 mm
    3.2 x 10 = 32
    Answer: 32 mm
  • Q: 2f) Convert 55 cm 2 mm into mm.
    Ans: 1 cm = 10 mm
    55 cm 2 mm = 55 cm + 2 mm
    = 55 x 10 mm + 2 mm
    = 550 mm + 2 mm
    = 552 mm
    Answer: 552 mm

lessons.title: Exercise 2
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 2

  • Q: 1a) Solve: 22 km + 33 km
    Ans: Add the same units: kilometres with kilometres.
    22 km + 33 km = 55 km
    Answer: 55 km
  • Q: 1b) Solve: 88 km + 6 km 17 m
    Ans: Add kilometres with kilometres and metres with metres.
    Kilometres: 88 km + 6 km = 94 km
    Metres: 0 m + 17 m = 17 m
    Answer: 94 km 17 m
  • Q: 1c) Solve: 82 m + 22 m
    Ans: Add the same units: metres with metres.
    82 m + 22 m = 104 m
    Answer: 104 m
  • Q: 1d) Solve: 71 cm 2 mm + 11 cm 6 mm

  • Q: 5a) Kamal covers a distance of 2 km 712 m going from his school to his house. He covers a distance of 1 km 216 m from his house to the masjid. Find the difference between the two distances.

  • Q: 5b) Kamal covers a distance of 2 km 712 m going from his school to his house. He covers a distance of 1 km 216 m from his house to the masjid. Convert the difference between the two distances into metres.
    Ans: From part (a), the difference is 1 km 496 m.

  • Q: 6a) The length of Ahmad's room is 12 m 56 cm. His sister's room is 10 m 44 cm long. What will be the total length of both rooms in cm?

    Centimetres: 56 cm - 44 cm = 12 cm
    Answer: 2 m 12 cm

Exercise 4

  • Q: 1a) Solve: 34 h 11 min 13 sec + 11 h 18 min 32 sec
    Ans: Add hours with hours, minutes with minutes and seconds with seconds, starting from the smaller unit.
