  • Q: 2a) Solve: 45 h 45 min 49 sec - 10 h 23 min 38 sec
    Ans: Subtract hours from hours, minutes from minutes and seconds from seconds, starting from the smaller unit.
    Seconds: 49 sec - 38 sec = 11 sec
    Minutes: 45 min - 23 min = 22 min
    Hours: 45 h - 10 h = 35 h
    Answer: 35 h 22 min 11 sec
  • Q: 2b) Solve: 57 h 22 min 27 sec - 33 h 11 min 12 sec
    Ans: Subtract hours from hours, minutes from minutes and seconds from seconds.
    Seconds: 27 sec - 12 sec = 15 sec
    Minutes: 22 min - 11 min = 11 min
    Hours: 57 h - 33 h = 24 h
    Answer: 24 h 11 min 15 sec
  • Q: 2c) Solve: 65 h 28 min 56 sec - 54 h 20 min 45 sec
    Ans: Subtract hours from hours, minutes from minutes and seconds from seconds.
    Seconds: 56 sec - 45 sec = 11 sec
    Minutes: 28 min - 20 min = 8 min
    Hours: 65 h - 54 h = 11 h
    Answer: 11 h 8 min 11 sec
  • Q: 2d) Solve: 6 h 26 min 42 sec - 5 h 15 min 31 sec
    Ans: Subtract hours from hours, minutes from minutes and seconds from seconds.
    Seconds: 42 sec - 31 sec = 11 sec

    Hours: 6 h - 5 h = 1 h

  • Q: 2e) Solve: 25 years 8 months 3 days - 23 years 6 months 1 day
    Ans: Subtract years from years, months from months and days from days.
    Days: 3 days - 1 day = 2 days
    Months: 8 months - 6 months = 2 months
    Years: 25 years - 23 years = 2 years
    Answer: 2 years 2 months 2 days
  • Q: 2f) Solve: 62 h 53 min 29 sec - 51 h 42 min 08 sec
    Ans: Subtract hours from hours, minutes from minutes and seconds from seconds.
    Seconds: 29 sec - 08 sec = 21 sec
    Minutes: 53 min - 42 min = 11 min
    Hours: 62 h - 51 h = 11 h
    Answer: 11 h 11 min 21 sec
  • Q: 3a) Ahmad went to his grand mother's home on Sunday. He stayed there for 2 hours and 20 minutes. On Monday, he went to his aunt's home and he spent 4 hours and 23 minutes there. How much time did he spend at his relative's home?
    Ans: Add hours with hours and minutes with minutes.
    Hours: 2 h + 4 h = 6 h
    Minutes: 20 min + 23 min = 43 min
    Total time = 6 h 43 min
    Answer: 6 h 43 min
    Note: The printed answer key gives 2 h 3 min, which is incorrect.
  • Q: 3b) Ahmad went to his grand mother's home on Sunday. He stayed there for 2 hours and 20 minutes. On Monday, he went to his aunt's home and he spent 4 hours and 23 minutes there. Write the time he spent at his relative's home in minutes.
    Ans: From part (a), the total time is 6 h 43 min.
    1 hour = 60 min
    6 h 43 min = 6 h + 43 min
    = 6 x 60 min + 43 min
    = 360 min + 43 min
    = 403 min
    Answer: 403 min
    Note: The printed answer key gives 123 min, which is incorrect.
  • Q: 4a) Ejaz travelled 6 hours 34 minutes 45 seconds in a bus and 4 hours 20 minutes 12 seconds in a train. How much more time did he travel in the bus than the train?

mcqs.q: Encircle the correct option: In the 12 hours format, 13:50 hours can be written as:
mcqs.why: 13:50 hours is after 12 noon, so it is p.m. time. Subtract 12 from the hours: 13 - 12 = 1. So 13:50 hours can be written as 1:50 p.m. Answer: 1:50 p.m

mcqs.q: Encircle the correct option: In the 24 hours format, 3:55 p.m can be written as:
mcqs.why: 3:55 p.m is after 12 noon. To write p.m. time in the 24 hours format, add 12 to the hours: 3 + 12 = 15. So 3:55 p.m can be written as 15:55. Answer: 15:55

mcqs.q: Encircle the correct option: Which is the longest time?
mcqs.why: 1 year = 12 months, so 2 years = 2 x 12 = 24 months. 1 year 3 months = 12 + 3 = 15 months, which is less than 24 months. 12 months and 350 days are also less than 2 years. So the longest time is 2 years.

mcqs.q: Encircle the correct option: There are _____ months in 2 years, 6 months.
mcqs.why: 1 year = 12 months. 2 years = 2 x 12 months = 24 months. 24 months + 6 months = 30 months. So there are 30 months in 2 years, 6 months.

mcqs.q: Encircle the correct option: To convert years into months, we multiply the given years by _____.
mcqs.why: There are 12 months in 1 year, as shown in this lesson's conversions such as 2 years = 24 months. So to convert years into months, we multiply the given years by 12.

    Ans: Add hours with hours, minutes with minutes and seconds with seconds.
    Seconds: 38 sec + 06 sec = 44 sec
    Minutes: 25 min + 34 min = 59 min
    Hours: 44 h + 32 h = 76 h
    Answer: 76 h 59 min 44 sec
  • Q: 7c) Solve: 6 h 25 min 35 sec + 3 h 13 min 14 sec
    Ans: Add hours with hours, minutes with minutes and seconds with seconds.
    Seconds: 35 sec + 14 sec = 49 sec
    Minutes: 25 min + 13 min = 38 min
    Hours: 6 h + 3 h = 9 h
    Answer: 9 h 38 min 49 sec
  • Q: 8a) Solve: 38 h 33 min 38 sec - 00 h 22 min 26 sec
    Ans: Subtract hours from hours, minutes from minutes and seconds from seconds.
    Seconds: 38 sec - 26 sec = 12 sec
    Minutes: 33 min - 22 min = 11 min
    Hours: 38 h - 00 h = 38 h
    Answer: 38 h 11 min 12 sec
  • Q: 8b) Solve: 56 h 56 min 58 sec - 44 h 43 min 37 sec
    Ans: Subtract hours from hours, minutes from minutes and seconds from seconds.
    Seconds: 58 sec - 37 sec = 21 sec
    Minutes: 56 min - 43 min = 13 min
    Hours: 56 h - 44 h = 12 h
    Answer: 12 h 13 min 21 sec
  • Q: 8c) Solve: 37 h 54 min 49 sec - 21 h 32 min 00 sec
    Ans: Subtract hours from hours, minutes from minutes and seconds from seconds.
    Seconds: 49 sec - 00 sec = 49 sec
    Minutes: 54 min - 32 min = 22 min
    Hours: 37 h - 21 h = 16 h
    Answer: 16 h 22 min 49 sec
  • Q: 9a) Afnan spends 5 hours 23 minutes in studying, and 1 hour 20 minutes playing. How much time does he spend in both activities?
    Ans: Add hours with hours and minutes with minutes.
    Hours: 5 h + 1 h = 6 h
    Minutes: 23 min + 20 min = 43 min
    Answer: 6 h 43 min
  • Q: 9b) Afnan spends 5 hours 23 minutes in studying, and 1 hour 20 minutes playing. Write the total time in minutes.
    Ans: From part (a), the total time is 6 h 43 min.
    1 hour = 60 min
    6 h 43 min = 6 h + 43 min
    = 6 x 60 min + 43 min
    = 360 min + 43 min
    = 403 min
    Answer: 403 min
  • Q: 10) It takes a cook 2 hours 43 minutes 54 second to make a savoury dish and one hour 12 minutes 24 seconds to make a desert. How much more time does he take to make the savoury dish?
    Ans: Subtract hours from hours, minutes from minutes and seconds from seconds.
    Seconds: 54 sec - 24 sec = 30 sec
    Minutes: 43 min - 12 min = 31 min
    Hours: 2 h - 1 h = 1 h
    Answer: 1 h 31 min 30 sec
  • Q: 11a) Asfand Yar lives in Pakistan. He spends 7 years 4 months 2 days in Saudi Arabia, and 2 years 7 months 7 days in the United Arab Emirates. How much time does he spend out of Pakistan?
    Ans: Add years with years, months with months and days with days.
    Days: 2 days + 7 days = 9 days
    Months: 4 months + 7 months = 11 months
    Years: 7 years + 2 years = 9 years
    Answer: 9 years 11 months 9 days
  • Q: 11b) Asfand Yar lives in Pakistan. He spends 7 years 4 months 2 days in Saudi Arabia, and 2 years 7 months 7 days in the United Arab Emirates. Write the total time he spends out of Pakistan in days.
    Ans: From part (a), the total time is 9 years 11 months 9 days.
    1 year = 12 months
    9 years 11 months = 9 x 12 months + 11 months = 108 months + 11 months = 119 months
    1 month = 30 days
    119 months 9 days = 119 x 30 days + 9 days = 3570 days + 9 days = 3579 days
    Answer: 3579 days
  • Q: 12) Farheen completes her medical in 4 years 10 months 7 days, and her house job in 2 years 2 days. How much time did she spend in her medical education and house job, altogether?
    Ans: 2 years 2 days = 2 years 0 months 2 days.
    Add years with years, months with months and days with days.
    Days: 7 days + 2 days = 9 days
    Months: 10 months + 0 months = 10 months
    Years: 4 years + 2 years = 6 years
    Answer: 6 years 10 months 9 days

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Try Yourself (book p. 116)

  • Q: Write 5 a.m and 5 p.m in 12-hours and 24-hours format.
    Ans: In the 12-hour clock, a.m is used after 12 midnight and p.m is used after 12 noon.
    In the 24-hour clock, p.m hours are counted by adding 12.
    5 a.m in 12-hours format = 5:00 a.m
    5 a.m in 24-hours format = 05:00 hours
    5 p.m in 12-hours format = 5:00 p.m
    5 + 12 = 17, so 5 p.m in 24-hours format = 17:00 hours
    Answer: 5 a.m = 5:00 a.m = 05:00 hours; 5 p.m = 5:00 p.m = 17:00 hours

Try Yourself (book p. 120)

  • Q: Convert 5 hours, 5 min into minutes.
    Ans: 1 hour = 60 min
    5 hours, 5 min = 5 h + 5 min
    = 5 x 60 min + 5 min
    = 300 min + 5 min
    = 305 min
    Answer: 305 min

Try It! (book p. 120)

  • Q: How many seconds are there in one day?
    Ans: 1 day = 24 hours
    1 hour = 60 min
    24 hours = 24 x 60 min = 1440 min
    1 min = 60 sec
    1440 min = 1440 x 60 sec = 86400 sec
    Answer: 86400 sec

Try Yourself (book p. 122)

  • Q: Convert 10 months, 22 days to days.
    Ans: 1 month = 30 days
    10 months 22 days = 10 months + 22 days
    = 10 x 30 days + 22 days
    = 300 days + 22 days
    = 322 days
    Answer: 322 days

Try It! (book p. 123)

  • Q: How many weeks are there in 4 years? How many days are there in 12 years?
    Ans: 1 year = 52 weeks
    4 years = 4 x 52 weeks = 208 weeks
    1 year = 12 months and 1 month = 30 days, so 1 year = 12 x 30 days = 360 days
    12 years = 12 x 360 days = 4320 days
    Answer: 208 weeks in 4 years; 4320 days in 12 years

lessons.title: Exercise 1 and 2 — Lines and Angles
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 1

  • Q: 1. Identify parallel and non-parallel lines from the given lines and write their names as well. a) Two horizontal lines, one above the other, both pointing left and right.
    Ans: The two lines never meet each other and the distance between them remains the same.
    Answer: Parallel lines.
  • Q: 1. Identify parallel and non-parallel lines from the given lines and write their names as well. b) Two lines crossing each other, one horizontal and one almost vertical.
    Ans: The two lines intersect each other at a point.
    Lines which intersect each other at some point are called non-parallel lines.
    Answer: Non-parallel lines.
  • Q: 1. Identify parallel and non-parallel lines from the given lines and write their names as well. c) Two vertical lines standing side by side, both pointing up and down.
    Ans: The two lines never meet each other and the distance between them remains the same.
    Answer: Parallel lines.
  • Q: 1. Identify parallel and non-parallel lines from the given lines and write their names as well. d) Two lines crossing each other like the letter X.
    Ans: The two lines intersect each other at a point.
    Lines which intersect each other at some point are called non-parallel lines.
    Answer: Non-parallel lines.
  • Q: 1. Identify parallel and non-parallel lines from the given lines and write their names as well. e) Two slanting lines leaning to the right, side by side in the same direction.
    Ans: The two lines never meet each other and the distance between them remains the same.
    Answer: Parallel lines.
  • Q: 1. Identify parallel and non-parallel lines from the given lines and write their names as well. f) Two lines crossing each other like a flat X.
    Ans: The two lines intersect each other at a point.
    Lines which intersect each other at some point are called non-parallel lines.
    Answer: Non-parallel lines.

Exercise 2

  • Q: 1. Write the names and types of angles in the following. a) Angle ABC, with vertex B, one ray going to C on the right and the other ray going up to A.
    Ans: The vertex is B, so the angle is named angle ABC.
    The angle is smaller than a right angle (less than 90 degrees).
    Answer: Angle ABC is an acute angle.
  • Q: 1. Write the names and types of angles in the following. b) Angle DEF, with vertex E, one ray going to D on the right and the other ray going down to F, marked with a small square at E.
    Ans: The vertex is E, so the angle is named angle DEF.
    The small square shows that the angle measures 90 degrees.
    Answer: Angle DEF is a right angle.
  • Q: 1. Write the names and types of angles in the following. c) Angle GHI, with vertex H, one ray going to I on the right and the other ray going up to the left to G, with a wide shaded sector at H.
    Ans: The vertex is H, so the angle is named angle GHI.
    The angle is greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees.
    Answer: Angle GHI is an obtuse angle.
  • Q: 1. Write the names and types of angles in the following. d) Angle JKL, with vertex K, one ray going to L on the right and the other ray going up to J.
    Ans: The vertex is K, so the angle is named angle JKL.
    The angle is smaller than a right angle (less than 90 degrees).
    Answer: Angle JKL is an acute angle.
  • Q: 2. Measure the following angles. Angle ABC, with vertex B, ray BC going to the right and ray BA going up to the right.
    Ans: Place the centre point of the protractor on vertex B.
    Place the baseline of the protractor exactly on ray BC.
    Read the inner scale where ray BA crosses it.
    The angle measures 60 degrees, which is less than 90 degrees.
    Answer: Angle ABC = 60 degrees, an acute angle.
  • Q: 2. Measure the following angles. Angle EFG, with vertex F, ray FG going to the right and ray FE going up to the right at a small height.
    Ans: Place the centre point of the protractor on vertex F.
    Place the baseline of the protractor exactly on ray FG.
    Read the inner scale where ray FE crosses it.
    The angle measures 30 degrees, which is less than 90 degrees.
    Answer: Angle EFG = 30 degrees, an acute angle.
  • Q: 2. Measure the following angles. Angle IJK, with vertex J, ray JK going to the right and ray JI going up to the left.
    Ans: Place the centre point of the protractor on vertex J.
    Place the baseline of the protractor exactly on ray JK.
    Read the scale where ray JI crosses it.
    The angle measures 120 degrees, which is greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees.
    Answer: Angle IJK = 120 degrees, an obtuse angle.
  • Q: 2. Measure the following angles. Angle MNO, with vertex N, ray NO going to the right and ray NM going straight up.
    Ans: Place the centre point of the protractor on vertex N.
    Place the baseline of the protractor exactly on ray NO.
    Read the scale where ray NM crosses it.
    The angle measures 90 degrees.
    Answer: Angle MNO = 90 degrees, a right angle.
  • Q: 2. Measure the following angles. Angle PQR, with vertex Q, ray QR going to the right and ray QP going up to the right at a very small height.
    Ans: Place the centre point of the protractor on vertex Q.
    Place the baseline of the protractor exactly on ray QR.
    Read the inner scale where ray QP crosses it.
    The angle measures 20 degrees, which is less than 90 degrees.
    Answer: Angle PQR = 20 degrees, an acute angle.
  • Q: 3. Construct the angles of the given measurements. a) 60 degrees
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A horizontal ray with its vertex at the left end, and a second ray rising from the vertex up to the right; the angle between the two rays is marked with an arc and labelled 60 degrees.
    Step 1: Draw a ray with the help of a ruler.
    Step 2: Place the centre point of the protractor on the vertex and the baseline exactly on the ray.
    Step 3: Mark a point at 60 degrees on the scale.
    Step 4: Remove the protractor and join the vertex to the marked point.
    Answer: An angle of 60 degrees is constructed.
  • Q: 3. Construct the angles of the given measurements. b) 30 degrees
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A horizontal ray with its vertex at the left end, and a second ray rising gently from the vertex up to the right; the angle between the two rays is marked with an arc and labelled 30 degrees.
    Step 1: Draw a ray with the help of a ruler.
    Step 2: Place the centre point of the protractor on the vertex and the baseline exactly on the ray.
    Step 3: Mark a point at 30 degrees on the scale.
    Step 4: Remove the protractor and join the vertex to the marked point.
    Answer: An angle of 30 degrees is constructed.
  • Q: 3. Construct the angles of the given measurements. c) 115 degrees
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A horizontal ray with its vertex at the left end, and a second ray rising from the vertex up to the left; the wide angle between the two rays is marked with an arc and labelled 115 degrees.
    Step 1: Draw a ray with the help of a ruler.
    Step 2: Place the centre point of the protractor on the vertex and the baseline exactly on the ray.
    Step 3: Mark a point at 115 degrees on the scale.
    Step 4: Remove the protractor and join the vertex to the marked point.
    Answer: An angle of 115 degrees is constructed.
  • Q: 3. Construct the angles of the given measurements. d) 90 degrees
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A horizontal ray with its vertex at the left end, and a second ray rising straight up from the vertex; the angle between the two rays is marked with a small square and labelled 90 degrees.
    Step 1: Draw a ray with the help of a ruler.
    Step 2: Place the centre point of the protractor on the vertex and the baseline exactly on the ray.
    Step 3: Mark a point at 90 degrees on the scale.
    Step 4: Remove the protractor and join the vertex to the marked point.
    Answer: An angle of 90 degrees (a right angle) is constructed.
  • Q: 4. Measure the angles in the following figures and write their names as well. First figure: a blue square divided by a diagonal line from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner, with yellow marks at the top-left corner, at the top-right corner between the top side and the diagonal, in the middle on the diagonal, at the bottom-left corner, and at the bottom-right corner.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A square with corners top-left, top-right, bottom-right and bottom-left; a diagonal joins the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner; yellow angle marks are shown at all four corners and at the middle of the diagonal.
    All angles of a square are right angles, so each corner measures 90 degrees.
    The diagonal of a square divides each corner angle into two equal parts: 90 degrees / 2 = 45 degrees.
    At the top-left corner: 90 degrees, a right angle.
    At the top-right corner, between the top side and the diagonal: 45 degrees, an acute angle.
    At the middle of the diagonal: the diagonal is a straight line, so the angle on it is 180 degrees, a straight angle.
    At the bottom-left corner: 90 degrees in total, a right angle, divided by the diagonal into 45 degrees + 45 degrees.
    At the bottom-right corner: 90 degrees, a right angle.
    Answer: Corner angles are 90 degrees (right angles), the angles made by the diagonal at the corners are 45 degrees (acute angles), and the angle on the diagonal is 180 degrees (a straight angle).
  • Q: 4. Measure the angles in the following figures and write their names as well. Second figure: a five-sided figure like an arrowhead pointing to the left, with a vertical side on the right, yellow marks at the left point, at the top corner, at the top-right corner, at the bottom corner, and at the bottom-right corner.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A pentagon with a point on the left, a vertical side on the right, and yellow angle marks at its five corners: the left point, the top corner, the top-right corner, the bottom corner and the bottom-right corner.
    Measure each angle with a protractor by placing the centre point on the corner and the baseline on one side.
    At the left point: about 60 degrees, an acute angle.
    At the top corner: about 150 degrees, an obtuse angle.
    At the top-right corner: 90 degrees, a right angle.
    At the bottom corner: about 150 degrees, an obtuse angle.
    At the bottom-right corner: 90 degrees, a right angle.
    Check: 60 + 150 + 90 + 150 + 90 = 540 degrees, which is the total of the inside angles of a five-sided figure.
    Answer: Acute angle about 60 degrees at the point, obtuse angles of about 150 degrees at the top and bottom corners, and right angles of 90 degrees at the two right corners.

mcqs.q: Two horizontal lines, one above the other, both pointing left and right. What kind of lines are they?
mcqs.why: The two lines never meet each other and the distance between them remains the same. Lines that never meet each other are parallel lines. Answer: Parallel lines.

mcqs.q: Two lines crossing each other like the letter X. What kind of lines are they?
options: Lines with the same distance between them
mcqs.why: The two lines intersect each other at a point. Lines which intersect each other at some point are called non-parallel lines. Answer: Non-parallel lines.

mcqs.q: Two vertical lines standing side by side, both pointing up and down, never meet each other. What kind of lines are they?
mcqs.why: The two lines never meet each other and the distance between them remains the same. That is the property of parallel lines. Answer: Parallel lines.

mcqs.q: Angle ABC, with vertex B, is smaller than a right angle (less than 90 degrees). What type of angle is it?
options: Angle ABC is a right angle
Angle ABC is an obtuse angle
Angle ABC is a straight angle
Angle ABC is an acute angle
mcqs.why: The vertex is B, so the angle is named angle ABC. The angle is smaller than a right angle (less than 90 degrees). An angle less than 90 degrees is an acute angle. Answer: Angle ABC is an acute angle.

mcqs.q: Angle DEF, with vertex E, is marked with a small square at E. What type of angle is it?
options: Angle DEF is a right angle
Angle DEF is an acute angle
Angle DEF is an obtuse angle
Angle DEF is a straight angle
mcqs.why: The vertex is E, so the angle is named angle DEF. The small square shows that the angle measures 90 degrees. An angle of 90 degrees is a right angle. Answer: Angle DEF is a right angle.

mcqs.q: Angle GHI, with vertex H, is greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees. What type of angle is it?
options: Angle GHI is an acute angle
Angle GHI is an obtuse angle
Angle GHI is a right angle
Angle GHI is a straight angle
mcqs.why: The vertex is H, so the angle is named angle GHI. The angle is greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees. Such an angle is an obtuse angle. Answer: Angle GHI is an obtuse angle.

mcqs.q: When measured with a protractor, angle ABC measures 60 degrees. What is angle ABC?
options: Angle ABC = 60 degrees, a right angle
Angle ABC = 60 degrees, an obtuse angle
Angle ABC = 60 degrees, an acute angle
Angle ABC = 90 degrees, a right angle
mcqs.why: Place the centre point of the protractor on vertex B. Place the baseline of the protractor exactly on ray BC. Read the inner scale where ray BA crosses it. The angle measures 60 degrees, which is less than 90 degrees. Answer: Angle ABC = 60 degrees, an acute angle.

mcqs.q: When measured with a protractor, angle IJK measures 120 degrees. What is angle IJK?
options: Angle IJK = 120 degrees, an acute angle
Angle IJK = 120 degrees, a right angle
Angle IJK = 90 degrees, a right angle
Angle IJK = 120 degrees, an obtuse angle
mcqs.why: Place the centre point of the protractor on vertex J. Place the baseline of the protractor exactly on ray JK. Read the scale where ray JI crosses it. The angle measures 120 degrees, which is greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees. Answer: Angle IJK = 120 degrees, an obtuse angle.

mcqs.q: When measured with a protractor, angle MNO measures 90 degrees. What is angle MNO?
options: Angle MNO = 90 degrees, a right angle
Angle MNO = 90 degrees, an acute angle
Angle MNO = 90 degrees, an obtuse angle
Angle MNO = 180 degrees, a straight angle
mcqs.why: Place the centre point of the protractor on vertex N. Place the baseline of the protractor exactly on ray NO. Read the scale where ray NM crosses it. The angle measures 90 degrees. Answer: Angle MNO = 90 degrees, a right angle.

mcqs.q: When measured with a protractor, angle EFG measures 30 degrees. What is angle EFG?
options: Angle EFG = 30 degrees, a right angle
Angle EFG = 30 degrees, an acute angle
Angle EFG = 30 degrees, an obtuse angle
Angle EFG = 90 degrees, a right angle
mcqs.why: Place the centre point of the protractor on vertex F. Place the baseline of the protractor exactly on ray FG. Read the inner scale where ray FE crosses it. The angle measures 30 degrees, which is less than 90 degrees. Answer: Angle EFG = 30 degrees, an acute angle.

lessons.title: Exercise 3 and 4 — Circles, Perimeter and Area
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 3

  • Q: 1. Draw the parts of the following circles. Draw the diameter of the circle (a plain circle is given).
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A circle with a dot marked at its middle labelled as the centre; a straight line segment joins two opposite points on the circle and passes through the centre; this segment is the diameter.
    Step 1: Mark the centre point in the middle of the circle.
    Step 2: With a ruler, draw a straight line from one point on the circle to the opposite point on the circle, passing through the centre.
    The line segment which joins any two points on a circle and passes through its centre is called the diameter.
    Answer: The line segment drawn through the centre, joining two points on the circle, is the diameter of the circle.
  • Q: 1. Draw the parts of the following circles. Draw the radius of the circle (a plain circle is given).
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A circle with a dot marked at its middle labelled as the centre; a straight line segment joins the centre to one point on the circle; this segment is the radius.
    Step 1: Mark the centre point in the middle of the circle.
    Step 2: With a ruler, draw a straight line from the centre to any point on the circle.
    The line segment which joins any point on the circle to its centre is called the radius of the circle.
    Answer: The line segment drawn from the centre to a point on the circle is the radius of the circle.
  • Q: 1. Draw the parts of the following circles. Draw the centre of the circle (a plain circle is given).
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A circle with a single dot marked exactly in its middle; the dot is the centre of the circle.
    The point in the centre of a circle, from which the distance of all the points of the circle is the same, is called the centre of the circle.
    Step 1: Find the middle point of the circle.
    Step 2: Mark a dot there; this dot is the centre.
    Answer: The dot marked in the middle of the circle is its centre.
  • Q: 2. Write the names of parts of the circles. a) A circle with centre R; a dotted line joins point P at the top-left of the circle to point Q at the bottom-right, passing through R; a dotted line joins R down to point S at the bottom of the circle. Write Centre, Diameter and Radius.
    Ans: The centre is the middle point of the circle, which is R.
    The line joining two points on the circle through the centre is the diameter, which is PQ.
    The lines joining the centre to points on the circle are radii: PR, RQ and RS.
    Answer: Centre: R, Diameter: PQ, Radius: PR, RQ, RS.
  • Q: 2. Write the names of parts of the circles. b) A circle with centre L; a dotted line joins point J at the bottom-left of the circle to point K at the top-right, passing through L. Write Centre, Diameter and Radius.
    Ans: The centre is the middle point of the circle, which is L.
    The line joining two points on the circle through the centre is the diameter, which is JK.
    The lines joining the centre to points on the circle are radii: LJ and LK.
    Answer: Centre: L, Diameter: JK, Radius: LJ, LK.
  • Q: 2. Write the names of parts of the circles. c) A circle with centre C; a dotted line joins point A on the left of the circle to point B on the right, passing through C; another dotted line joins C up to point D on the circle. Write Centre, Diameter and Radius.
    Ans: The centre is the middle point of the circle, which is C.
    The line joining two points on the circle through the centre is the diameter, which is AB.
    The lines joining the centre to points on the circle are radii: CD, AC and CB.
    Answer: Centre: C, Diameter: AB, Radius: CD, AC, CB.

Exercise 4

  • Q: 1. Find the perimeter of the shaded figures. a) A blue shaded square on a grid, 5 squares long and 5 squares wide, each small square having side 1 m.
    Ans: Perimeter = sum of the lengths of all sides
    The shaded figure is a square of side 5 m.
    Perimeter = 5 m + 5 m + 5 m + 5 m = 20 m.
    Answer: The perimeter is 20 m.
  • Q: 1. Find the perimeter of the shaded figures. b) A pink shaded rectangle on a grid, 7 squares long and 4 squares wide, each small square having side 1 cm.
    Ans: Perimeter = sum of the lengths of all sides
    Length = 7 cm and breadth = 4 cm.
    Perimeter = 7 cm + 4 cm + 7 cm + 4 cm = 22 cm.
    Answer: The perimeter is 22 cm.
  • Q: 1. Find the perimeter of the shaded figures. c) A pink shaded rectangle on a grid, 6 squares long and 4 squares wide, each small square having side 1 m.
    Ans: Perimeter = sum of the lengths of all sides
    Length = 6 m and breadth = 4 m.
    Perimeter = 6 m + 4 m + 6 m + 4 m = 20 m.
    Answer: The perimeter is 20 m.
  • Q: 2. Find the area of the shaded figures. a) A dark blue shaded rectangle on a grid, 4 squares long and 3 squares wide, each small square having side 1 cm.
    Ans: Area = number of square boxes covered
    Number of squares = 4 x 3 = 12.
    Each square has area 1 cm².
    Area = 12 x 1 cm² = 12 cm².
    Answer: The area is 12 cm².
    Note: The printed answer key gives 4 cm², which is incorrect.
  • Q: 2. Find the area of the shaded figures. b) A peach shaded rectangle on a grid, 12 squares long and 7 squares wide, each small square having side 1 m.
    Ans: Area = number of square boxes covered
    Number of squares = 12 x 7 = 84.
    Each square has area 1 m².
    Area = 84 x 1 m² = 84 m².
    Answer: The area is 84 m².
  • Q: 2. Find the area of the shaded figures. c) A green shaded rectangle on a grid, 4 squares long and 2 squares wide, each small square having side 1 cm.
    Ans: Area = number of square boxes covered
    Number of squares = 4 x 2 = 8.
    Each square has area 1 cm².
    Area = 8 x 1 cm² = 8 cm².
    Answer: The area is 8 cm².
  • Q: 2. Find the area of the shaded figures. d) A red shaded figure on a grid shaped like a tower: the top part is 2 squares wide and 2 squares high, and below it are 2 rows each 4 squares wide; each small square has side 1 m.
    Ans: Area = number of square boxes covered
    Squares in the top part = 2 x 2 = 4.
    Squares in the lower rows = 4 + 4 = 8.
    Total squares = 4 + 8 = 12.
    Each square has area 1 m².
    Area = 12 x 1 m² = 12 m².
    Answer: The area is 12 m².
    Note: The printed answer key gives 1 m², which is incorrect.

mcqs.q: The line segment which joins any two points on a circle and passes through its centre is called the:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Mark the centre point in the middle of the circle. Step 2: With a ruler, draw a straight line from one point on the circle to the opposite point on the circle, passing through the centre. The line segment which joins any two points on a circle and passes through its centre is called the diameter. Answer: Diameter.

mcqs.q: The line segment which joins any point on the circle to its centre is called the:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Mark the centre point in the middle of the circle. Step 2: With a ruler, draw a straight line from the centre to any point on the circle. The line segment which joins any point on the circle to its centre is called the radius of the circle. Answer: Radius.

mcqs.q: The point in the centre of a circle, from which the distance of all the points of the circle is the same, is called the:
mcqs.why: The point in the centre of a circle, from which the distance of all the points of the circle is the same, is called the centre of the circle. Step 1: Find the middle point of the circle. Step 2: Mark a dot there; this dot is the centre. Answer: Centre.

mcqs.q: Find the perimeter of a square of side 5 m.
mcqs.why: Perimeter = sum of the lengths of all sides. The shaded figure is a square of side 5 m. Perimeter = 5 m + 5 m + 5 m + 5 m = 20 m. Answer: The perimeter is 20 m.

mcqs.q: Find the perimeter of a rectangle with length 7 cm and breadth 4 cm.
mcqs.why: Perimeter = sum of the lengths of all sides. Length = 7 cm and breadth = 4 cm. Perimeter = 7 cm + 4 cm + 7 cm + 4 cm = 22 cm. Answer: The perimeter is 22 cm.

mcqs.q: Find the perimeter of a rectangle with length 6 m and breadth 4 m.
mcqs.why: Perimeter = sum of the lengths of all sides. Length = 6 m and breadth = 4 m. Perimeter = 6 m + 4 m + 6 m + 4 m = 20 m. Answer: The perimeter is 20 m.

mcqs.q: Find the area of a rectangle on a grid, 4 squares long and 3 squares wide, each small square having side 1 cm.
mcqs.why: Area = number of square boxes covered. Number of squares = 4 x 3 = 12. Each square has area 1 cm². Area = 12 x 1 cm² = 12 cm². Answer: The area is 12 cm². Note: The printed answer key gives 4 cm², which is incorrect; the correct working above gives 12 cm².

mcqs.q: Find the area of a rectangle on a grid, 12 squares long and 7 squares wide, each small square having side 1 m.
mcqs.why: Area = number of square boxes covered. Number of squares = 12 x 7 = 84. Each square has area 1 m². Area = 84 x 1 m² = 84 m². Answer: The area is 84 m².

mcqs.q: Find the area of a rectangle on a grid, 4 squares long and 2 squares wide, each small square having side 1 cm.
mcqs.why: Area = number of square boxes covered. Number of squares = 4 x 2 = 8. Each square has area 1 cm². Area = 8 x 1 cm² = 8 cm². Answer: The area is 8 cm².

mcqs.q: Find the area of a figure on a grid shaped like a tower: the top part is 2 squares wide and 2 squares high, and below it are 2 rows each 4 squares wide; each small square has side 1 m.
mcqs.why: Area = number of square boxes covered. Squares in the top part = 2 x 2 = 4. Squares in the lower rows = 4 + 4 = 8. Total squares = 4 + 8 = 12. Each square has area 1 m². Area = 12 x 1 m² = 12 m². Answer: The area is 12 m². Note: The printed answer key gives 1 m², which is incorrect; the correct working above gives 12 m².

lessons.title: Exercise 5 and 6 — Symmetry and 3D Figures
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 5

  • Q: 1. Mark (tick) on the figures where you can see line of symmetry. a) A wrapped sweet (candy) shape with a dotted line drawn diagonally through its middle from one twisted end to the other.
    Ans: Folding the figure along the dotted line, the two parts cover each other exactly.
    So the dotted line divides the figure into two equal parts.
    Answer: Yes, tick it. The dotted line is a line of symmetry.
  • Q: 1. Mark (tick) on the figures where you can see line of symmetry. b) A hexagon (a six-sided figure, pointed at the left and right) with a dotted horizontal line drawn through its middle.
    Ans: Folding the figure along the dotted line, the upper part covers the lower part exactly.
    So the dotted line divides the figure into two equal parts.
    Answer: Yes, tick it. The dotted line is a line of symmetry.
  • Q: 1. Mark (tick) on the figures where you can see line of symmetry. c) A downward arrow shape (a block on top, a narrow neck and a triangular arrowhead at the bottom) with a short dotted horizontal line drawn across its narrow neck.
    Ans: Folding the figure along the dotted line, the block above the line does not cover the arrowhead below it.
    The two parts are not equal, so the dotted line does not divide the figure into two equal parts.
    Answer: No, do not tick it. The dotted line is not a line of symmetry.
  • Q: 1. Mark (tick) on the figures where you can see line of symmetry. d) A five-pointed star with a short dotted line drawn from the top point slanting down to the middle of the star.
    Ans: The line of symmetry of a star passes straight down through its top point and the middle of the star.
    The dotted line drawn here slants to one side, so folding along it the two parts would not cover each other.
    Answer: No, do not tick it. The dotted line as drawn is not a line of symmetry.
  • Q: 2. Complete the given figures. First figure (on dot paper): the upper half of a castle-like figure with a notch in the middle is drawn above a horizontal red line of symmetry.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): On dot paper, above a horizontal red line, there is the top half of a figure: a wide top bar, side towers going down on the left and right, and a square notch in the middle; below the red line the dot paper is empty.
    To complete the figure, draw the mirror image of the given half below the red line, at the same distance from the line: the side towers continue down the same amount, and the middle notch is copied below in reverse.
    Answer: The completed figure is the given half together with its exact mirror image below the red line of symmetry.
  • Q: 2. Complete the given figures. Second figure (on a square grid): a zigzag line like two arrowheads pointing left is drawn on the left of a vertical red dotted line of symmetry.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): On a square grid, a vertical red dotted line stands on the right; to its left a zigzag line goes: down-left to a point, back right and down to a second point, then down-left and across to meet the dotted line at the bottom.
    To complete the figure, draw the mirror image of the zigzag on the right side of the dotted line: every point is copied at the same distance on the other side of the line, making a matching zigzag opening to the right.
    Answer: The completed figure is the given zigzag together with its exact mirror image on the right of the line of symmetry.
  • Q: 2. Complete the given figures. Third figure (on a square grid): a stepped line ending in a slanting line is drawn above a horizontal red dotted line of symmetry.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): On a square grid, a horizontal red dotted line runs across the middle; above it a line rises in two small steps from the left, runs flat, rises once more, then slants down to meet the dotted line on the right.
    To complete the figure, draw the mirror image of the line below the dotted line: the slanting part goes down and to the left below the line, and the steps are copied in reverse order at the same distances below the line.
    Answer: The completed figure is the given half together with its exact mirror image below the line of symmetry.

Exercise 6

  • Q: 1. Write the names of these figures and label their vertices, edges, and surfaces. a) A light blue box with all sides equal, shown with dotted lines for the hidden edges.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A cube drawn in 3-D; one top corner is labelled Vertex, one vertical side edge is labelled Edge, and the flat right face is labelled Surface.
    All its surfaces are square, so the figure is a cube.
    A cube has 8 vertices, 12 edges and 6 surfaces.
    Answer: Cube: 8 vertices, 12 edges, 6 surfaces.
  • Q: 1. Write the names of these figures and label their vertices, edges, and surfaces. b) A long pink box, longer than it is tall, shown with dotted lines for the hidden edges.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A cuboid drawn in 3-D; one top corner is labelled Vertex, one side edge is labelled Edge, and the flat front face is labelled Surface.
    All its surfaces are of rectangular shape, so the figure is a cuboid.
    A cuboid has 8 vertices, 12 edges and 6 surfaces.
    Answer: Cuboid: 8 vertices, 12 edges, 6 surfaces.
  • Q: 1. Write the names of these figures and label their vertices, edges, and surfaces. c) A gold upright can-like figure with a flat circular top and bottom.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A cylinder standing upright; its top and bottom are circular surfaces, its side is a curved surface, and the circles where the side meets the top and bottom are its curved edges.
    The figure is a cylinder.
    A cylinder has 0 vertices, 2 edges and 3 surfaces.
    Answer: Cylinder: 0 vertices, 2 edges, 3 surfaces.
  • Q: 1. Write the names of these figures and label their vertices, edges, and surfaces. d) A round blue ball-like figure.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A sphere; it has only one curved surface all over, with no corner and no straight edge.
    The figure is a sphere.
    A sphere has 0 vertices, 0 edges and 1 surface.
    Answer: Sphere: 0 vertices, 0 edges, 1 surface.
  • Q: 1. Write the names of these figures and label their vertices, edges, and surfaces. e) A green figure with a pointed top and a round flat bottom.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A cone; its pointed top is its Vertex, its sloping side is a Curved surface, its flat round bottom is a Circular surface, and the circle at the bottom is its curved edge.
    The figure is a cone.
    A cone has 1 vertex, 1 edge and 2 surfaces.
    Answer: Cone: 1 vertex, 1 edge, 2 surfaces.
  • Q: 1. Write the names of these figures and label their vertices, edges, and surfaces. f) A blue figure with a flat four-sided base and triangular sides meeting at a top point.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A pyramid with a square base; its top point is labelled Vertex, one sloping side line is labelled Edge, and one triangular face is labelled Surface.
    The figure is a pyramid.
    A pyramid (with a square base) has 5 vertices, 8 edges and 5 surfaces.
    Answer: Pyramid: 5 vertices, 8 edges, 5 surfaces.
  • Q: 2. Look at the figures given below and write their properties. a) A sphere (round ball). Write Vertices, Edges, Surfaces and Shapes of surfaces.
    Ans: A sphere has a curved surface only.
    It has no vertices and no edges.
    Answer: Sphere: Vertices 0, Edges 0, Surfaces 1, Shape of surface: curved.
  • Q: 2. Look at the figures given below and write their properties. b) A pyramid with a square base. Write Vertices, Edges, Surfaces and Shapes of surfaces.
    Ans: A pyramid with a square base has 1 square surface and 4 triangular surfaces.
    Total surfaces = 1 + 4 = 5.
    Answer: Pyramid: Vertices 5, Edges 8, Surfaces 5, Shapes of surfaces: 1 square and 4 triangular.
  • Q: 2. Look at the figures given below and write their properties. c) A cylinder. Write Vertices, Edges, Surfaces and Shapes of surfaces.
    Ans: A cylinder has 1 curved surface and 2 circular surfaces.
    Total surfaces = 1 + 2 = 3, and it has 2 curved edges and no vertices.
    Answer: Cylinder: Vertices 0, Edges 2, Surfaces 3, Shapes of surfaces: 1 curved and 2 circular.
  • Q: 2. Look at the figures given below and write their properties. d) A cone. Write Vertices, Edges, Surfaces and Shapes of surfaces.
    Ans: A cone has 1 curved surface and 1 circular surface.
    Total surfaces = 1 + 1 = 2, and it has 1 vertex and 1 curved edge.
    Answer: Cone: Vertices 1, Edges 1, Surfaces 2, Shapes of surfaces: 1 curved and 1 circular.
  • Q: 2. Look at the figures given below and write their properties. e) A cuboid (an orange long box). Write Vertices, Edges, Surfaces and Shapes of surfaces.
    Ans: A cuboid has all surfaces of rectangular shape.
    Answer: Cuboid: Vertices 8, Edges 12, Surfaces 6, Shapes of surfaces: rectangular.
  • Q: 2. Look at the figures given below and write their properties. f) A cube (a pink box with all sides equal). Write Vertices, Edges, Surfaces and Shapes of surfaces.
    Ans: A cube has all surfaces of square shape.
    Answer: Cube: Vertices 8, Edges 12, Surfaces 6, Shapes of surfaces: square.
  • Q: 3. Mark (tick) the figure which has the given properties. a) 0 vertices, 3 surfaces, 2 edges. The three figures are: a cone, a cylinder, and a pyramid.
    Ans: A cone has 1 vertex, 2 surfaces and 1 edge, so it does not match.
    A cylinder has 0 vertices, 3 surfaces and 2 edges, so it matches.
    A pyramid has 5 vertices, 5 surfaces and 8 edges, so it does not match.
    Answer: Tick the cylinder (the middle figure).
  • Q: 3. Mark (tick) the figure which has the given properties. b) 8 vertices, 6 flat surfaces, 12 edges. The three figures are: a cylinder, a pyramid, and a cube.
    Ans: A cylinder has 0 vertices, so it does not match.
    A pyramid has 5 vertices, so it does not match.
    A cube has 8 vertices, 6 flat surfaces and 12 edges, so it matches.
    Answer: Tick the cube (the third figure).
  • Q: 3. Mark (tick) the figure which has the given properties. c) 0 vertices, 1 surface, 0 edges. The three figures are: a sphere, a cuboid, and a cylinder.
    Ans: A sphere has 0 vertices, 1 surface (curved) and 0 edges, so it matches.
    A cuboid has 8 vertices and a cylinder has 3 surfaces, so they do not match.
    Answer: Tick the sphere (the first figure).
  • Q: 3. Mark (tick) the figure which has the given properties. d) 5 vertices, 5 surface, 8 edges. The three figures are: a cube, a pyramid, and a cone.
    Ans: A cube has 8 vertices, so it does not match.
    A pyramid has 5 vertices, 5 surfaces and 8 edges, so it matches.
    A cone has 1 vertex, so it does not match.
    Answer: Tick the pyramid (the middle figure).
  • Q: 3. Mark (tick) the figure which has the given properties. e) 1 vertex, 2 surfaces, 1 edge. The three figures are: a cone, a cube, and a cuboid.
    Ans: A cone has 1 vertex, 2 surfaces and 1 edge, so it matches.
    A cube and a cuboid each have 8 vertices, so they do not match.
    Answer: Tick the cone (the first figure).
  • Q: 3. Mark (tick) the figure which has the given properties. f) 8 vertices, 6 rectangular surfaces, 12 edges. The three figures are: a cylinder, a pyramid, and a cuboid.
    Ans: A cylinder has 0 vertices, so it does not match.
    A pyramid has 5 vertices, so it does not match.
    A cuboid has 8 vertices, 6 rectangular surfaces and 12 edges, so it matches.
    Answer: Tick the cuboid (the third figure).

mcqs.q: A cube has all its surfaces square. How many vertices, edges and surfaces does a cube have?
mcqs.why: All its surfaces are square, so the figure is a cube. A cube has 8 vertices, 12 edges and 6 surfaces. Answer: Cube: 8 vertices, 12 edges, 6 surfaces.

mcqs.q: How many vertices, edges and surfaces does a cylinder have?
mcqs.why: A cylinder has 1 curved surface and 2 circular surfaces. Total surfaces = 1 + 2 = 3, and it has 2 curved edges and no vertices. Answer: Cylinder: 0 vertices, 2 edges, 3 surfaces.

mcqs.q: How many vertices, edges and surfaces does a sphere have?
mcqs.why: A sphere has a curved surface only. It has no vertices and no edges. Answer: Sphere: Vertices 0, Edges 0, Surfaces 1, Shape of surface: curved.

mcqs.q: How many vertices, edges and surfaces does a cone have?
mcqs.why: A cone has 1 curved surface and 1 circular surface. Total surfaces = 1 + 1 = 2, and it has 1 vertex and 1 curved edge. Answer: Cone: Vertices 1, Edges 1, Surfaces 2.

mcqs.q: How many vertices, edges and surfaces does a pyramid with a square base have?
mcqs.why: A pyramid with a square base has 1 square surface and 4 triangular surfaces. Total surfaces = 1 + 4 = 5. Answer: Pyramid: Vertices 5, Edges 8, Surfaces 5, Shapes of surfaces: 1 square and 4 triangular.

mcqs.q: Which figure has 0 vertices, 3 surfaces and 2 edges: a cone, a cylinder, or a pyramid?
mcqs.why: A cone has 1 vertex, 2 surfaces and 1 edge, so it does not match. A cylinder has 0 vertices, 3 surfaces and 2 edges, so it matches. A pyramid has 5 vertices, 5 surfaces and 8 edges, so it does not match. Answer: Cylinder.

mcqs.q: Which figure has 8 vertices, 6 flat surfaces and 12 edges: a cylinder, a pyramid, or a cube?
mcqs.why: A cylinder has 0 vertices, so it does not match. A pyramid has 5 vertices, so it does not match. A cube has 8 vertices, 6 flat surfaces and 12 edges, so it matches. Answer: Cube.

mcqs.q: Which figure has 0 vertices, 1 surface and 0 edges: a sphere, a cuboid, or a cylinder?
mcqs.why: A sphere has 0 vertices, 1 surface (curved) and 0 edges, so it matches. A cuboid has 8 vertices and a cylinder has 3 surfaces, so they do not match. Answer: Sphere.

mcqs.q: Which figure has 5 vertices, 5 surfaces and 8 edges: a cube, a pyramid, or a cone?
mcqs.why: A cube has 8 vertices, so it does not match. A pyramid has 5 vertices, 5 surfaces and 8 edges, so it matches. A cone has 1 vertex, so it does not match. Answer: Pyramid.

mcqs.q: A hexagon has a dotted horizontal line through its middle. Folding along the line, the upper part covers the lower part exactly. Is the dotted line a line of symmetry?
options: No, it is not a line of symmetry
Yes, it is a line of symmetry
Yes, but the parts are not equal
No, the parts do not match
mcqs.why: Folding the figure along the dotted line, the upper part covers the lower part exactly. So the dotted line divides the figure into two equal parts. Answer: Yes, tick it. The dotted line is a line of symmetry.

lessons.title: Review Exercise — Part 1
lessons.notes_html:
Review Exercise (Questions 1–17)

  • Q: 1. Encircle the correct answer. a) The lines which keep going straight and never meet each other are called:
    Options: (a) horizontal lines   (b) vertical lines   (c) non-parallel lines   (d) parallel lines
    Ans: parallel lines
  • Q: 1. Encircle the correct answer. b) There are _____ small parts in a protractor and each part is equal to 1 degree.
    Options: (a) 150   (b) 120   (c) 180   (d) 360
    Ans: 180
  • Q: 1. Encircle the correct answer. c) When horizontal and vertical lines intersect each other at a point, they form:
    Options: (a) right angles   (b) obtuse angles   (c) acute angles   (d) horizontal angles
    Ans: right angles
  • Q: 1. Encircle the correct answer. d) An angle less than _____ is called an acute angle.
    Options: (a) 90 degrees   (b) 80 degrees   (c) 100 degrees   (d) 180 degrees
    Ans: 90 degrees
  • Q: 1. Encircle the correct answer. e) The length of boundary a circle is called _____ of the circle.
    Options: (a) circumference   (b) centre   (c) diameter   (d) radius
    Ans: circumference
  • Q: 1. Encircle the correct answer. f) The surface covered by a closed figure is the _____ of that figure.
    Options: (a) length   (b) side   (c) perimeter   (d) area
    Ans: area
  • Q: 1. Encircle the correct answer. g) The line of symmetry divides a figure into _____ equal parts.
    Options: (a) 5   (b) 4   (c) 3   (d) 2
    Ans: 2
  • Q: 2. Encircle the parallel lines from the following. a) Two horizontal lines, one above the other.
    Ans: The two lines never meet each other and the distance between them remains the same.
    Answer: These are parallel lines, so encircle them.
  • Q: 2. Encircle the parallel lines from the following. b) A vertical line and a horizontal line crossing each other, with a small square mark at the crossing.
    Ans: The two lines intersect each other at a point (they form a right angle there).
    Lines which intersect each other are non-parallel lines.
    Answer: These are not parallel lines, so do not encircle them.
  • Q: 2. Encircle the parallel lines from the following. c) A vertical line and a slanting line crossing each other near the top.
    Ans: The two lines intersect each other at a point.
    Lines which intersect each other are non-parallel lines.
    Answer: These are not parallel lines, so do not encircle them.
  • Q: 3. Differentiate the right, acute and obtuse angle, in the following. a) An angle with one ray pointing to the right and the other ray pointing up to the right, narrower than a right angle.
    Ans: The angle is less than 90 degrees.
    An angle less than 90 degrees is an acute angle.
    Answer: Acute angle.
  • Q: 3. Differentiate the right, acute and obtuse angle, in the following. b) An angle with one ray pointing to the right and the other ray pointing up to the left, wider than a right angle.
    Ans: The angle is greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees.
    Such an angle is an obtuse angle.
    Answer: Obtuse angle.
  • Q: 3. Differentiate the right, acute and obtuse angle, in the following. c) A V-shaped angle with one ray pointing up to the left and the other ray pointing up to the right, opening straight up.
    Ans: The two rays are at a quarter turn from each other, so the angle measures 90 degrees.
    An angle of 90 degrees is a right angle.
    Answer: Right angle.
  • Q: 4. Draw the angles of given measurements. a) 135 degrees
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A horizontal ray with its vertex at the left end, and a second ray rising from the vertex up to the left; the wide angle between the rays is marked with an arc and labelled 135 degrees.
    Step 1: Draw a ray with the help of a ruler.
    Step 2: Place the centre point of the protractor on the vertex and the baseline exactly on the ray.
    Step 3: Mark a point at 135 degrees on the scale.
    Step 4: Remove the protractor and join the vertex to the marked point.
    Answer: An angle of 135 degrees is drawn.
  • Q: 4. Draw the angles of given measurements. b) 95 degrees
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A horizontal ray with its vertex at the left end, and a second ray rising from the vertex almost straight up, leaning slightly to the left; the angle between the rays is marked with an arc and labelled 95 degrees.
    Step 1: Draw a ray with the help of a ruler.
    Step 2: Place the centre point of the protractor on the vertex and the baseline exactly on the ray.
    Step 3: Mark a point at 95 degrees on the scale.
    Step 4: Remove the protractor and join the vertex to the marked point.
    Answer: An angle of 95 degrees is drawn.
  • Q: 4. Draw the angles of given measurements. c) 70 degrees
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A horizontal ray with its vertex at the left end, and a second ray rising from the vertex up to the right; the angle between the rays is marked with an arc and labelled 70 degrees.
    Step 1: Draw a ray with the help of a ruler.
    Step 2: Place the centre point of the protractor on the vertex and the baseline exactly on the ray.
    Step 3: Mark a point at 70 degrees on the scale.
    Step 4: Remove the protractor and join the vertex to the marked point.
    Answer: An angle of 70 degrees is drawn.
  • Q: 4. Draw the angles of given measurements. d) 20 degrees
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A horizontal ray with its vertex at the left end, and a second ray rising gently from the vertex up to the right; the small angle between the rays is marked with an arc and labelled 20 degrees.
    Step 1: Draw a ray with the help of a ruler.
    Step 2: Place the centre point of the protractor on the vertex and the baseline exactly on the ray.
    Step 3: Mark a point at 20 degrees on the scale.
    Step 4: Remove the protractor and join the vertex to the marked point.
    Answer: An angle of 20 degrees is drawn.

mcqs.q: 1. Encircle the correct answer. a) The lines which keep going straight and never meet each other are called:
mcqs.why: Parallel lines never meet each other and the distance between them remains the same, as shown for the two horizontal lines in this exercise. So lines that never meet are parallel lines.

mcqs.q: 1. Encircle the correct answer. b) There are _____ small parts in a protractor and each part is equal to 1 degree.
mcqs.why: A protractor is used to measure angles in degrees. It is divided into 180 small parts and each part is equal to 1 degree, so there are 180 parts in a protractor.

mcqs.q: 1. Encircle the correct answer. c) When horizontal and vertical lines intersect each other at a point, they form:
mcqs.why: When a vertical line and a horizontal line cross each other, the angle at the crossing is marked with a small square. The small square shows 90 degrees, which is a right angle.

mcqs.q: 1. Encircle the correct answer. d) An angle less than _____ is called an acute angle.
mcqs.why: An angle less than 90 degrees is an acute angle, as stated in this exercise: an angle narrower than a right angle, less than 90 degrees, is acute.

mcqs.q: 1. Encircle the correct answer. e) The length of boundary a circle is called _____ of the circle.
mcqs.why: The length of the boundary of a circle is called the circumference of the circle, as stated when labelling the circle in this unit. The centre, diameter and radius are other parts, not the boundary length.

mcqs.q: 1. Encircle the correct answer. f) The surface covered by a closed figure is the _____ of that figure.
mcqs.why: Area is the surface covered by a figure, found by counting the square boxes covered. Perimeter is the length of the boundary, not the surface covered, so the surface covered is the area.

mcqs.q: 1. Encircle the correct answer. g) The line of symmetry divides a figure into _____ equal parts.
mcqs.why: Folding a figure along its line of symmetry, the two parts cover each other exactly. So the line of symmetry divides the figure into two equal parts, that is, 2 equal parts.

mcqs.q: Two horizontal lines, one above the other. Should they be encircled as parallel lines?
options: These are not parallel lines, so do not encircle them
These are parallel lines, so encircle them
mcqs.why: The two lines never meet each other and the distance between them remains the same. Answer: These are parallel lines, so encircle them.

mcqs.q: An angle with one ray pointing to the right and the other ray pointing up to the right, narrower than a right angle, is less than 90 degrees. What type of angle is it?
mcqs.why: The angle is less than 90 degrees. An angle less than 90 degrees is an acute angle. Answer: Acute angle.

mcqs.q: An angle with one ray pointing to the right and the other ray pointing up to the left, wider than a right angle, is greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees. What type of angle is it?
mcqs.why: The angle is greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees. Such an angle is an obtuse angle. Answer: Obtuse angle.

lessons.title: Review Exercise — Part 2
lessons.notes_html:
Review Exercise (Questions 18–34)

  • Q: 5. Label the circle. a) The label line points to the straight line that passes through the centre of the circle from the top of the circle to the bottom.
    Ans: The line segment which joins any two points on a circle and passes through its centre is called the diameter.
    Answer: a) Diameter.
  • Q: 5. Label the circle. b) The label line points to the curved boundary line of the circle itself.
    Ans: The length of the boundary of a circle is called the circumference of the circle.
    Answer: b) Circumference.
  • Q: 5. Label the circle. c) The label line points to the dot in the middle of the circle, from which a line goes to the right-hand point of the circle.
    Ans: The point in the middle of a circle, from which all points of the circle are at the same distance, is called the centre.
    Answer: c) Centre.
  • Q: 5. Label the circle. d) The label line points to the line segment joining the centre of the circle to a point on the circle on the right side.
    Ans: The line segment which joins any point on the circle to its centre is called the radius.
    Answer: d) Radius.
  • Q: 6. Find the perimeter and area of the shaded figures. a) A blue shaded rectangle on a grid, 6 squares long and 4 squares wide, each small square having side 1 m.
    Ans: Perimeter = sum of the lengths of all sides
    Length = 6 m and breadth = 4 m.
    Perimeter = 6 m + 4 m + 6 m + 4 m = 20 m.
    Area = number of square boxes = 6 x 4 = 24 squares.
    Area = 24 x 1 m² = 24 m².
    Answer: Perimeter 20 m, Area 24 m².
  • Q: 6. Find the perimeter and area of the shaded figures. b) A light blue shaded square on a grid, 4 squares long and 4 squares wide, each small square having side 1 cm.
    Ans: Perimeter = sum of the lengths of all sides
    Side of the square = 4 cm.
    Perimeter = 4 cm + 4 cm + 4 cm + 4 cm = 16 cm.
    Area = number of square boxes = 4 x 4 = 16 squares.
    Area = 16 x 1 cm² = 16 cm².
    Answer: Perimeter 16 cm, Area 16 cm².
  • Q: 6. Find the perimeter and area of the shaded figures. c) A shaded rectangle on a grid, 9 squares long and 5 squares wide, each small square having side 1 m.
    Ans: Perimeter = sum of the lengths of all sides
    Length = 9 m and breadth = 5 m.
    Perimeter = 9 m + 5 m + 9 m + 5 m = 28 m.
    Area = number of square boxes = 9 x 5 = 45 squares.
    Area = 45 x 1 m² = 45 m².
    Answer: Perimeter 28 m, Area 45 m².
  • Q: 7. Identify the symmetry in the given figures and draw lines of symmetry, where possible. a) A star-like figure: a square with a triangular point sticking out from the middle of each of its four sides (top, bottom, left and right).
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A square with one triangular point at the middle of each side; lines of symmetry can be drawn vertically through the top and bottom points, horizontally through the left and right points, and along both diagonals through opposite corners.
    The figure looks the same on both sides of each of these lines.
    Answer: The figure has symmetry, with 4 lines of symmetry (vertical, horizontal and two diagonal lines).
  • Q: 7. Identify the symmetry in the given figures and draw lines of symmetry, where possible. b) An irregular four-sided figure with all sides of different lengths and no matching parts.
    Ans: No line can divide this figure into two parts that cover each other exactly.
    Whichever way it is folded, the two parts do not match.
    Answer: The figure has no symmetry; no line of symmetry can be drawn.
  • Q: 7. Identify the symmetry in the given figures and draw lines of symmetry, where possible. c) A tall pointed figure like a kite: a point at the top, sides slanting out and then coming in to a flat bottom, the same on the left and right.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A pointed figure, widest below its top point, with a flat base; a vertical line drawn from the top point straight down through the middle to the base divides it into two matching halves.
    The left half is the mirror image of the right half.
    Answer: The figure has symmetry, with 1 line of symmetry (the vertical line through the middle).
  • Q: 7. Identify the symmetry in the given figures and draw lines of symmetry, where possible. d) A crown-like figure: a flat bottom, two sides slanting slightly outwards to two sharp points at the top, with a V-shaped notch in the middle of the top.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A figure with a flat base, two top points of equal height on the left and right, and an equal V-notch in the centre of the top; a vertical line drawn through the middle of the notch down to the base divides it into two matching halves.
    The left half is the mirror image of the right half.
    Answer: The figure has symmetry, with 1 line of symmetry (the vertical line through the middle).
  • Q: 8. Complete the given figures and find their perimeter and area as well, where possible. a) On a square grid (each square of side 1 m), a horizontal red dotted line of symmetry runs across the middle; below it a pink stepped outline like a bowl is drawn: it goes down in steps from the line, across a flat bottom 1 square wide, and up in steps back to the line, 5 squares wide at the line and 3 squares deep.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): The given half is a stepped bowl shape hanging below the horizontal line of symmetry, 5 m wide at the line and 3 m deep; rows of the half, from the line downwards, are 5, 3 and 1 squares wide.
    Complete the figure by drawing the mirror image of the bowl above the line.
    Area of the given half = 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 squares = 9 m².
    Area of the completed figure = 2 x 9 m² = 18 m².
    The stepped boundary of the half is 11 m long (its width 5 m across plus 3 m down and 3 m up in steps), and the line of symmetry itself is inside the figure, not part of the boundary.
    Perimeter of the completed figure = 2 x 11 m = 22 m.
    Answer: Perimeter 22 m, Area 18 m².
  • Q: 8. Complete the given figures and find their perimeter and area as well, where possible. b) On a square grid (each square of side 1 cm), a vertical red dotted line of symmetry is drawn; on the right side of the grid, away from the line, there is a green C-shaped figure 6 squares tall: its left bar is 1 square wide, with arms of 2, 3 and 2 squares at the top, upper-middle and bottom rows.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): The green figure is like the letter C facing right, made of 10 squares: 2 in the top row, 3 in the next row, 1 in each of the next three rows, and 2 in the bottom row; the vertical red dotted line is its line of symmetry, some columns to its left.
    Complete the figure by drawing the mirror image of the green figure on the left side of the line, at the same distance from the line; the two halves face each other and do not touch.
    Area of the given figure = 10 squares = 10 cm².
    Area of the completed figure = 2 x 10 cm² = 20 cm².
    Perimeter of the given figure: counting the outside edges of its 10 squares gives 20 cm.
    Perimeter of the completed figure = 2 x 20 cm = 40 cm.
    Answer: Perimeter 40 cm, Area 20 cm².
  • Q: 8. Complete the given figures and find their perimeter and area as well, where possible. c) On dot paper (dots 1 m apart), a red cross is drawn: one vertical and one horizontal line of symmetry crossing each other. In the top-left part, touching the horizontal line, a stepped figure is drawn: from the top it is 2 squares wide for 1 row, 3 squares wide for 1 row, 2 squares wide for 1 row, and 1 square wide (in the second column) for the bottom row.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): The given stepped figure sits in the top-left quarter, against the horizontal line of symmetry but one column away from the vertical line; the red cross gives two lines of symmetry, so the figure must be copied into all four quarters.
    Complete the figure by reflecting it across the horizontal line, across the vertical line, and across both lines, making four copies in all.
    Area of the given figure = 2 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 8 squares = 8 m².
    Area of the completed figure = 4 x 8 m² = 32 m².
    Perimeter of the given figure: counting its outside edges gives 14 m.
    The copies above and below the horizontal line join along 1 m where the figure touches that line, so each joined pair has perimeter 14 m + 14 m - 2 x 1 m = 26 m; the left and right pairs do not touch each other.
    Perimeter of the completed figure = 2 x 26 m = 52 m.
    Answer: Perimeter 52 m, Area 32 m².
  • Q: 8. Complete the given figures and find their perimeter and area as well, where possible. d) On dot paper (dots 1 cm apart), two red diagonal lines cross each other like the letter X; these are the lines of symmetry. In the top part, between the two diagonals, a small green figure with some slanting sides is drawn.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): Two red diagonal lines cross at the centre of the dot paper, dividing it into four equal parts (top, right, bottom and left); a small green figure with slanting and straight sides is drawn in the top part.
    Complete the figure by reflecting the green figure across each diagonal line, so that a matching copy appears in the right, bottom and left parts, making four copies in all.
    The sides of the copies include slanting (diagonal) sides, whose lengths are not a whole number of centimetres, so the perimeter and area cannot be found exactly in whole cm and cm².
    Answer: The figure is completed by drawing its mirror image across both diagonal lines; perimeter and area in whole units are not possible for this figure.
  • Q: 9. Encircle the figures which have the following properties: a) 6 flat surfaces. The three figures are: a cube (blue), a cylinder (light blue, standing upright), and a cuboid (pink, lying flat).
    Ans: A cube has 6 surfaces, and all of them are flat.
    A cylinder has 3 surfaces, of which only 2 are flat and 1 is curved, so it does not have 6 flat surfaces.
    A cuboid has 6 surfaces, and all of them are flat.
    Answer: Encircle the cube and the cuboid.
  • Q: 9. Encircle the figures which have the following properties: b) 1 vertex. The three figures are: a cylinder (light blue, standing upright), a cuboid (pink, lying flat), and a cone (light green, point downwards).
    Ans: A cylinder has 0 vertices.
    A cuboid has 8 vertices.
    A cone has exactly 1 vertex (its pointed end).
    Answer: Encircle the cone.

mcqs.q: The label line points to the straight line that passes through the centre of the circle from the top of the circle to the bottom. What is this part called?
mcqs.why: The line segment which joins any two points on a circle and passes through its centre is called the diameter. Answer: a) Diameter.

mcqs.q: The label line points to the curved boundary line of the circle itself. What is this part called?
mcqs.why: The length of the boundary of a circle is called the circumference of the circle. Answer: b) Circumference.

mcqs.q: The label line points to the dot in the middle of the circle, from which a line goes to the right-hand point of the circle. What is this part called?
mcqs.why: The point in the middle of a circle, from which all points of the circle are at the same distance, is called the centre. Answer: c) Centre.

mcqs.q: The label line points to the line segment joining the centre of the circle to a point on the circle on the right side. What is this part called?
mcqs.why: The line segment which joins any point on the circle to its centre is called the radius. Answer: d) Radius.

mcqs.q: Find the perimeter and area of a rectangle on a grid, 6 squares long and 4 squares wide, each small square having side 1 m.
mcqs.why: Perimeter = sum of the lengths of all sides. Length = 6 m and breadth = 4 m. Perimeter = 6 m + 4 m + 6 m + 4 m = 20 m. Area = number of square boxes = 6 x 4 = 24 squares. Area = 24 x 1 m² = 24 m². Answer: Perimeter 20 m, Area 24 m².

mcqs.q: Find the perimeter and area of a square on a grid, 4 squares long and 4 squares wide, each small square having side 1 cm.
mcqs.why: Perimeter = sum of the lengths of all sides. Side of the square = 4 cm. Perimeter = 4 cm + 4 cm + 4 cm + 4 cm = 16 cm. Area = number of square boxes = 4 x 4 = 16 squares. Area = 16 x 1 cm² = 16 cm². Answer: Perimeter 16 cm, Area 16 cm².

mcqs.q: Find the perimeter and area of a rectangle on a grid, 9 squares long and 5 squares wide, each small square having side 1 m.
mcqs.why: Perimeter = sum of the lengths of all sides. Length = 9 m and breadth = 5 m. Perimeter = 9 m + 5 m + 9 m + 5 m = 28 m. Area = number of square boxes = 9 x 5 = 45 squares. Area = 45 x 1 m² = 45 m². Answer: Perimeter 28 m, Area 45 m².

mcqs.q: A star-like figure is a square with a triangular point sticking out from the middle of each of its four sides. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
mcqs.why: Lines of symmetry can be drawn vertically through the top and bottom points, horizontally through the left and right points, and along both diagonals through opposite corners. The figure looks the same on both sides of each of these lines. Answer: The figure has symmetry, with 4 lines of symmetry (vertical, horizontal and two diagonal lines).

mcqs.q: Which figures have 6 flat surfaces: a cube, a cylinder, and a cuboid?
mcqs.why: A cube has 6 surfaces, and all of them are flat. A cylinder has 3 surfaces, of which only 2 are flat and 1 is curved, so it does not have 6 flat surfaces. A cuboid has 6 surfaces, and all of them are flat. Answer: Encircle the cube and the cuboid.

mcqs.q: Which figure has 1 vertex: a cylinder, a cuboid, or a cone?
mcqs.why: A cylinder has 0 vertices. A cuboid has 8 vertices. A cone has exactly 1 vertex (its pointed end). Answer: Encircle the cone.

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Try Yourself (book p. 132)

  • Q: Try Yourself: Look at the things in your surroundings. Can you see parallel lines?
    Ans: Parallel lines never meet each other and the distance between them always remains the same.
    Yes, parallel lines can be seen all around us.
    Examples: the two rails of a railway track, the two long edges of a ruler, the opposite edges of a book or notebook, and the lines marked on a road.
    Answer: Yes, for example the rails of a railway track and the opposite edges of a book are parallel lines.

Try It (book p. 133)

  • Q: Try It! Look at the things around you, can you distinguish between parallel and non-parallel lines?
    Ans: Parallel lines never meet each other, even if they are extended, and the distance between them always remains the same, for example the two rails of a railway track.
    Non-parallel lines intersect each other at some point, if they are extended, for example the two blades of a pair of scissors, which meet at point O.
    Answer: Lines that never meet are parallel lines, and lines that meet at a point are non-parallel lines.

Try Yourself (book p. 135)

  • Q: Try Yourself: Look at the clock and find what angles are its hands making? The clock shows 5 o'clock: the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand is at 5.
    Ans: In one hour the hour hand moves from one number to the next, which is 30 degrees.
    From 12 to 5 there are 5 steps.
    Angle = 5 x 30 degrees = 150 degrees.
    An angle greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees is an obtuse angle.
    Answer: The hands make an angle of 150 degrees, which is an obtuse angle.

Try Yourself (book p. 137)

  • Q: Try Yourself: Measure the angles given below by using a protractor. First angle: one ray points to the right and the other ray points up and slightly to the left, opening at the top.
    Ans: Place the centre point of the protractor on the vertex of the angle.
    Place the baseline of the protractor exactly on the ray pointing to the right.
    Read the mark where the second ray crosses the scale.
    The angle measures about 105 degrees.
    An angle greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees is an obtuse angle.
    Answer: About 105 degrees, an obtuse angle.
  • Q: Try Yourself: Measure the angles given below by using a protractor. Second angle: the vertex is at the right, one ray points to the left and the other ray points up and to the left at 45 degrees.
    Ans: Place the centre point of the protractor on the vertex of the angle.
    Place the baseline of the protractor exactly on one ray.
    Read the mark where the second ray crosses the scale.
    The angle measures 45 degrees.
    An angle less than 90 degrees is an acute angle.
    Answer: 45 degrees, an acute angle.

Try Yourself (book p. 138)

  • Q: Try Yourself: Draw an angle of 60 degrees by using a protractor.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A ray drawn with a ruler, with the vertex at its left end; a second ray rises from the same vertex up to the right, making 60 degrees with the first ray; the angle between the rays is marked with a small arc and labelled 60 degrees.
    Step 1: Draw a ray with the help of a ruler.
    Step 2: Place the centre point of the protractor on the vertex (the starting point of the ray) and place the baseline exactly on the ray.
    Step 3: Mark a point at 60 degrees on the scale.
    Step 4: Remove the protractor and join the vertex to the marked point with a ruler.
    Answer: The angle drawn measures 60 degrees, which is an acute angle.
  • Q: Try Yourself: Draw an angle of 140 degrees by using a protractor.
    Ans: Diagram (in words): A ray drawn with a ruler, with the vertex at its left end; a second ray rises from the same vertex up to the left, making 140 degrees with the first ray; the angle between the rays is marked with a small arc and labelled 140 degrees.
    Step 1: Draw a ray with the help of a ruler.
    Step 2: Place the centre point of the protractor on the vertex (the starting point of the ray) and place the baseline exactly on the ray.
    Step 3: Mark a point at 140 degrees on the scale.
    Step 4: Remove the protractor and join the vertex to the marked point with a ruler.
    Answer: The angle drawn measures 140 degrees, which is an obtuse angle.

Try Yourself (book p. 139)

  • Q: Try Yourself: Which of the following angles is acute? First clock: the hands make an angle marked with a small square at the centre. Second clock: the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand is at 1.
    Ans: In the first clock the small square shows a right angle, which measures 90 degrees.
    In the second clock the hands are 1 step apart, so the angle = 1 x 30 degrees = 30 degrees.
    An angle less than 90 degrees is an acute angle.
    Answer: The angle in the second clock (30 degrees) is acute.

Try Yourself (book p. 140)

  • Q: Try Yourself: Which of the following is an obtuse angle? First clock (pink): the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand is at 5, and the sector between them on the right side is shaded. Second clock (blue): the minute hand is at 12 and the hour hand is at 3, marked with a small square.
    Ans: First clock: the hands are 5 steps apart, so the angle = 5 x 30 degrees = 150 degrees, which is greater than 90 degrees and less than 180 degrees.
    Second clock: the small square shows a right angle of 90 degrees.
    Answer: The angle in the first (pink) clock, 150 degrees, is an obtuse angle.
  • Q: Try Yourself: Measure the angles and write their types. First figure: a yellow square is shaded between a ray pointing to the right and a ray pointing straight down.
    Ans: The shaded angle is marked with a square corner, so it measures 90 degrees.
    An angle which measures 90 degrees is called a right angle.
    Answer: 90 degrees, a right angle.
  • Q: Try Yourself: Measure the angles and write their types. Second figure: a pink sector is shaded between a ray pointing to the right and a ray pointing up to the right.
    Ans: Place the centre point of the protractor on the vertex and the baseline on the ray pointing to the right.
    Read the scale where the second ray crosses it.
    The shaded angle measures about 60 degrees.
    An angle less than 90 degrees is an acute angle.
    Answer: About 60 degrees, an acute angle.
  • Q: Try Yourself: Measure the angles and write their types. Third figure: an orange sector, wider than a right angle, is shaded between a ray pointing to the right and a ray pointing up to the left.
    Ans: Place the centre point of the protractor on the vertex and the baseline on the ray pointing to the right.
    Read the scale where the second ray crosses it.
    The shaded angle measures about 135 degrees.
    An angle greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees is an obtuse angle.
    Answer: About 135 degrees, an obtuse angle.

Try Yourself (book p. 147)

  • Q: Try Yourself: Find the perimeter. A rectangle is drawn on a square grid; it is 3 squares long and 4 squares wide, and each small square has side 1 cm.
    Ans: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary of a closed figure.
    Perimeter = sum of the lengths of all sides
    Length = 3 cm and breadth = 4 cm.
    Perimeter = 3 cm + 4 cm + 3 cm + 4 cm = 14 cm.
    Answer: The perimeter is 14 cm.

Try Yourself (book p. 148)

  • Q: Try Yourself: Find the area. A figure is drawn on a square grid; it is a horizontal bar 5 squares long and 1 square wide with 1 extra square on top of its middle, and each small square has area 1 square metre.
    Ans: Area is the surface covered by a figure, found by counting the square boxes.
    Squares in the horizontal bar = 5.
    Extra square on top = 1.
    Total squares = 5 + 1 = 6.
    Area = 6 x 1 square metre = 6 square metres.
    Answer: The area is 6 m².

Try Yourself (book p. 149)

  • Q: Try Yourself: Draw a square and a rectangle on the square grid, with the same perimeter and area.
    Ans: Take a square of side 4 cm.
    Perimeter of the square = 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16 cm.
    Area of the square = 4 x 4 = 16 cm².
    A different rectangle cannot have both the same perimeter and the same area as this square, because the perimeter and area together fix the length and breadth; the only figure with perimeter 16 cm and area 16 cm² has all sides 4 cm.
    So draw the square of side 4 cm, and the rectangle with the same perimeter and area is the same 4 cm by 4 cm figure itself.
