    Answer: Square of side 4 cm has perimeter 16 cm and area 16 cm²; no different rectangle has the same perimeter and area.

lessons.title: Exercise 1 and 2
lessons.notes_html:
Exercise 1

  • Q: 1a. A horizontal bar graph shows the minimum suggested sleep time (Scale: a small square in the horizontal direction is equal to 2 hours): Infants = 14 hours, 1-2 years = 12 hours, 3-5 years = 10 hours, 6-12 years = 9 hours, 13-18 years = 7 hours. For children of 6 to 12 years, the time duration of suggested sleep is _____.
    Ans: Find the bar for 6-12 years in the graph.
    The bar for 6-12 years ends at 9 hours.
    Answer: 9 hours.
  • Q: 1b. A horizontal bar graph shows the minimum suggested sleep time (Scale: a small square in the horizontal direction is equal to 2 hours): Infants = 14 hours, 1-2 years = 12 hours, 3-5 years = 10 hours, 6-12 years = 9 hours, 13-18 years = 7 hours. The time duration of sleep for age group _____ is the maximum, by _____ hours.
    Ans: Compare the lengths of all the bars:
    Infants = 14 hours, 1-2 years = 12 hours, 3-5 years = 10 hours, 6-12 years = 9 hours, 13-18 years = 7 hours.
    The longest bar is the bar for Infants.
    Its length shows 14 hours, which is the maximum.
    Answer: The time duration of sleep for age group Infants is the maximum, by 14 hours.
  • Q: 1c. A horizontal bar graph shows the minimum suggested sleep time (Scale: a small square in the horizontal direction is equal to 2 hours): Infants = 14 hours, 1-2 years = 12 hours, 3-5 years = 10 hours, 6-12 years = 9 hours, 13-18 years = 7 hours. The sleep duration for children of age 13 to 18 years is _____ hours less than the sleep duration for children of age 3 to 5 years.
    Ans: Sleep duration for 3 to 5 years = 10 hours.
    Sleep duration for 13 to 18 years = 7 hours.
    Difference = 10 - 7 = 3 hours.
    Answer: The sleep duration for children of age 13 to 18 years is 3 hours less than the sleep duration for children of age 3 to 5 years.
  • Q: 1d. A horizontal bar graph shows the minimum suggested sleep time (Scale: a small square in the horizontal direction is equal to 2 hours): Infants = 14 hours, 1-2 years = 12 hours, 3-5 years = 10 hours, 6-12 years = 9 hours, 13-18 years = 7 hours. The time duration for sleep for age group _____ is minimum, by _____ hours.
    Ans: Compare the lengths of all the bars:
    Infants = 14 hours, 1-2 years = 12 hours, 3-5 years = 10 hours, 6-12 years = 9 hours, 13-18 years = 7 hours.
    The shortest bar is the bar for 13-18 years.
    Its length shows 7 hours, which is the minimum.
    Answer: The time duration for sleep for age group 13-18 years is minimum, by 7 hours.
  • Q: 2a. A vertical bar graph shows the number of people from different areas and provinces of Pakistan who participated in games in April 2020 (Scale: one vertical square = 10 people): AJ&K = 5, Balochistan = 10, Gilgit Baltistan = 15, Islamabad = 20, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa = 10, Punjab = 40, Sindh = 30. The greatest number of people are from _____ and their number is _____.
    Ans: Compare the heights of all the bars:
    AJ&K = 5, Balochistan = 10, Gilgit Baltistan = 15, Islamabad = 20, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa = 10, Punjab = 40, Sindh = 30.
    The tallest bar is the bar for Punjab.
    Its height shows 40 people, which is the greatest number.
    Answer: The greatest number of people are from Punjab and their number is 40.
  • Q: 2b. A vertical bar graph shows the number of people from different areas and provinces of Pakistan who participated in games in April 2020 (Scale: one vertical square = 10 people): AJ&K = 5, Balochistan = 10, Gilgit Baltistan = 15, Islamabad = 20, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa = 10, Punjab = 40, Sindh = 30. The least number of people are from _____ and their number is _____.
    Ans: Compare the heights of all the bars:
    AJ&K = 5, Balochistan = 10, Gilgit Baltistan = 15, Islamabad = 20, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa = 10, Punjab = 40, Sindh = 30.
    The shortest bar is the bar for AJ&K.
    Its height shows 5 people, which is the least number.
    Answer: The least number of people are from AJ&K and their number is 5.
  • Q: 2c. A vertical bar graph shows the number of people from different areas and provinces of Pakistan who participated in games in April 2020 (Scale: one vertical square = 10 people): AJ&K = 5, Balochistan = 10, Gilgit Baltistan = 15, Islamabad = 20, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa = 10, Punjab = 40, Sindh = 30. From which area did 30 people participate?
    Ans: Read the height of each bar:
    AJ&K = 5, Balochistan = 10, Gilgit Baltistan = 15, Islamabad = 20, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa = 10, Punjab = 40, Sindh = 30.
    The bar that reaches 30 is the bar for Sindh.
    Answer: 30 people participated from Sindh.
  • Q: 2d. A vertical bar graph shows the number of people from different areas and provinces of Pakistan who participated in games in April 2020 (Scale: one vertical square = 10 people): AJ&K = 5, Balochistan = 10, Gilgit Baltistan = 15, Islamabad = 20, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa = 10, Punjab = 40, Sindh = 30. From which two areas did the same number of people participate?
    Ans: Read the height of each bar:
    AJ&K = 5, Balochistan = 10, Gilgit Baltistan = 15, Islamabad = 20, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa = 10, Punjab = 40, Sindh = 30.
    Balochistan = 10 people and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa = 10 people.
    Both bars are of the same height.
    Answer: The same number of people (10) participated from Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
  • Q: 2e. A vertical bar graph shows the number of people from different areas and provinces of Pakistan who participated in games in April 2020 (Scale: one vertical square = 10 people): AJ&K = 5, Balochistan = 10, Gilgit Baltistan = 15, Islamabad = 20, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa = 10, Punjab = 40, Sindh = 30. What is the total number of people who participated in the games?
    Ans: Read the number of people from each area:
    AJ&K = 5
    Balochistan = 10
    Gilgit Baltistan = 15
    Islamabad = 20
    Khyber Pakhtunkhwa = 10
    Punjab = 40
    Sindh = 30
    Add them step by step:
    5 + 10 = 15
    15 + 15 = 30
    30 + 20 = 50
    50 + 10 = 60
    60 + 40 = 100
    100 + 30 = 130
    Answer: The total number of people who participated in the games is 130.

Exercise 2

  • Q: 1a. A line graph shows the total number of customers coming to a superstore for shopping from 11 am to 6 pm in a week. Reading the points from the graph (approximately): Monday = 700, Tuesday = 300, Wednesday = 500, Thursday = 400, Friday = 600, Saturday = 850, Sunday = 1,000. On what day did the maximum number of customers come? How many?
    Ans: Read the point for each day:
    Monday = 700, Tuesday = 300, Wednesday = 500, Thursday = 400, Friday = 600, Saturday = 850, Sunday = 1,000.
    The highest point of the line graph is on Sunday.
    It shows 1,000 customers.
    Answer: The maximum number of customers came on Sunday, and they were 1,000.
  • Q: 1b. A line graph shows the total number of customers coming to a superstore for shopping from 11 am to 6 pm in a week. Reading the points from the graph (approximately): Monday = 700, Tuesday = 300, Wednesday = 500, Thursday = 400, Friday = 600, Saturday = 850, Sunday = 1,000. Find the total number of customers coming on Monday and Thursday. Is the number of customers more or less than the number of customers coming on Sunday?
    Ans: Customers on Monday = 700.
    Customers on Thursday = 400.
    Total = 700 + 400 = 1,100.
    Customers on Sunday = 1,000.
    Compare: 1,100 - 1,000 = 100.
    So 1,100 is more than 1,000 by 100.
    Answer: The total number of customers on Monday and Thursday is 1,100, which is 100 more than the number of customers on Sunday.
  • Q: 1c. A line graph shows the total number of customers coming to a superstore for shopping from 11 am to 6 pm in a week. Reading the points from the graph (approximately): Monday = 700, Tuesday = 300, Wednesday = 500, Thursday = 400, Friday = 600, Saturday = 850, Sunday = 1,000. On what day did the minimum number of customers come? How many?
    Ans: Read the point for each day:
    Monday = 700, Tuesday = 300, Wednesday = 500, Thursday = 400, Friday = 600, Saturday = 850, Sunday = 1,000.
    The lowest point of the line graph is on Tuesday.
    It shows 300 customers.
    Answer: The minimum number of customers came on Tuesday, and they were 300.
  • Q: 1d. A line graph shows the total number of customers coming to a superstore for shopping from 11 am to 6 pm in a week. Reading the points from the graph (approximately): Monday = 700, Tuesday = 300, Wednesday = 500, Thursday = 400, Friday = 600, Saturday = 850, Sunday = 1,000. How many customers came on Friday?
    Ans: Find the point above Friday on the line graph.
    The point for Friday is at 600 on the vertical axis.
    Answer: 600 customers came on Friday.
  • Q: 2a. A line graph shows the maximum temperature (in degree Celsius) of Peshawar during a week of August: Monday = 38°C, Tuesday = 36°C, Wednesday = 30°C, Thursday = 35°C, Friday = 35°C, Saturday = 33°C, Sunday = 31°C. On what day was the temperature the highest?

mcqs.why: Find the bar for 6-12 years in the graph. The bar for 6-12 years ends at 9 hours. Answer: 9 hours.

mcqs.why: Sleep duration for 3 to 5 years = 10 hours. Sleep duration for 13 to 18 years = 7 hours. Difference = 10 - 7 = 3 hours. Answer: The sleep duration for children of age 13 to 18 years is 3 hours less than the sleep duration for children of age 3 to 5 years.

  • Q: 2a. A pie chart titled 'Cattle of Village' shows: goats = 100, buffaloes = 98, bulls = 74, sheep = 58, donkeys = 35. Which type of cattle is bred the most?

  • Q: 2c. A pie chart titled 'Cattle of Village' shows: goats = 100, buffaloes = 98, bulls = 74, sheep = 58, donkeys = 35. What is the total number of sheep and goats? What is the total number of donkeys and buffaloes? Which one is more?
    Ans: Number of sheep = 58.
    Number of goats = 100.
    Total of sheep and goats = 58 + 100 = 158.
    Number of donkeys = 35.
    Number of buffaloes = 98.
    Total of donkeys and buffaloes = 35 + 98 = 133.
    Compare the two totals: 158 - 133 = 25.
    So 158 is more than 133 by 25.
    Answer: The total number of sheep and goats is 158, the total number of donkeys and buffaloes is 133, and the total of sheep and goats is more by 25.
  • Q: 2d. A pie chart titled 'Cattle of Village' shows: goats = 100, buffaloes = 98, bulls = 74, sheep = 58, donkeys = 35. What fraction is the number of bulls to the total number of cattle?

    330 + 35 = 365
    Number of bulls = 74.
    Fraction = number of bulls / total number of cattle = 74/365.
    Answer: The number of bulls is 74/365 of the total number of cattle.

mcqs.q: It is important that in a bar graph, the _____ of each bar is same.
mcqs.why: In a bar graph the bars are compared by their length or height, so every bar must have the same width. That is why the width of each bar is the same in a bar graph.

lessons.notes_html:
Review Exercise

  • Q: 1a. It is important that in a bar graph, the _____ of each bar is same.
    Options: (a) length   (b) colour   (c) width   (d) value

    Options: (a) two   (b) three   (c) four   (d) five

    Options: (a) pie chart   (b) line graph   (c) vertical bar graph   (d) horizontal bar graph

    Options: (a) pie chart   (b) line graph   (c) vertical bar graph   (d) horizontal bar graph
    Ans: line graph
  • Q: 2a. A vertical bar graph shows Marwa's weight from birth to 7 years (Weight in kilograms): First year = 8 kg, Second year = 12 kg, Third year = 14 kg, Fourth year = 14 kg, Fifth year = 17 kg, Sixth year = 22 kg, Seventh year = 30 kg. What was Marwa's weight at the age of one year?
    Ans: Find the bar for the First year in the graph.
    The bar for the First year reaches 8 kg.
    Answer: Marwa's weight at the age of one year was 8 kg.
  • Q: 2b. A vertical bar graph shows Marwa's weight from birth to 7 years (Weight in kilograms): First year = 8 kg, Second year = 12 kg, Third year = 14 kg, Fourth year = 14 kg, Fifth year = 17 kg, Sixth year = 22 kg, Seventh year = 30 kg. In which years was Marwa's weight the same and by how much?
    Ans: Read the height of each bar:
    First year = 8 kg, Second year = 12 kg, Third year = 14 kg, Fourth year = 14 kg, Fifth year = 17 kg, Sixth year = 22 kg, Seventh year = 30 kg.
    The bars for the Third year and the Fourth year are of the same height.
    Both show 14 kg.
    Answer: Marwa's weight was the same in the third and fourth year, and it was 14 kg.
  • Q: 2c. A vertical bar graph shows Marwa's weight from birth to 7 years (Weight in kilograms): First year = 8 kg, Second year = 12 kg, Third year = 14 kg, Fourth year = 14 kg, Fifth year = 17 kg, Sixth year = 22 kg, Seventh year = 30 kg. What was the time duration in which Marwa's weight increased the most, and by how much?
    Ans: Read Marwa's weight in each year:
    First year = 8 kg, Second year = 12 kg, Third year = 14 kg, Fourth year = 14 kg, Fifth year = 17 kg, Sixth year = 22 kg, Seventh year = 30 kg.
    Find the increase in each duration:
    First to second year: 12 - 8 = 4 kg
    Second to third year: 14 - 12 = 2 kg
    Third to fourth year: 14 - 14 = 0 kg
    Fourth to fifth year: 17 - 14 = 3 kg
    Fifth to sixth year: 22 - 17 = 5 kg
    Sixth to seventh year: 30 - 22 = 8 kg
    The biggest increase is 8 kg.
    It is between the sixth and seventh year.
    Answer: Marwa's weight increased the most between the sixth and seventh year, by 8 kg.
  • Q: 2d. A vertical bar graph shows Marwa's weight from birth to 7 years (Weight in kilograms): First year = 8 kg, Second year = 12 kg, Third year = 14 kg, Fourth year = 14 kg, Fifth year = 17 kg, Sixth year = 22 kg, Seventh year = 30 kg. What was the time duration in which Marwa's weight increased the least, and by how much?
    Ans: Read Marwa's weight in each year:
    First year = 8 kg, Second year = 12 kg, Third year = 14 kg, Fourth year = 14 kg, Fifth year = 17 kg, Sixth year = 22 kg, Seventh year = 30 kg.
    Find the increase in each duration:
    First to second year: 12 - 8 = 4 kg
    Second to third year: 14 - 12 = 2 kg
    Third to fourth year: 14 - 14 = 0 kg (weight stayed the same)
    Fourth to fifth year: 17 - 14 = 3 kg
    Fifth to sixth year: 22 - 17 = 5 kg
    Sixth to seventh year: 30 - 22 = 8 kg
    Leaving aside the third to fourth year, in which the weight did not increase at all, the smallest increase is 2 kg.
    It is between the second and third year.
    Answer: Marwa's weight increased the least between the second and third year, by 2 kg.
    Note: The printed answer key gives 4 kg, which is incorrect.
  • Q: 2e. A vertical bar graph shows Marwa's weight from birth to 7 years (Weight in kilograms): First year = 8 kg, Second year = 12 kg, Third year = 14 kg, Fourth year = 14 kg, Fifth year = 17 kg, Sixth year = 22 kg, Seventh year = 30 kg. How much did Marwa's weight increase in total from the age of one year to 7 years?
    Ans: Marwa's weight at the age of one year = 8 kg.
    Marwa's weight at the age of 7 years = 30 kg.
    Total increase = 30 - 8 = 22 kg.
    Answer: Marwa's weight increased by 22 kg in total from the age of one year to 7 years.
  • Q: 3a. A horizontal bar graph titled 'Ahad's garden' shows the number of flowers: Rose = 10, Chrysanthemum = 8, Tulip = 11, Daffodil = 10, Gul e qasidi = 12, Spring flower = 20. How many roses are there in Ahad's garden?
    Ans: Find the bar for Rose in the graph.
    The bar for Rose ends at 10.
    Answer: There are 10 roses in Ahad's garden.
  • Q: 3b. A horizontal bar graph titled 'Ahad's garden' shows the number of flowers: Rose = 10, Chrysanthemum = 8, Tulip = 11, Daffodil = 10, Gul e qasidi = 12, Spring flower = 20. How much less are the Tulips than the Gul e qasidi?
    Ans: Number of Gul e qasidi = 12.
    Number of Tulips = 11.
    Difference = 12 - 11 = 1.
    Answer: The Tulips are 1 less than the Gul e qasidi.
  • Q: 3c. A horizontal bar graph titled 'Ahad's garden' shows the number of flowers: Rose = 10, Chrysanthemum = 8, Tulip = 11, Daffodil = 10, Gul e qasidi = 12, Spring flower = 20. Which flowers are present in the most number in Ahad's garden? How many are they?
    Ans: Compare the lengths of all the bars:
    Rose = 10, Chrysanthemum = 8, Tulip = 11, Daffodil = 10, Gul e qasidi = 12, Spring flower = 20.
    The longest bar is the bar for Spring flower.
    Its length shows 20.
    Answer: Spring flowers are present in the most number in Ahad's garden, and they are 20.
  • Q: 3d. A horizontal bar graph titled 'Ahad's garden' shows the number of flowers: Rose = 10, Chrysanthemum = 8, Tulip = 11, Daffodil = 10, Gul e qasidi = 12, Spring flower = 20. Write a fraction for the number of Tulips.
    Ans: First find the total number of flowers:
    Rose = 10, Chrysanthemum = 8, Tulip = 11, Daffodil = 10, Gul e qasidi = 12, Spring flower = 20.
    Total = 10 + 8 = 18
    18 + 11 = 29
    29 + 10 = 39
    39 + 12 = 51
    51 + 20 = 71
    Number of Tulips = 11.
    Fraction = number of Tulips / total number of flowers = 11/71.
    Answer: The fraction for the number of Tulips is 11/71.
  • Q: 3e. A horizontal bar graph titled 'Ahad's garden' shows the number of flowers: Rose = 10, Chrysanthemum = 8, Tulip = 11, Daffodil = 10, Gul e qasidi = 12, Spring flower = 20. Which flowers are present in the least number in Ahad's garden? How many are they?
    Ans: Compare the lengths of all the bars:
    Rose = 10, Chrysanthemum = 8, Tulip = 11, Daffodil = 10, Gul e qasidi = 12, Spring flower = 20.

    Answer: Chrysanthemums are present in the least number in Ahad's garden, and they are 8.
  • Q: 4a. A line graph shows the cupcakes sold by Ibrahim in each hour from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m.: 1st hour = 7, 2nd hour = 15, 3rd hour = 20, 4th hour = 35, 5th hour = 15. How many cupcakes were sold in the third hour?

    1st hour = 7, 2nd hour = 15, 3rd hour = 20, 4th hour = 35, 5th hour = 15.
    The highest point of the line graph is in the fourth hour.

  • Q: 4c. A line graph shows the cupcakes sold by Ibrahim in each hour from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m.: 1st hour = 7, 2nd hour = 15, 3rd hour = 20, 4th hour = 35, 5th hour = 15. In which two hours were the same number of cupcakes sold? What was their number?
    Ans: Read the point for each hour:
    1st hour = 7, 2nd hour = 15, 3rd hour = 20, 4th hour = 35, 5th hour = 15.

  • Q: 4d. A line graph shows the cupcakes sold by Ibrahim in each hour from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m.: 1st hour = 7, 2nd hour = 15, 3rd hour = 20, 4th hour = 35, 5th hour = 15. If Ibrahim sold 92 cakes in total, how many cakes were sold in the first hour?
    Ans: Read the cupcakes sold in the other hours from the graph:
    2nd hour = 15, 3rd hour = 20, 4th hour = 35, 5th hour = 15.
    Add them: 15 + 20 = 35
    35 + 35 = 70
    70 + 15 = 85
    Total cakes sold = 92.
    Cakes sold in the first hour = 92 - 85 = 7.
    Answer: 7 cakes were sold in the first hour.
    Note: The printed answer key gives 8 cupcakes, which is incorrect.
  • Q: 5a. A pie chart titled 'Flavours of Ice Cream' shows the favourite flavours of Arham's 20 family members: Qulfa = 7, Chocolate = 4, Mango = 3, Strawberry = 3, Vanilla = 2, Pistachio = 1. How many people like vanilla ice cream?

  • Q: 5c. A pie chart titled 'Flavours of Ice Cream' shows the favourite flavours of Arham's 20 family members: Qulfa = 7, Chocolate = 4, Mango = 3, Strawberry = 3, Vanilla = 2, Pistachio = 1. Which flavour is liked by the same number of people? How many people like this flavour?
    Ans: Compare all the sectors of the pie chart:
    Qulfa = 7, Chocolate = 4, Mango = 3, Strawberry = 3, Vanilla = 2, Pistachio = 1.
    Mango = 3 people and Strawberry = 3 people.
    Both flavours have the same number.
    Answer: Mango and Strawberry are liked by the same number of people, and 3 people like each flavour.
    Note: The printed answer key gives mango and chocolate, 4, which is incorrect.
  • Q: 5d. A pie chart titled 'Flavours of Ice Cream' shows the favourite flavours of Arham's 20 family members: Qulfa = 7, Chocolate = 4, Mango = 3, Strawberry = 3, Vanilla = 2, Pistachio = 1. How much less are the number of people preferring pistachio ice cream than the number of people preferring qulfa ice cream?
    Ans: Number of people preferring qulfa = 7.
    Number of people preferring pistachio = 1.
    Difference = 7 - 1 = 6.
    Answer: The number of people preferring pistachio ice cream is 6 less than the number of people preferring qulfa ice cream.
  • Q: 5e. A pie chart titled 'Flavours of Ice Cream' shows the favourite flavours of Arham's 20 family members: Qulfa = 7, Chocolate = 4, Mango = 3, Strawberry = 3, Vanilla = 2, Pistachio = 1. There are 20 family members in total. The people preferring chocolate ice cream are 4. How will you show this number as a fraction?
    Ans: Number of people preferring chocolate = 4.
    Total number of family members = 20.
    Fraction = 4/20.
    Divide the numerator and denominator by 4: 4/20 = 1/5.
    Answer: The number is shown as the fraction 1/5.

mcqs.q: It is important that in a bar graph, the _____ of each bar is same.
mcqs.why: In a bar graph the bars are compared by their length or height, so every bar must have the same width. That is why the width of each bar is the same in a bar graph.

mcqs.q: A bar graph can be of _____ types.
mcqs.why: A bar graph can be drawn in two ways: with vertical bars and with horizontal bars. So a bar graph can be of two types, vertical and horizontal.

mcqs.q: _____ is also called a circle graph.
mcqs.why: A pie chart shows data in a circle divided into sectors, so a pie chart is also called a circle graph. A line graph and bar graphs are different kinds of graphs.

mcqs.q: A _____ is drawn by joining the dots representing the quantity of a given value in the question.
mcqs.why: In a line graph, dots are plotted for each value and then the dots are joined to make a line. So a line graph is drawn by joining the dots representing the quantity.

mcqs.q: A vertical bar graph shows Marwa's weight: First year = 8 kg, Second year = 12 kg, Third year = 14 kg, Fourth year = 14 kg, Fifth year = 17 kg, Sixth year = 22 kg, Seventh year = 30 kg. What was Marwa's weight at the age of one year?
mcqs.why: Find the bar for the First year in the graph. The bar for the First year reaches 8 kg. Answer: Marwa's weight at the age of one year was 8 kg.

mcqs.q: A vertical bar graph shows Marwa's weight: First year = 8 kg, Second year = 12 kg, Third year = 14 kg, Fourth year = 14 kg, Fifth year = 17 kg, Sixth year = 22 kg, Seventh year = 30 kg. In which years was Marwa's weight the same and by how much?
mcqs.why: Read the height of each bar: First year = 8 kg, Second year = 12 kg, Third year = 14 kg, Fourth year = 14 kg, Fifth year = 17 kg, Sixth year = 22 kg, Seventh year = 30 kg. The bars for the Third year and the Fourth year are of the same height. Both show 14 kg. Answer: Marwa's weight was the same in the third and fourth year, and it was 14 kg.

mcqs.q: A vertical bar graph shows Marwa's weight: First year = 8 kg, Second year = 12 kg, Third year = 14 kg, Fourth year = 14 kg, Fifth year = 17 kg, Sixth year = 22 kg, Seventh year = 30 kg. What was the time duration in which Marwa's weight increased the least (leaving aside the duration with no increase), and by how much?
mcqs.why: Read Marwa's weight in each year: First year = 8 kg, Second year = 12 kg, Third year = 14 kg, Fourth year = 14 kg, Fifth year = 17 kg, Sixth year = 22 kg, Seventh year = 30 kg. Find the increase in each duration: First to second year: 12 - 8 = 4 kg, Second to third year: 14 - 12 = 2 kg, Third to fourth year: 14 - 14 = 0 kg (weight stayed the same), Fourth to fifth year: 17 - 14 = 3 kg, Fifth to sixth year: 22 - 17 = 5 kg, Sixth to seventh year: 30 - 22 = 8 kg. Leaving aside the third to fourth year, in which the weight did not increase at all, the smallest increase is 2 kg. It is between the second and third year. Answer: Marwa's weight increased the least between the second and third year, by 2 kg. Note: The printed answer key gives 4 kg, which is incorrect; the correct working above gives 2 kg.

mcqs.q: A vertical bar graph shows Marwa's weight: First year = 8 kg, Second year = 12 kg, Third year = 14 kg, Fourth year = 14 kg, Fifth year = 17 kg, Sixth year = 22 kg, Seventh year = 30 kg. How much did Marwa's weight increase in total from the age of one year to 7 years?
mcqs.why: Marwa's weight at the age of one year = 8 kg. Marwa's weight at the age of 7 years = 30 kg. Total increase = 30 - 8 = 22 kg. Answer: Marwa's weight increased by 22 kg in total from the age of one year to 7 years.

mcqs.q: A horizontal bar graph titled 'Ahad's garden' shows the number of flowers: Rose = 10, Chrysanthemum = 8, Tulip = 11, Daffodil = 10, Gul e qasidi = 12, Spring flower = 20. Which flowers are present in the most number in Ahad's garden? How many are they?
mcqs.why: Compare the lengths of all the bars: Rose = 10, Chrysanthemum = 8, Tulip = 11, Daffodil = 10, Gul e qasidi = 12, Spring flower = 20. The longest bar is the bar for Spring flower. Its length shows 20. Answer: Spring flowers are present in the most number in Ahad's garden, and they are 20.

mcqs.q: A pie chart titled 'Flavours of Ice Cream' shows the favourite flavours of Arham's 20 family members: Qulfa = 7, Chocolate = 4, Mango = 3, Strawberry = 3, Vanilla = 2, Pistachio = 1. Which flavor is liked the most?
mcqs.why: Compare all the sectors of the pie chart: Qulfa = 7, Chocolate = 4, Mango = 3, Strawberry = 3, Vanilla = 2, Pistachio = 1. The biggest value is 7. It belongs to Qulfa. Answer: Qulfa is liked the most.

Try Yourself (book p. 164)

  • Q: 1. A pie chart titled 'Types of Vertebrates' shows: Fish = 32,900, Reptiles = 10,711, Birds = 10,425, Animals living in water and on land both = 7,302, Mammals = 5,513. By looking at the chart, write these types of vertebrates in ascending order.
    Ans: Read the number of each type from the pie chart:
    Mammals = 5,513
    Animals living in water and on land both = 7,302
    Birds = 10,425
    Reptiles = 10,711
    Fish = 32,900
    Now arrange the numbers from smallest to largest:
    5,513 < 7,302 < 10,425 < 10,711 < 32,900
    Answer: Mammals, Animals living in water and on land both, Birds, Reptiles, Fish.

Try Yourself (book p. 166)

  • Q: 1. A horizontal bar graph shows the number of students absent from school (Scale: a small square in the horizontal direction shows 2 students): Class 1 = 14, Class 2 = 10, Class 3 = 12, Class 4 = 4, Class 5 = 2, Class 6 = 1, Class 7 = 2, Class 8 = 1. In which classes is the difference between the number of absent students the least in the above graph?
    Ans: Read the number of absent students in each class:
    Class 1 = 14, Class 2 = 10, Class 3 = 12, Class 4 = 4
    Class 5 = 2, Class 6 = 1, Class 7 = 2, Class 8 = 1
    The least possible difference is 0, which happens when two classes have the same number of absent students.
    Class 5 and Class 7 both have 2 absent students, so 2 - 2 = 0.
    Class 6 and Class 8 both have 1 absent student, so 1 - 1 = 0.
    Answer: The difference is the least (zero) between Class 5 and Class 7, and between Class 6 and Class 8.

Try Yourself (book p. 170)

  • Q: 1. Try It! Challenge: A table shows the distance from Islamabad in kilometres: Jhelum = 125, Sialkot = 275, Mansehra = 150, Peshawar = 175, Kalar Kahar = 150. In the line graph drawn beside the table, the points are plotted at about: Jhelum = 125, Sialkot = 230, Mansehra = 150, Peshawar = 185, Kalar Kahar = 150. Observe the given line graph and find the mistake in it.
    Ans: Compare each point of the line graph with the table:
    Jhelum: table = 125 km, graph = 125 km. Correct.
    Sialkot: table = 275 km, graph = about 230 km. Wrong.
    Mansehra: table = 150 km, graph = 150 km. Correct.
    Peshawar: table = 175 km, graph = about 185 km. Wrong.
    Kalar Kahar: table = 150 km, graph = 150 km. Correct.
    The clear mistake is the point for Sialkot, which is plotted much lower than its true distance of 275 km.
    Answer: The distance of Sialkot from Islamabad is plotted wrongly in the line graph; it should be 275 km, not about 230 km.
